Key is NOT read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY. It comes from the plugin userConfig jev_api_key (sensitive) via env CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_JEV_API_KEY (src/hosts/claude.ts:130-133), so a separate key entry is needed.

interface.name: hook PreToolUse observe (async)
interface.purpose: hooks.json matcher ^(Bash|PowerShell|Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|WebFetch|mcp__.*)$. Rules, then Jev, then log the verdict and the would-be effect. Observer IO type has no stdout, so it cannot inject context (cli.ts:39-45).

interface.name: hook PreToolUse gate (sync, timeout 5s)
interface.purpose: Spawns node on every matched call. Exits before reading stdin unless mode=enforce (cli.ts:129-131). In enforce, outside auto mode, calls Jev within a budget of at most 3.5 s and prints permissionDecision ask/deny JSON. Never exit 2.

interface.name: hook PermissionDenied observe (async)
interface.purpose: Logs the classifier's denial label, parsed from the reason text like "[Label]".

interface.name: hook PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure observe (async)
interface.purpose: Logs that the tool ran and whether it succeeded.

interface.name: CLI jev-shadow mode <off|shadow|enforce>
interface.purpose: Writes ~/.config/jev-shadow/config.json (atomic rename). Off is the kill switch and applies to running sessions on the next call.

interface.name: CLI jev-shadow report [--log path]
interface.purpose: Prints per-hazard Jev vs classifier agreement, over-refusals, band accuracy, latency, tokens and errors.

interface.name: slash command /jev-shadow:report
interface.purpose: commands/report.md runs `!jev-shadow report`, allowed-tools Bash(jev-shadow report:*). It needs the plugin's bin on PATH, which is a risk given the user's PATH override in settings env.

interface.name: MCP servers / skills
interface.purpose: None. No .mcp.json, no SKILL.md, no MCP tool definitions.

security: Key handling: userConfig sensitive:true (plugin.json). The key reaches the hook process as env CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_JEV_API_KEY, never argv. It is wrapped in an opaque Secret class whose toJSON/toString/inspect print [secret] (jev.ts:129-150) and it is never logged. Not covered by the user's no-secret-leak protected-vars list, and unknown whether the Bash tool env inherits CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_* (unverified).

Config is user-owned (~/.config/jev-shadow/config.json or $JEV_SHADOW_CONFIG). It is never read from the repo, endpoint URLs are constants, and env JEV_SHADOW_MODE can only lower the mode. Invalid or absent config means off. A cloned project cannot redirect egress (config.ts:1-10,71-77).

No shell exec, no child_process, no installer, no postinstall, no telemetry. The only network call is fetch to the backend URL (grep of src/). Zero runtime dependencies (package.json has devDependencies only).

Redaction is a 16-pattern regex table (PEM, URL userinfo, auth headers, sk-/stripe/AKIA/ghp_/glpat/npm_/hf_/slack/JWT, mysql -p, --password flags, KEY=value assignments) applied before clipping, with the order enforced by branded types plus tsc @ts-expect-error tests. Reference values like $TOKEN are kept. It is heuristic: arbitrary secrets, client names, code and business data pass through unredacted.

Prompt-injection surface: the Jev state contains attacker-controllable command, file content and local script text (up to 3 scripts x 4000 chars read from the project). Per the brief, injected instructions can move Jev answers. In shadow mode the effect is only bad data in the log. In enforce mode it could induce a false allow, but allow just falls through to the normal permission flow, so Jev cannot grant permission (render prints nothing for allow).

Enforce-mode fail-open: policy.onError defaults to allow, and a hook timeout always fails open. Rule-table edge: writes whose path startsWith('/tmp/') are treated as routine (rules.ts:310), and I did not verify handling of '/tmp/../' traversal after SENSITIVE_PATHS. Local log stores 200-char redacted excerpts under ~/.claude/plugins/data/jev-shadow-*/log.jsonl.

Supply chain: brand-new repo by one contributor (34 commits, single day), 0 stars, no release tags. The plugin install copies committed dist/*.js, which CI checks matches the sources (git diff --exit-code dist/src), but no signing. It is readable and small (about 2.4k lines of TS).
gh-dreyfus92-jev-shadow.dataEgress: Nothing until the config file exists (default mode is off). Then, for each non-routine matched tool call, one HTTPS POST to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone containing: tool name, cwd (redacted, clipped 2000), and for Bash/PowerShell the command (redacted, up to 8000 chars) plus up to 3 referenced in-project script bodies (up to 4000 chars each, files at most 512 KB). For Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit outside the project or on sensitive paths it sends the file path plus a 3000-char content excerpt. For WebFetch it sends the URL and the prompt (1000 chars). For every mcp__* call, including gitnexus and playwright, it sends the server name and JSON-stringified input (up to 4000 chars), because mcp/fetch/other are always_judged (rules.ts:312-315). Read/Grep/Glob are not matched. Also sent: the fixed question pack and the API key in the Authorization header. Routine calls (read-only commands, project tests, in-project or /tmp edits) never leave the machine. Requests go to OpenRouter and on to TypeSafe, a third party, which matters for client projects. In shadow mode it also fires on bypassPermissions sessions, and nothing is compared in those.
gh-dreyfus92-jev-shadow.failureMode: Fail-safe by construction. All hooks exit 0 (ExitCode type makes 2 unrepresentable, cli.ts:47-51). ask() never throws, makes one attempt, and is bounded by a deadline measured from process start (observe 8 s default, capped at 10 s. gate 3 s default, capped at 3.5 s under the hook's 5 s timeout, which a test pins). Errors map to no_key, deadline, firewall (403), http, network or malformed. Shadow: the errors are only logged. Enforce: policy.onError defaults to allow, and a host timeout fails open. Missing, invalid or off config means no egress. Async observers pile up in the background with no host timeout beyond the 10 s cap. The Vercel path has been probed but the OpenRouter path is untested by the repo (no live test).
gh-dreyfus92-jev-shadow.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no skills, so no tool-definition tokens and no skillListingBudget usage. The only added text is the /jev-shadow:report command description. Shadow mode injects no additionalContext (observer has no stdout). Enforce mode adds only short deny/ask reason strings (about 30 tokens) when it fires. Effectively 0 tokens/turn in shadow mode.
gh-dreyfus92-jev-shadow.autoInvocation: Fully automatic and deterministic through hooks, with no prompting of Claude needed. Shadow by default and observation only, so it never influences the model. Off until the user runs `jev-shadow mode shadow`. Installs disabled and must be enabled per repo (`claude plugin enable ... --scope local`).
pros: OpenRouter is a first-class backend in code (src/jev.ts:197, config.ts:101), model pinned to typesafe/jev-1.13, no patching needed, and the key is a sensitive plugin option rather than argv or a repo file.

Shadow-first design is verifiably non-invasive. The observer's IO type has no stdout, all exits are 0, config is user-owned and can only be lowered by env, and the kill switch works mid-session (cli.ts:39-51, config.ts:1-10).

Directly produces the evidence needed before trusting Jev: per-hazard agreement with the real auto-mode classifier on the user's own sessions (joins PermissionDenied labels by tool_use_id), with latency and token stats.

Egress hygiene is better than typical: local rule table keeps routine calls off the network, 16-pattern redaction runs before clipping, order enforced by types, plus a leak corpus test and a no-scannable-secrets test.
Zero runtime dependencies, no shell exec, no telemetry, small readable codebase (about 2.4k LOC), CI on Node 20/22/24 with a committed-dist-matches-source check, MIT.

Enforce mode is the one variant that works in bypassPermissions/default/dontAsk sessions, where no classifier exists. It adds a fail-open ask/deny second opinion, consistent with the OpenRouter cookbook's fail-to-prompt posture.
No context cost: no MCP tools or skills, and shadow mode injects nothing.
cons: Measurement tool, not a Jev integration that adds value to the coding loop. The README itself says that for auto-mode users there is nothing to gate yet, only something to measure, and that it is not a replacement for the classifier. It only compares against the classifier when permission_mode is auto, while the user also runs many bypassPermissions sessions, where shadow collects verdicts with no reference label.

Broad egress: every non-routine Bash, every mcp__* call (gitnexus, playwright) and every WebFetch goes to OpenRouter/TypeSafe, including up to 3 project script bodies. Regex redaction cannot catch client-confidential code or names, a real concern for client projects.

Enforce mode has weak fit for this user: it stands down in auto, so it only adds latency (up to 3.5 s sync) and ask prompts in bypass sessions, and Jev is overconfident and injectable. Fail-open on timeout and onError=allow.

Very immature: created 2026-09-23, one author, 34 commits, 0 stars, no releases, v0.1, docs directory of rejected design candidates. The repo has 0 OpenRouter-specific tests (only mock-backend tests, roughly 64 test cases, no live check), and /api/v1/systemone is the alpha, no-SLA surface.

Setup friction: installs disabled and needs a per-repo enable, a separate jev_api_key entry (not OPENROUTER_API_KEY) and a manual `jev-shadow mode shadow` config. The /report command depends on `jev-shadow` being on PATH, which is fragile with the user's PATH override in settings env.
A sync node hook spawns on every matched call even in shadow mode (about 50 ms each on top of the gitnexus hooks), and mcp__.* is in the matcher so playwright/gitnexus calls all pay the spawn cost.
gh-dreyfus92-jev-shadow.verdict: Well-engineered, safe-by-default shadow harness with native OpenRouter support that could generate the calibration evidence to justify trusting Jev. It does not itself make Claude Code use Jev where it adds value, and it sends broad tool-call text (all MCP calls included) to a third party on a brand-new 0-star v0.1 repo. Worth a time-boxed shadow trial on personal projects only, not a daily-driver integration.

gh-nasrallah-al-jev-cli.name: jevctl (Nasrallah-AL/jev-cli)
gh-nasrallah-al-jev-cli.whatItDoes: MIT TypeScript npm CLI (`jevctl`, binary `jev`) wrapping TypeSafe Jev with commands verify, screen (prompt-injection and substance check), find, classify, extract, rerank, match, route, ask, compact, batch, plus auth/config/models/update. A Claude Code marketplace plugin (plugin/, name `jev`) adds one skill (SKILL.md, allowed-tools Bash(jev:*)), 8 slash commands (/jev:verify, screen, route, find, extract, compact, classify, ask) and an early-access function-hook module (fast-jev.ts) that replaces Claude Code's compaction summary with Jev-guided verbatim truncation. There is no MCP server. The plugin does not talk to any API itself; the skill and commands make Claude run the `jev` CLI through Bash.

providerSupport.evidence: The CLI supports OpenRouter natively. src/provider.ts:60 auto-detects OPENROUTER_API_KEY only if it matches /^sk-or-/. Lines 72-79 handle -P openrouter. Lines 105-108 map the model to typesafe/jev-1.13 ('jev-latest' becomes OPENROUTER_LATEST 'jev-1.13' at line 55). Lines 223-232 POST to the hardcoded URL https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY and body {model, state, questions}. JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter is read at src/config.ts:117. Cloudflare Workers AI is also supported. TypeSafe direct uses @typesafe-ai/sdk (provider.ts:191-196, with TYPESAFE_BASE_URL). The compaction hook does NOT support OpenRouter. plugin/hooks/fast-jev.ts:189 throws 'TYPESAFE_API_KEY is not configured' if there is no key. getApiKey (lines 245-252) reads only TYPESAFE_API_KEY, from the plugin option, the env or settings.env. The hook's URL is hardcoded to https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (src/vendor/compaction/request.ts:6 and the plugin/hooks/compaction copy). buildJevRequest accepts a baseUrl param, but nothing passes it and there is no userConfig or env knob for it. The hook's default model is 'jev-latest' (DEFAULT_MODEL), which OpenRouter does not accept because it has no latest alias. plugin.json documents the key as TypeSafe only. The OpenRouter hop is announced on stderr (provider.ts:173-181) when the provider is auto.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: CLI and skill: works today with OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-... and JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter (or -P openrouter), no patching. Hook: needs a local fork or edit of plugin/hooks/compaction/request.ts to set the URL to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone (or /api/alpha/decisions), the model to jev-1.13, and to read OPENROUTER_API_KEY in fast-jev.ts getApiKey. That is about 10 lines, but the change is overwritten on plugin update, and the vendored copy is guarded by a sync check in CI.
providerSupport.others: Cloudflare Workers AI (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN + CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, or JEV_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN).

interface.name: jev verify
interface.purpose: Check claims against evidence. Verdicts: verified, contradicted, unsupported or unknown. Exits 2 on contradicted by default (--fail-on).

interface.name: jev screen
interface.purpose: Prompt-injection, substance and relevance probabilities. Action is pass, review, block or skip. Exits 2 on block.

interface.name: jev find
interface.purpose: Pick the best-matching file, line or candidate for a query (max 250 candidates, 2000 chars each), with an exists verdict.

interface.name: jev classify
interface.purpose: Single-label, multi-label or taxonomy classification, with --other.

interface.name: jev extract
interface.purpose: Choose among regex-found spans for fields (email, date, amount and so on), so values cannot be hallucinated.

interface.name: jev rerank
interface.purpose: Independent relevance per candidate with a --min threshold.

interface.name: jev match
interface.purpose: Dedupe records or match left against right (same, unclear or different).

interface.name: jev route
interface.purpose: Map text to a handler plus typed args.

interface.name: jev ask
interface.purpose: Custom --noul, --choice and --score questions over text or JSON state.

interface.name: jev compact
interface.purpose: Offline Jev-guided transcript compaction of a session JSONL.

interface.name: jev batch
interface.purpose: Run classify, screen, verify or route over many rows (JSONL in, JSONL out).

interface.name: jev auth/config/models/update/version
interface.purpose: Key storage (keychain or a 0600 file), diagnostics, model listing (TypeSafe only), and a self-update that runs `npm install -g jevctl@latest`.

interface.name: skill jev (plugin/skills/jev/SKILL.md)
interface.purpose: Model-invoked by description match (13.2 KB body). Tells Claude to run a preflight (`jev config --json`) and then use jev for fact-checks, injection screening of untrusted fetches, find, classify and so on. allowed-tools: Bash(jev:*), Bash(npx jevctl:*), Bash(which:*), Read, Glob, Grep.

interface.name: slash commands /jev:verify|screen|route|find|extract|compact|classify|ask
interface.purpose: User-invoked wrappers, roughly 0.9-1.3 KB each, that instruct Claude to run the matching jev command and act on its result.

interface.name: hook session.compact (fast-jev.ts)
interface.purpose: Function hook. Asks Jev per old tool call whether the call and its result are still needed, truncates or drops stale ones, and falls back to the built-in summary on any error or if the reduction is below 25%.

interface.name: hook turn.complete (fast-jev.ts)
interface.purpose: Function hook. Calls $.session.compact() when context usage is at or above compactAtPercent (default 60). Set 0 to disable.

security: Key handling: keys come from env (TYPESAFE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY), OS keychain or a 0600 credentials file (src/credentials.ts:49-58). `jev auth login` reads the key from a masked prompt or --key-stdin. There is no --api-key flag, so the key is not exposed in argv. Config and status print keys masked. The keychain backends shell out via execFileSync (credentials.ts run()); the plan's Linux Secret Service path was not fully audited.

Shell exec: only execFileSync with argument arrays (credentials.ts, commands/update.ts). No shell string interpolation was seen in src. `jev update` runs `npm install -g jevctl@latest`. src/versionCheck.ts and cli.ts:168-180 run `npm view jevctl version` via execFileSync on ordinary commands, at most once a day, cached in the config dir. That is a hidden network call and subprocess. It is suppressed by JEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 or -q.

Telemetry: none found in src (grep for telemetry and analytics came back empty). The only extra egress is the daily npm update check. HTTP-Referer https://github.com/Nasrallah-AL/jev-cli and X-Title jevctl are sent to OpenRouter (provider.ts:233-234), which is harmless attribution.

Prompt-injection surface: the skill (SKILL.md) tells Claude to run `curl -s $url | jev screen` and act on the JSON. The screen model is the Jev model, which independent evals say can be moved by injected instructions inside the state, and is overconfident on unanswerable inputs. `pass` therefore gives false comfort. /jev:screen allows Bash(curl:*) and WebFetch. Fetched content is written to temp files and passed as @file, which is safe from argv injection. The skill's 'block' guidance is good behavior, but it relies on model discretion.

Trust chain: the plugin adds the skill allow-list Bash(jev:*) and Bash(npx jevctl:*). `npx jevctl` fetches and runs npm code at call time, so it is a supply-chain and auto-approval risk if used as the fallback. Prefer a global install pinned to a version. The hook (early-access function hooks) runs plugin TypeScript inside the Claude Code engine with $.http.fetch, $.env.get and $.settings.read access. It can read the whole settings env, but the code only reads TYPESAFE_API_KEY (fast-jev.ts:245-252). Third-party plugin code runs in-process, so pin the version and review it.

Compaction hook risk: it sends the full transcript (tool inputs and outputs, up to maxStateTokens 25000) to the provider (api.typesafe.ai, or OpenRouter if patched). That includes any secret or client data that appeared in tool output. It also alters the conversation by truncating tool results to 300 chars and dropping calls. There is a fallback, but a wrong 'not needed' decision silently loses context.

Provenance: young project (created 2026-09-18), single maintainer (Nasr Shaer 33 of 39 commits, plus MrJev and dependabot), SECURITY.md present. Compaction is adapted from tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction (MIT, vendored). CI runs typecheck, biome, build, tests on Node 20/22/24, and `claude plugin validate`.
gh-nasrallah-al-jev-cli.dataEgress: CLI: exactly the state and questions of each call go to the provider. With OpenRouter that is POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with body {model:'typesafe/jev-1.13', state, questions} and Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY. State is whatever text you pass: claims, evidence, fetched pages, file contents for find (up to 250 files at 2000 chars each), and so on. --dry-run prints the exact request first. Also a daily `npm view jevctl version` call to the npm registry (suppress with JEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1). Compaction hook: the fitted conversation history (tool call inputs and results, up to about 25k estimated tokens per request, several requests, concurrency 4) goes to api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone with the TYPESAFE key. It is not wired to OpenRouter. No other telemetry found.
gh-nasrallah-al-jev-cli.failureMode: CLI: fail-closed in the sense of a non-zero exit. Errors give exit 1 (network, config, malformed response). A judgment match gives exit 2 (default --fail-on: verify contradicted, screen block). validateAnswers (provider.ts:120-150) rejects missing or mistyped answers so a proxy failure cannot masquerade as a pass. The default timeout is 30 s per attempt (config.ts:49), and the TypeSafe transport retries twice. Nothing blocks Claude Code, because the CLI is invoked by the model through Bash. If the CLI is missing, the skill says to tell the user. Hook: fail-open to the built-in summary on missing key, HTTP or parse errors, budget overflow or a low reduction ratio (fast-jev.ts session.compact try/catch and next(event)). The turn.complete handler swallows errors and skips auto-compact. The risk is not failure but a successful yet wrong compaction (a lossy truncation replaces the summary). Note that the auto-compact trigger at 60% context is more aggressive than Claude Code's own default.
gh-nasrallah-al-jev-cli.contextCost: No MCP server, so no tool-definition overhead. The skill listing entry costs its description (about 1.3 KB, roughly 330 tokens) against the user's 2% skill listing budget. The 8 slash commands add about 8 KB of files in total, and their one-line descriptions are listed. When the skill is invoked, SKILL.md (13,253 chars, about 3.3k tokens) is loaded once into context. Each /jev:* command adds about 250-320 tokens. The hook injects no text into context. Compaction shows a toast and UI log only. Every jev call adds JSON output tokens unless --pluck is used.
gh-nasrallah-al-jev-cli.latencyImpact: Per CLI call: Node startup, plus one Jev request (p50 about 200 ms, p95 about 600 ms per the brief) plus the Bash tool overhead. The daily `npm view` update check can add seconds once a day per config cache, and is best disabled with JEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1. Nothing is added to the PreToolUse or PostToolUse paths, because the plugin registers no such hooks. The compaction hook adds several concurrent requests with up to 25k tokens each on compaction (seconds), and only at compaction time.
gh-nasrallah-al-jev-cli.autoInvocation: Partial and model-discretionary. The skill's description makes Claude likely to run `jev screen`, `verify` and `find` when the task matches, but nothing is deterministic. There is no PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest or UserPromptSubmit hook, so untrusted WebFetch and Bash output is never screened automatically. Slash commands are user-invoked. The only deterministic behaviors are the two function hooks (session.compact, turn.complete), which need CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 and a TYPESAFE key, so with OpenRouter only they would need patching. To meet the 'automatic without prompting' goal, the user would still write their own hooks (for example a PostToolUse WebFetch screen using `jev screen --fail-on block`, or the cookbook PermissionRequest gate) that call this CLI. That is feasible because of the stable exit codes.
pros: The CLI supports OpenRouter today with no patching: src/provider.ts:223-232 POSTs to /api/alpha/decisions with model typesafe/jev-1.13 and the OPENROUTER_API_KEY bearer. Setting JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter suffices, and it also handles the 'jev-latest' to 'jev-1.13' mapping that OpenRouter needs.

Broadest single surface for Jev: screen (injection plus substance), verify, find, classify, extract, rerank, route, batch, all with --json, --pluck and stable exit codes (0/1/2) that are usable as gates in the user's own hooks. That fits the OpenRouter cookbook fail-open pattern.

Careful engineering: validateAnswers rejects malformed proxy responses so a failure cannot count as 'probability 0'. --dry-run shows the exact outgoing payload. There is a stderr notice when a stray OPENROUTER_API_KEY silently triggers a third-party hop. Keys are never accepted on argv, and keychain or a 0600 file is used. Uses execFileSync with arrays, not shell strings.

Real test and CI investment for a 12-day-old project: about 200 vitest cases across commands, provider, config, output and the hook (test/plugin/hook.test.ts), CI on Node 20/22/24, biome, `claude plugin validate`, a drift check for the vendored hook, CHANGELOG, SECURITY.md, docs per command. MIT with NOTICE. Published on npm (0.2.3) and matching GitHub releases.

Zero MCP overhead and small always-on context: only a skill description entry, no tool schemas. SKILL.md gives sound guidance (check exists_verdict before trusting the top hit, treat `unclear` and `review` as a human decision, never ask the user to paste keys into chat). Works for personal and client projects when scoped, since --dry-run lets the data sent be inspected.

Compaction hook has sensible safeguards (falls back to the built-in summary on error or when reduction is under 25%, keeps recent messages and all user/assistant text, a concurrency cap, a toast with counts) and is a genuine novel use of Jev for context pruning.
cons: The only deterministic automation is the compaction hook, and it is TypeSafe-only: fast-jev.ts:189 and 245-252 require TYPESAFE_API_KEY, the URL is hardcoded to api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (request.ts:6), the default model is 'jev-latest' (not valid on OpenRouter), and there is no baseUrl or provider option. The user would need a local fork, and updates would overwrite it.

The hook depends on the early-access CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 feature; the type reference was generated on Claude Code 2.1.274 (user has 2.1.285). Replacing Claude Code's summary with lossy truncation, and auto-compacting at 60% context, is risky on client work and untested against this user's setup. Full transcripts (including any secrets in tool output) would leave the machine. Not recommended to enable.

Auto-invocation relies on the model choosing to run `jev` (skill description and Bash). There is no PreToolUse, PostToolUse or PermissionRequest hook shipped, so untrusted web fetches are not screened deterministically and the user's 'never have to prompt use jev' goal is only weakly met. The user would need to write their own hooks around `jev screen` / `jev ask`.

Requires a global `npm install -g jevctl` (the skill falls back to `npx jevctl`, which fetches unpinned code at run time and is pre-approved via allowed-tools Bash(npx jevctl:*)), plus a Node CLI cold start on every call. Its hidden daily `npm view` subprocess on normal commands needs JEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1.

Jev screen has documented weaknesses (injected instructions in state can move answers, overconfidence), so a `pass` is not a guarantee. The skill instructs Claude to trust `block/review/pass` outcomes without warning about this.

Very young and single-maintainer: created 2026-09-18, 23 stars, 3 forks, 0.2.x with pre-1.0 breaking-change warnings, marketplace plugin.json at 0.2.0 vs npm 0.2.3, the OpenRouter route uses the /alpha endpoint, and the OpenRouter key must start with sk-or- or is ignored silently in auto. The OPENROUTER_API_KEY is also not in the user's no-secret-leak protected-vars list yet.
gh-nasrallah-al-jev-cli.verdict: Solid, well-tested Jev CLI that already works with OpenRouter and gives stable exit codes for gating (screen, verify, ask), which is the best building block found for the user's own PermissionRequest/PostToolUse hooks. As a plugin it is only partly automatic (the skill is model-discretionary, and the deterministic compaction hook is TypeSafe-only, experimental and risky for client work), so use the CLI (pinned global install, JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter, JEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1) and skip the compaction hook.

gh-clownware-bouncer.name: clownware/bouncer
gh-clownware-bouncer.whatItDoes: Claude Code plugin with one PreToolUse hook (Bash|Edit|Write|NotebookEdit). It first applies deterministic hard rules and a fast-path allowlist. It then sends a redacted, structured description of the action plus about 7 noul questions from a user-owned YAML policy to Jev at api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone. Thresholds turn the answers into allow/ask/deny. Modes are observe (default, emits nothing), guard, full and seatbelt (for bypass sessions: hard rules deny, otherwise silent). It logs to decisions.jsonl and ships /calibrate, /explain, /mode and /status commands plus one SKILL.md.

providerSupport.evidence: The hook path is TypeSafe-only. src/hooks/pretooluse.ts:434 builds `new JevAdapter({ apiKey: apiKey() ?? "" })` with no baseUrl and no model. src/adapters/jev.ts:19-20 hard-codes DEFAULT_BASE_URL=https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone and DEFAULT_MODEL="jev-latest" (used at jev.ts:157,162). The key comes only from BOUNCER_TYPESAFE_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY (src/io/config.ts:170-176). The jev@<url> compat backend (config.ts:196-219, jev.ts:34) is wired only into calibrate (src/commands/calibrate.ts:490-492). The hook's adapterFor accepts only mock, jev and local (pretooluse.ts:433-441), so BOUNCER_BACKEND=jev@... makes the hook fail with `unknown backend`. Even in calibrate, the TypeSafe key is deliberately never sent to a jev@ URL (config.ts:182-186), so OpenRouter would need BOUNCER_JEV_COMPAT_API_KEY. The model is still hard-coded to jev-latest, and OpenRouter expects jev-1.13 or typesafe/jev-1.13. The `local` backend is an OpenAI-style chat adapter that needs logprobs and logit_bias, which OpenRouter does not give for Jev.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Moderate, and it needs a source fork plus rebuild. You would change adapterFor in pretooluse.ts to take a base URL, model and key from env (about 10-15 lines in TS), then run `npm run build` to regenerate the committed 12,937-line bin/bouncer.cjs bundle. Alternatively, hand-edit the bundle's DEFAULT_BASE_URL, DEFAULT_MODEL and key lookup. Either way you carry a fork and lose plugin auto-update. The adapter already speaks the {model,state,questions}->{answers} wire shape, which matches OpenRouter /api/v1/systemone. The model name (jev-1.13) and the Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY are the only differences. Untested by the author.
providerSupport.others: local (OpenAI-compatible llama.cpp or vLLM with logprobs), chat@<url> (calibration only), mock

interface.name: PreToolUse hook (hooks/hooks.json)
interface.purpose: matcher Bash|Edit|Write|NotebookEdit -> node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/bouncer.cjs pretooluse, Claude Code timeout 5 s. The policy's own timeout_ms defaults to 800. The hook emits permissionDecision allow/ask/deny with a reason, or nothing.

interface.name: /bouncer:calibrate
interface.purpose: Runs labelled fixtures through a backend (jev, jev@url, chat@url, local, mock), with --compare, --out and --from. Prints accuracy, Brier, ECE and false-allow gates.

interface.name: /bouncer:explain [tool_use_id]
interface.purpose: Shows per-question probabilities and the rule that decided the last or a named call.

interface.name: /bouncer:mode
interface.purpose: Shows or switches observe, guard, full or seatbelt.

interface.name: /bouncer:status
interface.purpose: Shows policy source, decision counts and p50/p95 latency from the log.

interface.name: skills/bouncer/SKILL.md
interface.purpose: Model-invoked skill, triggered when the user asks why a call was blocked or how to tune the policy. It has a description of about 500 chars and no MCP.

interface.name: CLI subcommands (bin/bouncer.cjs)
interface.purpose: Beyond the hook and commands, src/cli.ts also has judge, measure, export and skills. judge is a batch judge, measure uses a BOUNCER_REASONING_CMD shell command, and skills is a skill router. These are not wired into hooks.json.

security: Hook path has no shell exec of user data. The only child_process use is src/io/reasoning.ts (BOUNCER_REASONING_CMD, spawn shell:true), reached from the `measure` command and not from the hook. That command string comes from the environment.

Key handling is env-only, so no argv exposure (config.ts:153-176). The TypeSafe key is never forwarded to a jev@ URL (config.ts:182-186). The compat and local keys support *_FILE variants. The key is never read from policy YAML, so a cloned repo cannot redirect it.

A repo-level .bouncer.yaml overrides the user policy (config.ts:20-30). A hostile repo can only add prompts or change thresholds. But in mode full it could set thresholds or fast_path to auto-allow, and the docs argue that allow never widens what Claude Code permits. Worth knowing for client repos, since cloning a repo adopts its policy.

Prompt-injection surface: the command text goes into the state. It is structured as JSON fields to reduce impersonation (state.ts:13-17), but the author admits it 'narrows, does not close' the surface and is not a security boundary. Jev is known to be steerable by injected state. The mitigation is that deterministic hard rules run before the model and cannot be argued with.

Redaction: 14 regex shapes (private keys, sk-, ghp_, AKIA, JWT, bearer, url-credentials, assigned-secret) are applied before send and again on log write (redact.ts, log.ts). It is shape matching only, and the source says so. An OPENROUTER_API_KEY value would be caught only by the assigned-secret or sk-or... shape (`sk-or-v1-...` matches the openai-key regex \bsk-... 20+ chars).

CI has a gitleaks scan and action pins by SHA. The installer is the Claude Code plugin marketplace (marketplace.json source ./), with no install scripts. bin/bouncer.cjs is a committed esbuild bundle of about 12.9k lines including the yaml dep, so it is hard to audit and depends on the maintainer's build being honest. The repo is 2 weeks old with one main author, and 91 of 243 commits are by 'Claude'.
Telemetry: none found. The only network call sites are the Jev adapter and local.ts to the configured URL.
gh-clownware-bouncer.dataEgress: To api.typesafe.ai on each judged Bash/Edit/Write/NotebookEdit call (not on hard-rule or fast-path hits). It sends a JSON state of tool name, permission mode, cwd-relative and path-labelled facts, the redacted command line (capped at 4096 bytes), file existence, and byte counts for Write and Edit. It also sends about 7 question texts. Write.content, Edit old_string/new_string and NotebookEdit new_source are never sent (state.ts:5-9). Command strings and file paths do leave the machine, including client project names, hostnames and paths, with only regex-shape redaction. Locally it writes decisions.jsonl (redacted state, up to 8 MB x 2) under the plugin data dir or ~/.bouncer.
gh-clownware-bouncer.failureMode: Fail-open to the normal Claude Code prompt or flow. Every error path returns no decision (pretooluse.ts header and standDown at 257-296): timeout, bad key, 429 or 5xx, malformed response, an unloadable policy, or a missing policy. A per-session circuit breaker stands down after repeated failures. A partly answered response can never produce allow. A truncated state cannot be approved. on_error: deny is opt-in and is a no-op in observe. Timeouts are the policy timeout_ms (default 800) with at most one retry inside the same deadline, under a 5 s Claude Code hook timeout. With no TypeSafe key set, adapterFor throws an auth error and the hook stands down silently. Hard rules run before the adapter, so seatbelt with no key still gives the deterministic floor. It also wastes a breaker and log write on each judged call.
gh-clownware-bouncer.contextCost: Very low. There is no MCP server and no tool definitions. The hook injects no additionalContext, only a permissionDecisionReason or a rare systemMessage. The one skill description is about 500 chars (about 125 tokens) against the user's 2% skill budget. The four slash-command files add nothing until used. The bin/bouncer.cjs bundle is never loaded into context.
gh-clownware-bouncer.latencyImpact: README (line 674) measures 437 ms median and 549 ms p95 for a 7-question Jev call, with about 480 ms end to end and about 50 ms hook process overhead. That is per judged Bash/Edit/Write call, on top of the user's gitnexus and no-secret-leak hooks (Node cold start about 35-120 ms each). Hard rules and fast-path hits are near-instant, but the fast path matched 0 of 88 real calls because agents chain commands. Through OpenRouter (/alpha, p95 about 600 ms) the cost would be similar or worse. The policy timeout of 800 ms means slow calls fail open to a normal prompt.
gh-clownware-bouncer.autoInvocation: Fully automatic and deterministic. It is a PreToolUse hook on Bash/Edit/Write/NotebookEdit, so it needs no prompting. It ships in observe mode (logs only), so nothing takes effect until the user switches mode. Modes are skipped only for permission modes listed in skip_permission_modes (default plan). The bouncer skill is model-invoked only for explain and tune questions.
pros: Seatbelt mode is the right shape for this user's frequent bypassPermissions sessions: 19 deterministic hard rules (credential-file reads, git reset --hard, force push, clean -f, stash drop, credential literals on the command line, etc.) deny before any network call (hardrules.ts, default.yaml, evaluate.ts:231). Otherwise it is silent, so it adds no interruptions.

Careful safety engineering: observe by default, no path from error to block (pretooluse.ts:1-6), partial answers cannot allow, truncated state cannot allow, a per-session circuit breaker, and the policy cannot widen Claude Code permissions. The action description is sent instead of file contents or diffs.

Substantial verification for a 2-week-old repo: 34 test files, CI with gitleaks and pinned actions, 10 ADRs, a published calibration table (docs/calibration, 9 runs with committed jsonl), a frozen holdout set and a calibration harness with false-allow gates. The policy is versionable YAML per repo.
No context cost (no MCP, no injected text) and no shell exec in the hook path. Keys are env-only with *_FILE support, and are never forwarded to unrelated hosts.
The wire adapter is already the exact /systemone {model,state,questions} shape, so the fork to OpenRouter is small.
cons: OpenRouter is not supported in the hook. The hook is hard-wired to api.typesafe.ai with model jev-latest and a TypeSafe key (pretooluse.ts:434, jev.ts:19-20). The jev@<url> route exists only in calibrate, so the candidate's 'partial' rating overstates it. Using OpenRouter means forking, editing the TS and rebuilding the 12.9k-line committed bundle. The user would also need a separate TypeSafe key or a patch to use OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
Adds about 0.45-0.55 s (README 437/549 ms) to every judged Bash/Edit/Write, stacked on the gitnexus and no-secret-leak hooks. Bash calls that agents chain almost never hit the fast path (0 of 88).

Sends the redacted command line and file paths to a third party on every judged call. That is a problem for client work, and redaction is regex-shape only. OPENROUTER_API_KEY is still not in the user's no-secret-leak protected list, which is a separate gap.

Duplicates the user's fail-closed no-secret-leak hook. The value of the Jev questions on top of the hard rules is unproven for this user. Calibration is on the author's fixtures and mostly self-written, and Jev is known to be overconfident. It is not a security boundary, and the author says so.

Immature: created 2026-09-18, v0.2.9, 1 star, 2 forks, 2 human contributors plus Claude bot commits, no releases, a bundled artifact, and rapid churn (243 commits in 12 days). Observe mode as the default means no benefit until the user tunes the policy.

In defaultMode 'auto' the hook still runs and its ask/deny may stack with the auto classifier. The docs cover bypass and default modes, and the interaction with auto mode is not documented. Also, `full` (which can remove prompts) is explicitly not yet trusted by the author.
gh-clownware-bouncer.verdict: Well-engineered, fail-safe permission gate that fits the bypassPermissions use case. But the hook cannot talk to OpenRouter: it is hard-wired to api.typesafe.ai, jev-latest and a TypeSafe key, and the jev@ compat route exists only in calibrate. Getting OpenRouter means forking and rebuilding the bundle, and the added latency, the overlap with the existing hooks and the egress of commands to a third party are real costs. Its deterministic seatbelt floor is worth stealing or running keyless, and the Jev layer is secondary.

gh-keltokhy-jgrep.name: jev-grep (jgrep)
gh-keltokhy-jgrep.whatItDoes: Python CLI (PyPI jev-grep 0.6.0, command jgrep) that turns each input line, paragraph, file, JSONL/CSV field, text chunk, Python/Go/C function, or unified-diff hunk into one Jev yes/no (Noul) question built from a plain-English description. It prints matches in input order with probabilities. Answers are cached in SQLite and a $1 budget applies by default. It ships one SKILL.md (skills/jgrep/SKILL.md) but no MCP server, no hook, and no plugin.json or marketplace.json. Provider plumbing (URLs, keys, retries, cache, budget) lives in a separate shared package, jevkit-runtime 0.4.2 (github.com/keltokhy/jevkit-core, MIT, 0 stars, same author).

providerSupport.evidence: Providers are defined in jevkit-core, not in this repo. jgrep/core.py:5 declares PROVIDERS = catalog('typesafe','openrouter','gateway','diffusiongemma','laya','gliner'). jevkit-core src/jevkit_runtime/providers.py:76-91 gives typesafe = https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, model jev-1.13.0, env TYPESAFE_API_KEY. It gives openrouter = https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions, model typesafe/jev-1.13, env OPENROUTER_API_KEY. providers.py:92-99 defines a generic gateway with JEV_GATEWAY_URL and JEV_GATEWAY_API_KEY. settings.py:71-77 reads the key from the env var first, then ~/.config/jev/<provider>.key. client.py:205-209 sends 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' plus 'X-Title: jev tools' as HTTP headers, so the key never appears in argv. providers.py:154-191 selects a provider: --api or JEV_API wins, otherwise the first auto-selectable provider with a key, in the order typesafe then openrouter. The local providers have auto_select=False. For this user (OpenRouter key only), auto-selection lands on OpenRouter with no extra config.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Not needed. OpenRouter is a first-class provider and uses the /api/alpha/decisions endpoint with the typesafe/jev-1.13 model. It is one export away (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or a chmod 600 ~/.config/jev/openrouter.key). JEV_API=openrouter makes it explicit if a TypeSafe key is ever added. JEV_URL and JEV_MODEL overrides also exist (settings.py).
providerSupport.others: Also supports a self-hosted System One gateway (LiteLLM etc.) and three experimental local servers (OpenJev/DiffusionGemma, Laya, GLiNER2.5-Decide) that need no key. Those local servers would keep code off the network.

interface.name: jgrep "desc" [files|stdin]
interface.purpose: Line filter. One Jev call per line, default threshold -p 0.5, up to 32 concurrent calls (-j), 15 s timeout with 4 attempts and backoff. Exit 0/1/2 like grep.

interface.name: -o / --json / --jsonl --field / --csv --field / -c / -l / -q / -m / -v / -n / -H
interface.purpose: Output and record modes: probability column, JSON per match, structured records, counts, file lists, quiet mode, match cap.

interface.name: -r --glob --exclude --no-ignore
interface.purpose: Recursive search that respects .gitignore, skips symlinks and binaries.

interface.name: -e DESC (--all), -C N, --para, --whole, --chunks N --overlap N
interface.purpose: Multiple descriptions in one call, neighbour-line context, paragraph/whole-file/overlapping-passage units.

interface.name: --functions [--lang python|go|c]
interface.purpose: Judge complete functions and methods. Python uses stdlib ast. Go and C need the [code] extra (tree-sitter).

interface.name: --diff [-W|--function-context] [--repo DIR]
interface.purpose: Judge each unified-diff hunk from git diff, git log -p or format-patch. With -W it also sends the enclosing Python/Go/C function, read via git cat-file or the working tree.

interface.name: --estimate [--json]
interface.purpose: Offline preview of call count, tokens and cost. Needs no key and makes no network call.

interface.name: --emit-records
interface.purpose: Offline JSONL export of parsed units, with no model call.

interface.name: --budget / JEV_BUDGET, --timeout, --record FILE, --stats, --no-cache, --api, --model, --unordered, --max-chars
interface.purpose: Runtime controls. Default budget is $1 (cli.py:45). Default model is pinned to typesafe/jev-1.13 on OpenRouter.

interface.name: skills/jgrep/SKILL.md
interface.purpose: The only Claude Code artifact. Frontmatter name jgrep, one long description sentence (about 190 chars). The body (about 4.5 KB, roughly 1.1k tokens) documents diff/function/estimate usage and limitations. There is no hook, MCP server, or plugin manifest.

security: Key handling is good. The Bearer key goes in an HTTP header (jevkit-core client.py:205-209), never argv. It is read from env or ~/.config/jev/openrouter.key. SECURITY.md says keys are never written to the cache or logs. I did not audit every logging path.

This user's existing no-secret-leak hook does not list OPENROUTER_API_KEY. An env-var key would be visible to any Bash command Claude runs (env, printenv). A key file at ~/.config/jev/openrouter.key is also readable by Read or cat unless the hook is extended.

No shell exec: diff_context.py:71 and :101 call git via subprocess with fixed argv lists. GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH, GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS and protocol.ext.allow=never are set to blunt hostile repos. -W confines paths to the repo root. The README says it is not a sandbox. A worker-process pool exists in jevkit-core workers.py; I did not review it in depth.

No telemetry found: the only outbound hits are the provider endpoint (plus an X-Title 'jev tools' header) and the optional gateway or local URLs. The X-Title header lets OpenRouter attribute traffic to 'jev tools'.

Prompt-injection surface: every judged line, hunk or function is untrusted text placed in the Jev state. The README admits 'text in the input can try to steer the answer. Do not use jgrep as a security boundary'. Output is only a probability, so Jev cannot inject instructions into Claude, and matched lines are echoed verbatim to Claude's context, which is normal grep behaviour.

Supply chain: this is a single-maintainer, one-person project created 2026-09-18. Publishing uses PyPI Trusted Publishing from a GitHub workflow with actions pinned by SHA. The runtime dependency jevkit-runtime is a second package from the same author, at version 0.4.2. The repo is only 12 days old, so it has no track record.

Install happens outside Claude Code (uv tool install jev-grep), a PyPI package the user would have to trust. I did not run it. The pyproject [tool.uv.sources] editable path ../jevkit-core only affects source checkouts; the published wheel depends on the PyPI jevkit-runtime.

Local cache ~/.cache/jev/answers.v3.sqlite persists answers keyed by provider, endpoint, model, text and description (protocol.answer_key). I did not verify whether it stores plaintext or a hash of client code; treat it as possibly containing derived data.
gh-keltokhy-jgrep.dataEgress: Every judged unit is POSTed to openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions. That is the full line (up to 8000 chars by default), the -C neighbour lines, the whole paragraph, file or chunk, the full function body for --functions, and each full diff hunk plus the enclosing function up to 8000 chars with -W. The description question goes along with it, plus the model name and the Bearer key. Cached answers are not re-sent. A recursive search over a client repo therefore uploads its source text to OpenRouter, and from there to TypeSafe as the model provider. A large run is one request per unit (32 in flight), which is an easy way to send a lot of client code without a prompt. No file paths or telemetry are sent beyond what the state text contains. The local backends (--api diffusiongemma, laya or gliner) keep everything on the machine but need a self-run server.
gh-keltokhy-jgrep.failureMode: Fail-closed for the tool itself, not for Claude Code. There is no hook, so a jgrep failure cannot block anything. Bad key: JevFatal stops the run at once, exit 2. Timeout: the default is 15 s per line with 4 attempts, exponential backoff, and Retry-After honoured for 408/429/5xx/529 (transport.py:16,52). Failed lines are reported as errors and exit 2. Budget: at $1 the run stops with 'stopped at the budget' and exits 2 while printing partial results. Distinguishing 'no match' (exit 1) from 'error' (exit 2) is well handled, but Claude has to read the exit code and stderr. On the alpha endpoint with no SLA, a large tree at 32 concurrency can hit 429s and produce partial results.
gh-keltokhy-jgrep.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no hook-injected text. As a skill, the description is one line of about 190 chars (about 50 tokens against a skillListingBudgetFraction of 0.02). The SKILL.md body is about 4.5 KB (about 1.1k tokens), loaded only when the skill is invoked. Output goes to Claude only for what it pipes back, e.g. 'jgrep ... | head'.
gh-keltokhy-jgrep.autoInvocation: Skill-description trigger only (model discretion). The description is 'Filter text, records, code functions, or complete diff hunks by a plain-English description using Jev. Use for semantic filtering and code navigation...'. It says nothing about when Claude should pick it over Grep, and it is not framed as a proactive default. Nothing forces it: no hook, no CLAUDE.md snippet, and no permission allow-rules are provided. The SKILL.md starts with 'Check command -v jgrep', so the CLI must be installed first. To make it automatic, the user would need their own CLAUDE.md rule or a rewritten skill description, plus Bash(jgrep:*) in the allowlist.
pros: OpenRouter is first-class and working out of the box: jevkit-core providers.py:84-91 uses /api/alpha/decisions with typesafe/jev-1.13, and OPENROUTER_API_KEY or ~/.config/jev/openrouter.key is auto-selected when it is the only key. No patching.

Real code-oriented modes rather than only text grep: --functions (Python AST; Go/C via tree-sitter), --diff for git diff/log -p hunks, and -W for enclosing-function context. All are usable as a review filter, e.g. `git diff | jgrep --diff "removes error handling"`.

--estimate is genuinely offline (no key, no network) and reports call count, tokens and cost. A hard $1 default budget, reserved per request before sending, guards against a stray recursive run. The cache makes repeats free.

Safety-conscious engineering: git is invoked via fixed argv with hostile-repo env flags, -W paths are confined to the repo root, key goes in a header, and no telemetry was found. The README and SKILL.md openly state that model output is not a security boundary and that flagged code needs manual inspection.

Broad tests: about 146 test functions across 10 files, offline against a fake API and a local HTTP server. There are benchmarks (SMS spam F1 0.91, AG News 86.6%, a 20-example code-review experiment) and honest caveats. The license is MIT, and releases (v0.4.1 tag, PyPI 0.6.0) are published via trusted publishing.
Tiny context footprint: no MCP tools, a roughly 50-token skill listing entry, and a roughly 1.1k-token body loaded only on use. Cost is about $0.0000126 per typical line.
Pipe-friendly with grep-style exit codes and --json output, so it can be chained in Bash or wrapped in a user-written hook.
cons: It is a filter over text Claude already has or a file set, not a decision gate and not a replacement for real Grep or gitnexus. Claude will still default to Grep/gitnexus unless the description or a CLAUDE.md rule pushes it. The skill description contains no 'use proactively when...' guidance, so the user's 'never prompt use jev' goal is not met by the repo as shipped.

Every judged unit is uploaded to OpenRouter and TypeSafe. --functions -r or --diff -W on a client repo sends source code out, one request per function or hunk, at 32 concurrent. There is no allowlist, secret redaction, or per-project opt-in. For client projects this needs a policy decision, or a local --api backend.

Cost is per unit, not per file: a large recursive run means thousands of parallel calls to an /alpha endpoint with no SLA and 32k context, risking 429s and partial results (exit 2). The $1 budget caps spend but not egress volume.

Accuracy limits apply: TypeSafe itself documents weak spots (counting, numeric comparison, double negatives, long inputs). Jev's overconfidence on unanswerable inputs and injection steering are amplified when the input is untrusted repo text. The tool's own code-review experiment used only 20 handwritten examples.

Brand new and single-maintainer: created 2026-09-18, 52 commits in 12 days (47 by keltokhy, 4 by Claude, 1 by Neel Patel), 4 forks, and a runtime split across two repos (jevkit-core has 0 stars). The GitHub release tag is v0.4.1 while pyproject and PyPI are at 0.6.0, and a 0.5.x/0.6.0 breaking change to --budget semantics already happened. Expect API churn.

Install and setup are manual: `uv tool install jev-grep` (PyPI, not vetted by this audit), the key must be placed in env or a file, the skill has to be copied into ~/.claude/skills, and Bash(jgrep:*) must be allowed. OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not covered by the user's no-secret-leak hook.

Fit to the workflow is narrow. Many daily tasks (find a symbol, read a file) are better served by ripgrep/gitnexus at zero cost and zero egress. The best fit is the semantic review filter on diffs, and that is an occasional rather than daily use.
Known open limitations documented in the README: CRLF patches and quoted paths with spaces give spurious errors, and C with macros is often skipped.
gh-keltokhy-jgrep.verdict: The strongest OpenRouter-ready Jev CLI found so far. It is well engineered, tested and cost-guarded, and works with only OPENROUTER_API_KEY, with a small context footprint. It is still an opt-in filter, not an automatic integration: nothing makes Claude reach for it, it uploads client source to OpenRouter and TypeSafe, and it is a 12-day-old single-author project. Worth installing as a manually or CLAUDE.md-nudged semantic diff/function filter for personal repos, not as the automatic Jev backbone.

security: Key handling is good: keystore.py resolves env then OS secret store then 0600 file; Linux store uses `secret-tool store` with the key on stdin (keystore.py ~195), not argv; macOS `security ... -w value` briefly puts key in a child's argv (acknowledged in a comment, irrelevant on Linux). `jev setup-key` serves a one-time localhost page with Host-header check, so the agent never sees the key. Caveat: store() also writes the key into every ~/.hermes profile .env if that dir exists.

OPENROUTER_API_KEY is read from process env first; if the user exports it via settings env, every Bash subprocess (and the agent) can read it; it is not in no-secret-leak.cjs protected list yet (user-side gap, not the candidate's).

Shell exec: `jev lane step --run <cmd>` runs the agent-supplied string with shell=True, cwd=repo, 900s timeout (lanes.py:145) - equivalent to Bash tool, but it bypasses Claude Code Bash permission rules/hooks matching, since the permission sees only `jev lane step ...`. Under bypass/auto mode this is a permission-laundering path for the arbitrary command in --run.

Installer modifies ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (backup + marker block, additive and removable via --uninstall), writes ~/.claude/agents and skills, symlinks ~/.local/bin/jev to the checkout (executes code from the clone on every call; a compromised update = code exec). Also touches ~/.codex/~/.agents skills and Hermes config if present. --check dry-run and --no-claude-md exist.

Prompt-injection surface: skills instruct the agent to pass task text to a third-party model; Jev's outputs are typed (closed action ids, thresholds in code), and code-first pre-rules/risk words are enforced locally; jev rerank has an injection screen for passages. Independent evals say injected instructions in state can move Jev answers - mitigated only partly by local rails.

No telemetry found: outbound hosts in code are the four Jev providers, models.dev/api.json (catalog, key names only), key-setup links; plan.py has an OpenRouter v1 base for a computer-use planner (chat completions, separate feature). Logs hold decisions only, per README. Not exhaustively audited (678-line installer, ~50 modules, 216 files).
SECURITY.md with private reporting; two data-leak bugs reportedly fixed. Contributors: 8 (Steve Darlow 89 of 114 commits, plus a bot-like 'DevBot' and 'Co-Agent'), repo 12 days old, MIT.
gh-kerpopule-hermes-jev-skills.dataEgress: For Claude Code lane use: `jev lane classify` sends the task text you pass (redacted, capped 3,000 chars) plus optional --context line; `lane step` sends task text, a diff stat and the last ~15 lines/1,200 chars of each check's output (redacted; sensitive-looking text is withheld); paths outside the diff stat and whole logs/files are not sent; `facts` never sent. Other commands per README: route sends the redacted turn up to 2,500 chars; rerank 900 chars/passage; search question + result snippets; gate command up to 2,000 chars with comments stripped. Everything goes to openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (when JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter), with HTTP-Referer github URL and X-Title 'Hermes Jev Skills'. `jev models` fetches models.dev/api.json (no data uploaded). A separate `jev doctor` verify call sends a synthetic sentence. Client work is included in task text whenever the agent writes it into --task, so client-project use needs a private-profile equivalent (only Hermes `private_profiles` exists).
gh-kerpopule-hermes-jev-skills.failureMode: Fail-open everywhere by design: no key, timeout (lane commands default 4 s, routing 2.5 s), 4xx/429/5xx, malformed reply, or low confidence all yield keep_current/no_opinion/verify-yourself (client.py JevError codes, retry loop bounded by total wall-clock budget; state_too_large at 60k chars; every reply validated against the asked question). Gate never approves on Jev failure (gate.py header). Caveat: fail-open here means 'do nothing extra', and since invocation is by model discretion there is no hard enforcement either way. `lane step` failures in the subprocess check (exit 124/127) are reported as evidence, not hidden.
gh-kerpopule-hermes-jev-skills.contextCost: No MCP tools, no hook-injected text. Always-on cost is static: CLAUDE.md lanes block ~1.9k chars (~480 tokens) every session; 11 skill descriptions (~150-250 chars each, ~2.3k chars, ~600 tokens incl. names) against the 2% skillListingBudgetFraction; 4 subagent descriptions (~250 chars each, ~250 tokens). Total roughly 1.3k tokens of standing context. Loading a full SKILL.md when triggered: 4.8k-16k chars each (jev-computer-use 16k = ~4k tokens; model-routing 9.5k = ~2.4k tokens). Each `jev` call adds a Bash tool call plus JSON result (~200-500 tokens).
gh-kerpopule-hermes-jev-skills.latencyImpact: Per CLI call: Python startup (~50-100 ms) + one HTTPS request ~0.4 s p50 measured by author (README), 4 s cap for lane commands; `lane step` additionally waits for the user's test command. Zero latency on turns where the agent does not choose to call it. Adds a serial Bash round-trip (model turn + tool call) before every delegated task, which dwarfs Jev's own latency.
gh-kerpopule-hermes-jev-skills.autoInvocation: Skill descriptions and one CLAUDE.md block, both at the model's discretion; no hooks (no PreToolUse/PermissionRequest/UserPromptSubmit/Stop wiring for Claude Code). The Hermes plugin's real automatic behaviours (pre_llm_call routing, web result screen, decide_tools) do not run in Claude Code. Claude Code only auto-picks lanes if Opus 5.5 chooses to follow the instruction when it delegates to subagents; the main-thread model is never switched.
pros: OpenRouter is a first-class, native backend: client.py:30-31 posts {state, model, questions} to /api/alpha/decisions with Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY; JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter selects it; no patching needed.

Strong engineering for safety and privacy: per-feature egress documented and enforced by redaction, secret-looking text never sent, question-shape validation, reply validation against the asked question, fail-open codes, risk words never route cheapest, gate never approves on failure.
Key handling well designed: secret-tool with stdin (no argv leak on Linux), one-time localhost setup page, --tty mode, JEV_PROXY_API_KEY isolation so provider keys never go to override hosts.
Installer is additive/removable: --check dry run, CLAUDE.md marker block with timestamped backup, --no-claude-md, --uninstall, agents only overwritten if they carry the managed marker.

Broad offline test suite (59 files, incl. test_install, test_lanes, test_custom_endpoint, test_gate); shadow-mode + `jev shadow report` culture and measured evals (lane replay: Sonnet lane -51% cost on 9 commits with parity, honest that Haiku was not cheapest).

jevkit is a reusable stdlib CLI: `jev decide`/`jev gate` with JSON policies could be wrapped by the user's own PermissionRequest hook (gate-strict/gate-task policies already model command-risk questions and return approve/ask_human/deny/no_opinion).
cons: No Claude Code hooks: nothing runs unless Claude decides to; this fails the user's core requirement of automatic use without prompting. Main automatic value (per-turn routing, web-injection screening, skill suggestion) is Hermes-only.

The Claude Code value proposition is downshifting delegated subagents to Haiku/Sonnet; with Opus 5.5 main and subscription billing this saves subscription usage only marginally, adds a Bash round-trip before each delegation, and the author's own data shows lanes barely help when work already runs at a mid model (-3.9% on 2,656 runs; 9-commit replay is a tiny sample).

Standing context ~1.3k tokens (CLAUDE.md block + 11 skill descriptions + 4 agent descriptions), much of it irrelevant to daily coding (mailbox, social research, computer/browser use, frontier-work Hermes ladder).

`jev lane step --run <cmd>` executes shell=True commands outside Claude Code's permission/hook matching; combined with bypassPermissions/auto and the existing fail-closed no-secret-leak hook, this is a hook-bypass path unless jev is denied or wrapped.

Provider precedence: TYPESAFE_API_KEY, keychain and credentials file win over OpenRouter unless JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter is set; installer symlinks ~/.local/bin/jev into a git checkout (unpinned code exec on update) and writes ~/.claude and ~/.codex; OPENROUTER_API_KEY not yet protected by user's leak hook.

Very young (created 2026-09-18, v0.22.0 in 11 days, 114 commits, 89 by one author, some bot-like committers), large surface (50 modules, 216 files) for a small useful core; uses ~typesafe/jev-latest moving alias on an /alpha endpoint with no SLA; Jev evals show calibration and injection weaknesses, and client-project task text would leave the machine with no private-profile control outside Hermes.
gh-kerpopule-hermes-jev-skills.verdict: Well-built, OpenRouter-native and fail-open, but for Claude Code it is only skills plus a CLAUDE.md nudge and lane subagents with no hooks, so it will not deliver automatic use and its lane routing adds ~1.3k standing tokens for marginal gain on an Opus-main subscription setup. Best treated as a source of reusable pieces (jevkit client, gate/decide policies, question-writing docs) rather than installed wholesale.

gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.name: jevwire (wesleydionisio fork of Brainwires/jevwire)
gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.whatItDoes: Claude Code plugin (v0.6.0) + stdio MCP server (6 tools) + embeddable TS library around Jev. The plugin hooks (SessionStart cmd; UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SessionEnd as type:http posts to a self-spawned loopback daemon on 127.0.0.1:10522) run a deterministic bash/path prefilter, then ask Jev typed questions for: tool-call gate notes (additionalContext) and a deny-once "tripwire" (hard regex shapes like rm -rf ~, force-push main, DROP TABLE, plus Jev-scored destructive/outward/out-of-scope calls), prompt-injection screening of WebFetch/WebSearch/mcp__ results, stop-short and false "tests pass" detection at Stop, optional per-prompt task classification. Never emits allow, never prompts the user unless ask_on_trip. It is a fork of Brainwires/jevwire (original author Josh Guyette); Wesley Dionisio added the OpenRouter provider in 4 commits on 2026-09-18 (a27d59c, d9d9f58, 0f852ef, 92bf204). Upstream Brainwires has since moved to 0.6.3 (pr_scope commit lint, staged-secret trip) and its tree has no src/jev/provider.ts, so the OpenRouter support exists only in this fork.

gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.tests: 44 vitest files (about 15k lines) incl. hooks conformance (http vs command hook byte-equality), never-allow, daemon e2e/control/watchdog, redact, openrouter.test.ts, replay/acceptance snapshots; CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs type-check, tests, build and a committed-bundle freshness check on Node 20/22. Not run here.
gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.runtime: Node >=20 (TypeScript, esbuild single-file dependency-free bundles plugin/dist/hook.mjs 240 KB and mcp.mjs 1.5 MB committed); no install/build step; long-lived detached node daemon on 127.0.0.1:10522
gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.install: /plugin marketplace add wesleydionisio/jevwire (fork) or Brainwires/jevwire (upstream, no OpenRouter), /plugin install jev@brainwires-jevwire, set OpenRouter API key in /plugin option or export OPENROUTER_API_KEY + JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter before launching claude, then /reload-plugins. Or bare MCP: claude mcp add jev -e JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter -e OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... -- npx -y jevwire (note: npm package would be upstream, which lacks OpenRouter; use the fork's plugin/dist/mcp.mjs directly).
security: Key handling: OpenRouter key read from env or plugin userConfig (sensitive). hooks.json passes it as HTTP headers X-Jev-Env-Key-OpenRouter: $OPENROUTER_API_KEY / Authorization Bearer to http://127.0.0.1:10522 on every hook call (allowedEnvVars lists it). Loopback only, timingSafeEqual auth, but a different local user who squats port 10522 first receives payloads AND the key; SECURITY.md admits this and says multi-user hosts unsupported. Fine on a single-user box.

Key is not on argv (configure-openrouter.mjs reads env), but that script writes the plaintext key into ~/.claude/settings.json env (mode 600). The user's no-secret-leak hook does not yet protect OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so the key is also in every Bash child env and readable by the model via env/printenv unless added to the protected list.

Daemon is a detached long-lived node process (control.ts spawn detached+unref, stdout to daemon.log), idle exit 30 min; /v1/health unauthenticated but carries no secret; no shutdown endpoint; keyless install runs unauthenticated.

Prompt-injection surface: Jev answers can be moved by injected text (independent evals). Tripwire is soft: the deny text tells Claude to re-issue with '# jev:intended <reason>' and then it passes without judgment, so a compromised/injected agent can self-override; Claude Code's own permission rules still apply. Stop hook can block once per prompt (a wrong Jev answer just costs one extra turn). Notes are declarative to avoid tripping Claude's injection defenses.

Redaction is best-effort regex (sk-, ghp_, AKIA, Bearer, JWT, key=value, PEM, long hex) applied before send and before local logging; misses unshaped secrets. Sensitive-path predicate (src/util/sensitive-path.ts) blocks .env, keys, .ssh, .aws, .claude/settings*.json for jev_rank/jev_verify file reads, realpath-confined to project root.

No telemetry found in src (grep for telemetry/analytics returned nothing); only outbound is the Jev API plus OpenRouter attribution headers (HTTP-Referer https://github.com/Brainwires/jevwire, X-Title jevwire). Local decision log and session files written to the plugin data dir (deletable, described in SECURITY.md).

Supply chain: committed minified bundles (mcp.mjs 1.5 MB) are what actually run; CI checks they match the source, but the user cannot easily review them; fork owner has 0 stars and 4 commits, so trust anchor is thin. Recommend pinning to a reviewed commit SHA. No installers with curl|sh; no postinstall.
gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.dataEgress: To openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (and onward to TypeSafe as model provider) only when the prefilter decides to judge: tool name plus redacted excerpt of arguments (<=4,000 chars) for Bash/Write/Edit/NotebookEdit/mcp__ calls that are not plainly read-only or in-project edits (in advisory mode: writes outside project, sensitive paths, unrecognized shell commands, MCP tools with unknown effects); last 3 user prompts (<=2,000 chars each) and captured subagent task prompt; Claude's final assistant message (tail 6,000 chars) at every Stop when stop_check=true; the FULL text of every WebFetch/WebSearch/mcp__* tool result in 16,000-char chunks up to 8 chunks (about 128k chars) when screen_results=true (default) - this includes gitnexus and playwright outputs (code snippets, page snapshots) for client projects; file contents only if jev_rank/jev_verify MCP tools are pointed at paths. Regex redaction is best-effort. Also OpenRouter sees the account key and attribution headers. Memoization (5 min) avoids repeated identical calls. For client/NDA projects this is a real third-party (OpenRouter + TypeSafe) egress of code and tool output.
gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.failureMode: Fail-open everywhere: every command hook exits 0 with empty stdout on error; http hooks get 200 {} even on auth failure (never non-2xx), refused connection is a non-blocking error in Claude Code; hook Jev deadline 1.5 s (JEV_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS), hooks.json timeout 5 s (2 s SessionEnd); no key or provider mismatch means judgment hooks inactive and a once-per-session notice; port conflict means hooks inactive for the session. Handlers cannot emit permissionDecision allow (tests/hooks/never-allow.test.ts). The only blocking outputs are the tripwire deny (works in bypassPermissions, one-time, self-overridable via marker) and the Stop block (max once per prompt). MCP tools retry (3 retries, 30 s deadline). Pinned-model retirement would look like silence. If daemon is down, UserPromptSubmit falls back to a node command hook (about 160 ms).
gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.latencyImpact: Prefilter-skipped calls (ls, git status, in-project edits, reads): daemon p50 2.8 ms / p95 8.4 ms per README (measured on macOS, TypeSafe direct, not OpenRouter). Judged calls: p50 about 210 ms warm, about 500 ms first, plus the extra OpenRouter alpha hop on this user's path (Jev p95 about 600 ms); identical judgment repeated in 5 min returns from memo in 5 ms. Hook Jev deadline 1.5 s, hard cap 5 s. Costly spots for this user: PostToolUse screening runs synchronously on every mcp__ result (gitnexus, playwright) and WebFetch/WebSearch, up to 8 chunks each; Stop check adds a call per turn end; PreToolUse also matches every mcp__.* call. Stacks on top of the gitnexus hook (seconds) and no-secret-leak. SessionStart adds about 170-600 ms once per session. Sequential-vs-parallel hook ordering with the user's other hooks is by Claude Code (matching hooks run in parallel), so overhead is roughly max, not sum, per event.
gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.contextCost: MCP: 6 tools. Description/param text I could measure statically is roughly 5-6k chars in describe() strings plus longer tool descriptions and JSON schemas: estimate about 2.5-4k tokens of tool definitions per session (deferred behind ToolSearch in recent Claude Code if tool search is on). Skill: jev-decisions description about 100 tokens always in listing (with skillListingBudgetFraction 0.02 it competes for a tiny budget); SKILL.md body 11.7 KB (about 2.9k tokens) plus references/question-writing.md 3.4 KB only when invoked. Hook-injected text: SessionStart once-per-session note only when unconfigured; [jev] notes at most 5 per prompt (each about 60-100 tokens), typically zero for ordinary work; injection flags and stop-block messages rare; route_prompts is off by default, so no per-prompt line. Six slash commands are disable-model-invocation.
gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.autoInvocation: Yes, without prompting: hooks fire deterministically on prompt submit, gated tool calls, mcp/web results, and Stop, and nothing needs the model to decide to call anything. This is the only candidate style that satisfies 'automatic without saying use jev'. Caveat: hook output is advisory, PreToolUse notes arrive after the call ran, and only the tripwire deny and one Stop block can change behavior. The 6 MCP tools rely on model discretion via the jev-decisions skill (rank-glob-before-read is a genuinely useful nudge but unprompted use is unreliable).
pros: Only candidate that actually delivers automatic, prompt-free use: hooks.json wires SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse (Bash|Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Agent|Task|mcp__.*), PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SessionEnd; deterministic prefilter (src/hooks/prefilter.ts) keeps ls/git status/reads/in-project edits at about 3 ms with zero model calls

OpenRouter is a first-class, explicit provider: src/jev/provider.ts + client.ts:159 POST /api/alpha/decisions with model typesafe/jev-1.13 and Bearer key; explicit provider never silently falls back to TypeSafe; OPENROUTER_BASE_URL override; tests/openrouter.test.ts

Safe failure modes by design: fail-open everywhere, cannot emit permissionDecision allow (never-allow test), never prompts unless ask_on_trip, 1.5 s per-hook deadline, kill switches JEV_HOOKS_DISABLE=1, gate=off, stop_check/screen_results toggles, /jev:off, JEV_DAEMON_DISABLE=1

Tripwire deny works under bypassPermissions where the user has no prompts: hard code rules (rm -rf ~, force push main, DROP TABLE, mkfs, dd of=/dev, chmod -R 777, fork bomb) fire without any model call, so this part has value even with Jev offline; Stop hook catches 'tests pass' claims contradicted by a verification ledger (evidence-based, not only model opinion)

Engineering quality above typical for a 0-star repo: 44 test files incl. http/command hook byte conformance, daemon lock/contention tests, redaction tests, CI with Node 20/22 and bundle freshness check; honest docs (SECURITY.md lists exactly what leaves the machine and the port-squatting residual risk; skill has a 'when not to use it' section); local decision log plus /jev:calibrate to tune thresholds on the user's own data
Cheap per-call cost (about $0.0045 per 108k input tokens reported for jev_rank), tool defs small (6 tools), no per-prompt context injection by default
cons: Broad egress with default settings: screen_results=true sends the full text (up to about 128k chars) of every WebFetch/WebSearch/mcp__* result (gitnexus code, playwright snapshots) to OpenRouter/TypeSafe, and Stop sends the final assistant message every turn; on client projects this is third-party code egress; regex redaction is best-effort. Would need screen_results=false and possibly gate=off/limited matchers for client work

Latency stacking: synchronous PostToolUse on every mcp__ result and PreToolUse on all mcp__.* plus Stop calls, on top of gitnexus (seconds) and no-secret-leak; README latencies are measured on macOS against TypeSafe direct, not OpenRouter alpha

Weak enforcement: notes for PreToolUse arrive after the call already ran; tripwire is answerable by Claude re-issuing with '# jev:intended <reason>' so it is a speed bump not a guard, especially under prompt injection; Jev evals show overconfidence and injection sensitivity. In bypassPermissions the plugin deliberately cannot prompt the user, so value is mainly the 8 regex rules plus Stop nudges

Key exposure surface: OPENROUTER_API_KEY sent as HTTP headers to the loopback daemon on every hook call and becomes visible in the process env; configure-openrouter.mjs writes it plaintext to ~/.claude/settings.json; user's no-secret-leak hook does not yet cover OPENROUTER_API_KEY; loopback port squat by another local user leaks payloads and key (fine on single-user machine)

Provenance risk: the OpenRouter support lives only in a 0-star personal fork (wesleydionisio) that is 4 commits ahead of Brainwires 0.6.0 and now behind upstream 0.6.3 (which lacks provider.ts); 12 days old, no releases/tags, runs 1.7 MB of committed minified bundles; OpenRouter Decisions API is alpha with no SLA; fixed port 10522 (hardcoded in hook URLs) and a resident daemon; MCP tools rely on model discretion (skill only) so unprompted use of rank/verify is unreliable

Overlap and noise with the user's existing setup: Stop hook can force an extra turn on a false positive; PreToolUse matcher on Agent|Task and mcp__.* adds hook invocations for every subagent spawn and every gitnexus/playwright call; the user's caveman UserPromptSubmit and plannotator hooks are independent but /jev commands run through Bash (sandbox loopback quirk documented)
gh-wesleydionisio-jevwire.verdict: The strongest fit for an automatic, OpenRouter-hosted Jev: real hook coverage, explicit OpenRouter provider, fail-open and never-allow by design, and unusually good tests and honest docs. Adopt only pinned to a reviewed commit and with screen_results off (or matchers narrowed) and OPENROUTER_API_KEY added to the secret-leak list, because default egress of MCP/web results and the fork-only, alpha, 0-star provenance are the real risks.

gh-okooo5km-jev.name: okooo5km/jev
gh-okooo5km-jev.whatItDoes: Unofficial single-file stdlib-Python CLI (jev/scripts/jev, ~2170 lines) plus an Agent Skill (SKILL.md) for TypeSafe Jev. Verbs: yes (Noul), pick (Choice), score, filter (semantic grep per line), run SPEC (multi-question specs: mail, feedback, signal, commit, route), raw, auth, provider. Talks to TypeSafe api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone by default or OpenRouter /api/alpha/decisions. Not an MCP server, not a hook. Meant to be invoked by the model via Bash when SKILL.md description matches. Built-in specs are in Chinese. No PermissionRequest hook recipe is shipped.

providerSupport.evidence: jev/scripts/jev:56-73 PROVIDERS table. typesafe: base_url https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, key env TYPESAFE_API_KEY, default model jev-latest. openrouter: base_url https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions, key env OPENROUTER_API_KEY, key check URL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key, default model ~typesafe/jev-latest, key_prefix sk-or-, headers X-Title and HTTP-Referer. Model normalization at :295-330 maps to typesafe/jev-1.13 for OpenRouter. Payload is {model,state,questions} (:723-724). Provider order: --provider, then JEV_PROVIDER, then pinned default in config.ini, then auto (TypeSafe key if present, else OpenRouter, :248-283). JEV_BASE_URL overrides the URL (:342-343).
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Already native. Setting JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter (or removing any TYPESAFE_API_KEY and providing only OPENROUTER_API_KEY) is sufficient. No patching needed.
