security: Key handling is good. The key is read from env, then $JEV_ENV_FILE, then ~/.config/jev/.env (jev:196-228), and sent only as an Authorization Bearer header (:350-351). It is never taken from argv. `auth set` needs a TTY with hidden input and writes 0600 via O_EXCL and chmod (:1582-1617). SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent never to read or print key files or pass keys as args.
`auth set --stdin` exists, so a key could be piped in. SKILL.md forbids the agent from doing so, but that is only an instruction.
JEV_DEBUG=1 prints the full request payload (state) to stderr (:697-701). The Authorization header is not printed in the code I read, but not exhaustively verified.
No subprocess, os.system, eval or exec found in the CLI (grep returned nothing). Pure stdlib http.client and urllib. Proxy support exists (test_proxy.py).
No telemetry. Only static X-Title: jev-cli and HTTP-Referer github header on OpenRouter calls, which is OpenRouter's normal app attribution.

Installer is decent: version regex check, refuses symlinked home, sha256 verify before extract, atomic swap, main() wrapper against truncation. The checksum comes from the same release host, so it guards integrity but not a compromised repo. The user does not need the installer: the single file can be read and copied.

Prompt-injection surface: the state text (diffs, logs, files) goes to the model, and injected instructions in state can shift verdicts (per the brief). If used as a gate, an attacker-controlled diff or command can talk its way past. Pin an OpenRouter key with a low spend limit.

Supply chain: a solo maintainer, 12 commits in 2 days, 1 fork, 11 stars, created 2026-09-18. The Bash-invoked script would run with the user's full env, so read and vendor it rather than auto-updating.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not yet in the user's no-secret-leak.cjs protected list, so add it before storing the key in env or a .env file.
gh-okooo5km-jev.dataEgress: The state text, the question text and criteria, and the model name go to openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions, plus the Bearer key and a static User-Agent/X-Title/Referer. For filter and -l, every input line is sent, and one request is made per line. For `jev run commit`, `git diff --cached` content leaves the machine, which matters for client code. The CLI does no redaction beyond a SIZE_WARN_TOKENS=30000 warning. OpenRouter's own logging and provider policies apply.
gh-okooo5km-jev.failureMode: Not a hook, so it fails per call. A network error or HTTP 4xx/5xx gives exit code 2 with a message on stderr after retries with backoff on 429/5xx (default --retries and --timeout 60 s, jev:2020 and 2067). Exit 1 means a legitimate "no", so a naive script that treats non-zero as "no" conflates error with no. The caller must distinguish 2 from 1. The default 60 s timeout with retries is far too long for a hook, and a hook would need --timeout 3 --retries 0. If used inside a PermissionRequest hook wrapper, fail-open-to-prompt has to be written by the user. The alpha endpoint may move (SKILL.md acknowledges this, and JEV_BASE_URL is the escape hatch).
gh-okooo5km-jev.contextCost: Low. One skill. The frontmatter description is about 1.2k chars (~300 tokens) and is always in the listing, which is noticeable with skillListingBudgetFraction 0.02 (may get truncated). The body is 9.1k chars (~2.3k tokens), loaded when triggered, and references/cli.md (~24k chars, ~6k tokens) only if read. Zero MCP tools and zero hook-injected text.
gh-okooo5km-jev.autoInvocation: Skill description trigger only, at model discretion. It fires when the model reads a task as classify/triage/route/filter. Opus will rarely reach for a Jev call in ordinary coding, so it is not reliably "automatic". No hooks, no PermissionRequest recipe, no CLAUDE.md snippet. The user would have to write his own hook or CLAUDE.md rule that shells out to `jev yes` or `jev run`. Use for hooks: `JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter /abs/path/jev yes "..." --timeout 3 --retries 0 --json`.
pros: OpenRouter is a first-class provider in code (jev:65-73), with correct model normalization to typesafe/jev-1.13 and ~typesafe/jev-latest, and the request body matches the alpha/decisions schema. It works with only OPENROUTER_API_KEY, with no changes.

Well-engineered key handling for this user: keys stay out of argv, files are written 0600, and there is a status/check command that never prints a key. That suits a setup with a fail-closed secret hook.
Zero dependencies (stdlib only, Python 3.9+), a single readable 2.1k-line file with no subprocess or eval, and no telemetry. It is easy to audit and vendor, so it can be used without the installer.

Substantial test suite: about 190 test functions across 15 files (test_providers 52, test_auth 29, test_provider_admin 31), a mock server, and CI on Python 3.9/3.11/3.13 on Linux and macOS with pinned action SHAs and shellcheck.
Useful primitives for shell pipelines: filter as a semantic grep, -l batch with concurrency, --json output, and exit codes usable in shell tests. It also handles retry/backoff and connection reuse.
Ships a `commit` spec (type, secret leak, breaking change, risk) and a `route` spec that map onto real dev workflows. Users can add JSON specs in ~/.config/jev/specs.
Low context cost (no MCP tool defs, one skill) and the Apache-2.0 license.
cons: It is not automatic. It is a skill plus CLI with no hooks, and it provides no PermissionRequest hook (the official cookbook pattern), Stop hook or CLAUDE.md snippet. Reaching the user's goal (Claude Code uses it without being told) requires writing the hook glue himself, so this is a building block, not the integration.

Auto-invocation depends on Opus choosing the skill from the description. That description is long (~1.2k chars), partly Chinese, and aimed at classify/triage/email/feedback, not coding, and it may be truncated at a 0.02 skill listing budget.
Default provider is TypeSafe. With both keys present, auto picks TypeSafe (jev:274-279). The user must pin openrouter (JEV_PROVIDER or `jev provider default openrouter`).
Default 60 s timeout and retries make it unsuitable for a hook as-is. Exit code 1 (no) versus 2 (error) must be handled carefully in glue code.
Built-in specs and error messages are in Chinese, and the main README is Chinese (an English README.en.md exists). Spec instructions must be rewritten for an English coding context.
Very new and low-adoption: created 2026-09-18, 12 commits by a single author, 11 stars, 1 fork, and it is unofficial. It depends on an alpha endpoint that may move.
Data egress of diffs and commands to a third party. `jev run commit` sends the staged diff, which is a concern for client repos. No redaction is offered.
Jev calibration and prompt-injection weaknesses apply unchanged, and the CLI adds no mitigation.
gh-okooo5km-jev.verdict: A well-built, OpenRouter-native, auditable CLI, and the best ready-made client available for shell-level Jev calls. It is only a building block: it ships no hook or automatic trigger, so the user would still write PermissionRequest/PreToolUse glue (calling it with JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter, --timeout 3 --retries 0) and adapt the Chinese specs. Vendor the single file instead of running the installer.

gh-stas4000-claude-subagent-router.name: stas4000/claude-subagent-router
gh-stas4000-claude-subagent-router.whatItDoes: A PreToolUse hook on the Agent tool (router/hook.py). For builder briefs, router/pick.py sends the description plus the first 1000 chars of the brief and long routing instructions to a Jev System One Choice question (3 options: s55-builder, s55-builder-deep, o55-builder-precise). It takes the top probability and rewrites updatedInput.subagent_type. If the key is unset or the call fails, a regex keyword picker answers instead. router/guard.py denies any Sonnet agent whose file lacks a valid effort, or that has effort max. The hook also forces run_in_background to false and logs each pick to .router/picks.jsonl. It ships 6 agent files, a verifier_guard hook and a report script. It is a sub-agent model router, not a permission or general decision helper.

providerSupport.evidence: router/pick.py:36 DEFAULT_URL=https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone; :37 DEFAULT_MODEL=jev-latest; :144 reads JEV_API_KEY; :147-149 JEV_URL must start with https; :150-153 body is {model,state:{context},questions:{decision:{type:choice,instructions,criteria}}}; :160-163 reads out.answers.decision.probabilities; :164-166 reads usage.input_tokens and usage.cost. The wire format is TypeSafe's own schema, so it should match OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Trivial with no code change: JEV_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone, JEV_MODEL=jev-1.13, and JEV_API_KEY set to the OpenRouter key. The variable name is Jev-specific, so the OpenRouter key would have to be aliased or duplicated into JEV_API_KEY, and it is not auto-read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY. The default model 'jev-latest' is unverified on OpenRouter. The OpenRouter response (answers/probabilities/usage.cost) was not checked against the parser. It does not use /alpha/decisions.
providerSupport.others: No other providers. It is Jev only, with a local regex fallback.

gh-stas4000-claude-subagent-router.runtime: Python 3.10+, stdlib only (urllib). No MCP server, no plugin.json, no installer. Install is manual copy plus a settings merge.
gh-stas4000-claude-subagent-router.tests: 83 unittest test functions across 5 files (pick 32, hook 21, guard 16, report 8, verifier_guard 6). The README says the network is mocked in every test. Not executed by me. Well organised, but the repo is about 1 day old.
security: Key handling is good. It travels only in an Authorization header (never argv), only to an https URL, and redirects are blocked (pick.py:115-120). Errors redact the key (pick.py:281-283).
No subprocess, eval or exec anywhere in router/. The only file I/O is reading /proc, reading agent files and appending the ledger with mode 0600.
No telemetry beyond the Jev call. The default host is api.typesafe.ai, and JEV_URL can be any https host, so a poisoned environment could redirect the key.

Prompt-injection surface: the brief text (up to 1000 chars) goes into Jev state, and Jev is known to be steerable by injected state. The worst outcome is a downgrade of a builder from Opus to Sonnet. The guard still enforces Sonnet effort, and the tool permissions of the picked agent still apply.

Hook 'allow' decisions carry updatedInput, and a PreToolUse allow can bypass the normal permission prompt for that Agent call. This is low impact for Agent, but it is a behaviour change to be aware of.

The guard is not scoped to this repo's agents. Any Agent call with a model override containing 'sonnet' and no matching agent file is DENIED (guard.py:73-78). That can break built-in agents such as Explore or general-purpose that the user runs with model:sonnet.
The hook forces run_in_background=false on all Agent calls that request background (hook.py:71-74), silently changing the user's workflow unless ROUTER_FOREGROUND=0.

The ledger .router/picks.jsonl is written under CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. In client repos this creates an untracked directory that could be committed by accident, because only this repo's .gitignore ignores it. It holds the description, not the brief.
The hook does not read or touch OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and needs JEV_API_KEY. It does not conflict with no-secret-leak.cjs, but that protected-vars list would need JEV_API_KEY added.
gh-stas4000-claude-subagent-router.dataEgress: Per builder-agent call only: the Agent call's description (200 chars) and the brief text with whitespace collapsed, truncated to 1000 chars, plus a fixed routing-instructions text (~2.5k chars). All of it goes to the Jev endpoint (api.typesafe.ai by default, or whichever JEV_URL points to). The bearer key is sent only to that URL. Briefs written by the lead can quote client code, paths or business details, so client projects need review. Non-builder Agent calls send nothing. Nothing else leaves the machine, and without JEV_API_KEY nothing leaves at all.
gh-stas4000-claude-subagent-router.failureMode: Fail-safe. Any Jev error, timeout (12 s cap enforced by a daemon thread, with a 30 s hook timeout) or unparseable answer falls back to the regex picker, and if that fails the lead's pick stands. Malformed stdin or an exception exits 0 with no output. The one deliberate fail-closed path is the guard: a Sonnet agent without a valid effort, or a Sonnet model override without an agent file, is denied. Worst-case added latency is about 12 s per builder Agent call when Jev hangs. The docs claim a 0.44 s median.
gh-stas4000-claude-subagent-router.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no injected hook text. The cost is in the six agents, which add roughly 3k chars of description each to the Task/Agent tool listing (about 2-3k tokens in total). The README's suggested CLAUDE.md paragraph is small. The rewritten subagent choice is invisible to the model apart from the permissionDecisionReason string.
gh-stas4000-claude-subagent-router.latencyImpact: The hook only does work on Agent calls, which are rare, and only calls Jev for the 4 builder names. Python startup is about 30-50 ms. A Jev call takes about 0.3-0.6 s normally (p95 about 600 ms), and the worst case is 12 s. It never touches Bash, Read or Grep, so it does not stack with gitnexus or no-secret-leak.
gh-stas4000-claude-subagent-router.autoInvocation: Truly deterministic for the events it hooks: a PreToolUse hook on the Agent tool with no model discretion. But it only fires on Agent calls that name its s55-/o55- builder agents. The user has none of these, so they would have to adopt the agent set and add CLAUDE.md instructions telling the lead to use them. It does not cover Bash permissions, planning, commit checks or anything else.
pros: Well-engineered hook: stdlib only, no subprocess/eval, key never in argv, redirects blocked, errors redact the key (pick.py:115-120, 281-283).
Real automatic invocation through a PreToolUse Agent hook, with two fallbacks (regex picker, then the lead's pick) and a 12 s deadline that runs on a daemon thread.

Uses Jev the right way: one Choice question with probabilities and no free text. The system-one request shape (model/state/questions) is close to what OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone should accept, so JEV_URL/JEV_MODEL/JEV_API_KEY can point it at OpenRouter without code edits.
83 test functions, a pick ledger with cost accounting and a report CLI. MIT license. The author reports live data (92 picks, 0.44 s median, about $0.00004 a pick).
Model ids (claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5) and the effort frontmatter match the user's Claude Code version.
cons: Narrow value for this user. It only routes between Sonnet and Opus builder sub-agents, and the user runs Opus 5.5 main on a subscription, where cost savings matter less. Routing quality is only 0.71 on the author's private held-out briefs, and the routing prompt encodes the author's own domain rules (messaging engines, voice/earpiece, a 'brain') that will not fit this user's projects.

Requires adopting its own six agents plus CLAUDE.md wording. Nothing fires unless the lead uses the s55-/o55- builder names, and the regex fallback and the INSTRUCTIONS are tuned to the author's projects.

Intrusive side effects: it forces every background Agent call to the foreground (unless ROUTER_FOREGROUND=0). It also denies any Agent call with a 'sonnet' model override and no agent file, which could break built-in agents.

Not OpenRouter-native: it needs JEV_API_KEY, the default host is api.typesafe.ai and the default model 'jev-latest' is unverified on OpenRouter. It targets neither /alpha/decisions nor OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and the user would need to duplicate the key into the hook's environment and extend no-secret-leak.
Ships briefs (first 1000 chars) to a third party, a data egress risk for client projects, and writes a .router/ ledger into each project.
Brand new: 4 commits, 1 contributor, 7 stars, created on 2026-09-29, no release or plugin/marketplace packaging (manual copy and manual settings merge).
gh-stas4000-claude-subagent-router.verdict: The code is clean and safe-failing, and it is one of the few real automatic Jev hooks. It solves a narrow problem (Sonnet vs Opus builder routing), needs a wholesale adoption of its agents and conventions, and has intrusive side effects (forced foreground, Sonnet-override denials). It is switchable to OpenRouter only by env overrides. Treat it as a reference implementation of the pattern (a PreToolUse Agent hook with a Jev Choice question, an offline fallback and a deadline), not something to install as-is.

gh-nodardavituri-fast-compact.name: fast-compact (nodardavituri)
gh-nodardavituri-fast-compact.whatItDoes: Claude Code function-hooks plugin (TypeScript, no deps) registering /fc and /fast-compact. On invocation it schedules the built-in /compact with a "[fast-compact] <focus>" marker (hooks/fast-compact.ts:88,155-160) and answers that compaction from a session.compact hook. The hook plans which old tool outputs (>~1950 chars, older than the newest 10 calls) to cut, asks Jev one Noul question per output ("will the assistant need something from this again?") via POST to /api/v1/systemone, keeps the top-ranked ones whole (max 25% of old chars, score >= 0.45), and cuts the rest to 1000 head + 500 tail chars. Full originals are saved first to ~/.claude/fast-compact/<session>/ and the cut is then applied. Long old tool inputs and host notices are also trimmed. No tool call is ever deleted. It does not touch built-in /compact or auto-compaction (session.compact only acts on marker-prefixed manual/plugin triggers, hooks/fast-compact.ts:176-178).

providerSupport.evidence: src/jev.ts:13-16 ENDPOINTS = {openrouter: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone, typesafe: https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone}; provider default openrouter (hooks/fast-compact.ts:38); key from plugin option apiKey, else $.env OPENROUTER_API_KEY / TYPESAFE_API_KEY, else settings.json env block (hooks/fast-compact.ts:191-203); baseUrl option overrides (line 42); Bearer auth (src/jev.ts:167). Request body {model, state, questions}, answers parsed from answers[name].noul, usage.cost (src/jev.ts:57-144). Bench RESULTS.md reports real runs of typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917 through it (618 requests, $0.665), so the OpenRouter path was exercised by the author. Caveat: default model string is 'jev-latest' (src/jev.ts:18), not the 'jev-1.13' in the brief; it is user-configurable via the model option, but I could not verify OpenRouter accepts 'jev-latest'. It is not the /api/alpha/decisions endpoint.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Already native: OpenRouter is the default; nothing to patch. Set model to jev-1.13 in pluginConfigs if jev-latest is rejected.
providerSupport.others: TypeSafe direct (api.typesafe.ai) supported, but the README notes TypeSafe's web firewall returns HTML 403 on many real sessions.

interface.name: /fc and /fast-compact [focus]
interface.purpose: Slash commands registered on session.start via $.command.register (hooks/fast-compact.ts:128-141); the command.run handler schedules the built-in /compact with the marker and returns 'compacting…' (lines 147-170). Manual only.

interface.name: hook session.compact
interface.purpose: Intercepts compactions with trigger manual/plugin, no agentId and instructions starting with '[fast-compact]'; everything else is passed to next(e) untouched (lines 172-178). Returns {messages} or {skip}. A .catch returns {skip} so a failure never falls to the built-in summary (lines 301-308).

interface.name: hook command.run
interface.purpose: Handles fc/fast-compact; refuses a second run within 120 s while one is pending.

interface.name: hooks/hooks.json
interface.purpose: Only {"modules":["./fast-compact.ts"]}: a function-hooks module. Not a shell-command hook, no matcher.

interface.name: userConfig options
interface.purpose: provider, apiKey (sensitive), baseUrl, model, keepRecentCalls=10, cutTo=1500, keepWhole=0.25, minKeepScore=0.45, cutInputs, sendSamples, resumeSafe (.claude-plugin/plugin.json).

interface.name: MCP tools / skills
interface.purpose: None. No .mcp.json, no SKILL.md, no MCP server.

interface.name: bench/ (bun bench/run.ts --jev)
interface.purpose: Offline replay benchmark over local transcripts; dev-only, not part of the plugin runtime.

security: No shell exec, child_process, eval or process.env use anywhere in src/ or hooks/ (grep clean); runs in Claude Code's sandboxed function-hook environment using $.http, $.fs, $.env, $.settings.

Key handling: Bearer key in an HTTPS header via host $.http.fetch, never argv. But the hook can read arbitrary env by literal name and reads the whole settings.json (`$.settings.read()['env']`, hooks/fast-compact.ts:199) to find the key; it only extracts OPENROUTER_API_KEY / TYPESAFE_API_KEY. The plugin apiKey option is marked sensitive (stored by Claude Code securely).

Secret masking (src/redact.ts) is regex-only (sk-/ghp_/AKIA/JWT/Bearer/PEM/NAME=value URLs). The author calls it a safety net, not a guarantee. It would miss free-form secrets, client-confidential source, or business data.

Prompt-injection surface: tool outputs (samples of first 200 + last 100 chars, plus one-line notes) and conversation text go into Jev's state. The injection could only shift Noul scores, i.e. change which outputs stay whole. Impact is bounded to what is cut or kept, because the full text is archived and Claude is told where to read it. It is not a tool-execution vector.

Unsalted local archive: full cut outputs (which may contain secrets that the redactor did not mask) are written in plaintext to ~/.claude/fast-compact/<session>/ with no auto-cleanup. File names are sanitised to [A-Za-z0-9._-] (hooks/fast-compact.ts:243).
Hidden effect: resumeSafe (default on) drops hidden reasoning and image-only messages. Unknown behavior on CC 2.1.285 because it was built and tested on 2.1.283 against an early-access API.
No telemetry beyond the Jev call; a local ledger jsonl with sizes/cost is written monthly. Nothing to the author.

Repo is 1 day old, 5 stars, 0 forks, no release. Contributors are Nodar Davituri, 'tamara tran', and 'Devin AI'; much of the code is adapted from tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction, MIT. No installer scripts, and the install is the standard claude plugin marketplace add.
gh-nodardavituri-fast-compact.dataEgress: On each /fc run only, to openrouter.ai (or api.typesafe.ai): the user's and Claude's messages (long ones abridged to ~400 head + 150 tail chars), shortened tool inputs, a one-line note per tool output, and with sendSamples (default true) the first 200 + last 100 chars of each output being ranked, plus a 'goal' (last user request) and optional focus. Regex-masked for credentials first (src/redact.ts). State is bounded around 32k tokens (src/jev.ts:21). Nothing is sent unless the user types /fc, and nothing is sent when there is no key. Client-project code and conversation snippets would go to OpenRouter and TypeSafe, which matters for client work. No data goes to the author.
gh-nodardavituri-fast-compact.failureMode: Fail-safe, and better than most: Jev timeout is 6 s per request and is capped by the hook's 10 s budget minus a 2.5 s reserve (hooks/fast-compact.ts:101-104,210-211). 2 retries with backoff on 429/5xx/transport (src/jev.ts:158,172,196). Any Jev error or missing key falls back to keeping the newest outputs whole (decide() catches; jevSkipped is reported). Any hook exception returns {skip}, so it never triggers the slow built-in summary. If the archive write fails, that item is not cut. Because it acts only on its own marker, a plugin failure cannot affect normal /compact or auto-compaction. A risk: the function-hooks module load failure is silent in the TUI (CLAUDE.md), and the feature is early-access.
gh-nodardavituri-fast-compact.latencyImpact: None on normal tool calls or turns, since it is not a PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook. Only when /fc is typed: about 0.6 s and $0.0002 per run in the README example, up to about 6-7.5 s worst case before falling back to keeping the newest outputs.
gh-nodardavituri-fast-compact.contextCost: Very low. No MCP server and no tool definitions, no SKILL.md, so the skill listing budget is unaffected, and no hook-injected additionalContext. It adds two slash-command descriptions (about 60 tokens). It only reduces context when run: the example shows 103k to 81k chars (-21%), and cut markers of about 200 chars replace the middles. The compaction leaves a '/compact [fast-compact]' line in the transcript.
gh-nodardavituri-fast-compact.autoInvocation: Manual only. The user must type /fc; nothing triggers it on context thresholds. The design (marker-based /compact scheduling) exists specifically to leave built-in auto-compaction alone. It does not meet the user's 'automatic use' goal. Making it automatic would need a separate mechanism, e.g. a Stop/UserPromptSubmit hook that nags to run /fc, or a fork that hooks the auto trigger, and the code deliberately passes auto triggers through (hooks/fast-compact.ts:174-178).
pros: OpenRouter is the native default provider (src/jev.ts:14, hooks/fast-compact.ts:38), with the key read from env, plugin option or the settings.json env block. No patching is needed, and a key held in the settings env block works.

Safest failure design of any Jev integration seen: 6 s cap, retries, fallback to newest-kept, and {skip} on any error. It never falls to the slow summary and never touches built-in /compact or auto-compact.

Non-destructive: every cut is written to disk first, with a marker telling Claude the path, tool calls are never deleted, and an item whose archive write fails is left uncut. Directly fixes the failure mode of the upstream fast-jev-compaction project.
Zero context cost, with no MCP tools, no skill or hook injected text, and no per-tool-call latency. It suits the user's low skillListingBudget.

Real evidence: a 122-moment, 59-session replay bench (bench/RESULTS.md) with CIs, with per-run cost reporting; 4 test files (core spec plus plugin host tests, about 48 tests); credential-shaped strings are masked before send.
cons: Manual only (/fc), so it violates the requirement that Claude Code uses Jev automatically without being told. Auto-compaction is deliberately not intercepted, and the user gets no benefit on the long unattended auto/bypass sessions where compaction actually happens.

Depends on an early-access, undocumented function-hooks API (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1, tested only on CC 2.1.283, user on 2.1.285). Silent load failure, and it runs the built-in /compact with a marker as a hack (README Limits). It may break on any update.

Marginal measured value: bench shows Jev-keeps-whole 75% needed-usable vs 73% for just keeping the newest and 69% for head_tail at the same size. Jev adds only about 2 points over a no-Jev rule, which is within the confidence intervals (RESULTS.md), and only 48% of history is cuttable. Author says the measurements come from one person's sessions.

Sends conversation text and 300-char output samples to OpenRouter and TypeSafe on each run, with only regex masking, which is a concern for client projects. The full-text archive holds unmasked outputs in plaintext under ~/.claude/fast-compact/ indefinitely. OPENROUTER_API_KEY would need to be added to the settings.json env block (and to no-secret-leak.cjs protected vars), and the hook itself reads settings.json env.

Very young and unproven: created 2026-09-26, 5 stars, no release, 37 commits (shared with a forked history), and a 'Devin AI' co-author. The default model 'jev-latest' is unverified against OpenRouter; use 'jev-1.13'. It only shrinks tool output and does not summarise the conversation, so it complements rather than replaces /compact, and resumeSafe drops thinking blocks and image-only messages.
gh-nodardavituri-fast-compact.verdict: Well engineered, safe on failure, and OpenRouter-native, but it is a manual /fc command built on an early-access function-hooks API, and its measured benefit over a simple keep-the-newest rule is only about 2 points. It fails the user's core 'automatic, never prompt' requirement, so it is a niche optional tool rather than a daily integration. Try it only if manual pruning of tool output is wanted, and set model=jev-1.13.

pypi-org-project-jev-judge-mcp.name: jev-judge-mcp (PyPI) / PyModel/jev-judge-mcp
pypi-org-project-jev-judge-mcp.whatItDoes: Unofficial-looking Python rewrite (behavior-compatible with a frozen TypeSafe TS reference server, ADR-0001) of a Jev MCP server: stdio MCP server with 11 typed judgment tools (verify, gate, review, screen, compare, find, rerank, classify, decide, extract, score) that wrap Jev Decisions API calls and map probabilities to auto/review/escalate via local policy. Also ships two opt-in CLI hooks: `jev-judge-mcp hook gate` (PreToolUse Bash|Write|Edit, can only deny/ask, never allow) and `completion-hook` (PreToolUse Bash, only git push / gh pr create / gh pr merge), plus an installer, setup/doctor commands, and two packaged skills exposed as MCP resources.

providerSupport.evidence: src/jev_judge_mcp/providers/openrouter.py:18 URL = https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions; :25-28 slug jev-latest -> typesafe/jev-1.13; :50-56 Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY plus HTTP-Referer/X-Title headers. resolver.py:63-64,77-82,105-106: JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter or auto (needs sk-or- prefix key); order typesafe, openrouter, cloudflare, compatible. settings.py:31 OPENROUTER_API_KEY. typesafe.py uses typesafe-sdk (optional extra). It does NOT use /api/v1/systemone. Gotcha: a key file at ~/.config/jev-mcp/key (keyfile.py, resolver.py:49) counts as a TypeSafe key and wins under auto, so set JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter explicitly.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Nothing to patch: OpenRouter is a first-class provider. Hand-register the MCP entry with env {JEV_PROVIDER: openrouter, OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}} and no [typesafe] extra needed (server.py:153-167 only demands the SDK when typesafe is selected). The installer only writes a TYPESAFE_API_KEY reference (install/launch.py claude_code_entry), so its Claude Code entry must be edited by hand. Model slug is pinned to jev-1.13 for jev-latest; override with JEV_MCP_MODEL.
providerSupport.others: cloudflare (token + account id), compatible (JEV_API_KEY + JEV_API_BASE_URL, generic base URL), vercel explicitly unsupported.

interface.name: jev_verify (MCP)
interface.purpose: claims vs evidence -> verified/contradicted/unsupported per claim with action; no length cap

interface.name: jev_gate (MCP)
interface.purpose: request + diff + claims + evidence + test log in one call -> auto/review/escalate; caps 16 claims, 200k evidence units

interface.name: jev_review (MCP)
interface.purpose: diff vs request scores: correctness, spec match, test gap, blast radius, safe_to_apply

interface.name: jev_screen (MCP)
interface.purpose: screen fetched/pasted text for prompt injection and relevance -> pass/review/block/skip

interface.name: jev_compare (MCP)
interface.purpose: two passages same_fact/contradicts/different_facts, up to 10 aspects (docs vs code drift)

interface.name: jev_find (MCP)
interface.purpose: pick best of <=250 candidates or none

interface.name: jev_rerank (MCP)
interface.purpose: relevance score for every candidate, full ordering

interface.name: jev_classify (MCP)
interface.purpose: bucket <=64 items into <=250 classes

interface.name: jev_decide (MCP)
interface.purpose: one bounded choice among 2-6 options with ask_user/investigate/none escapes

interface.name: jev_extract (MCP)
interface.purpose: caller regex proposes candidates, Jev picks, value returned verbatim; regex runs in a worker subprocess

interface.name: jev_score (MCP)
interface.purpose: grade on caller-supplied ordered 2-10 level rubric (extension tool beyond the frozen ten)

interface.name: MCP resources/prompts jev-skill://jev-mcp/SKILL.md and jev-skill://jev/SKILL.md
interface.purpose: routing skill for the tools, and a cookbook skill for building apps on the Jev API; only read on demand

interface.name: jev-judge-mcp hook gate (PreToolUse command hook)
interface.purpose: opt-in; stdin hook event -> one Choice question allow/deny; prints only deny or ask JSON, never allow; thresholds 0.5 reported / 0.4 margin; 30 s provider timeout; JEV_GATE_STATE adds extra state; JEV_HOOK_REQUIRED=1 makes pre-call failures ask

interface.name: jev-judge-mcp completion-hook (PreToolUse Bash command hook)
interface.purpose: opt-in; only for git push / gh pr create / gh pr merge (cli.py:513-524); runs jev_gate on JEV_COMPLETION_DIFF (default HEAD) with claims/tests files from JEV_COMPLETION_CLAIMS / JEV_COMPLETION_TESTS; silently abstains when those env vars are unset; asks unless gate returns auto

interface.name: jev-judge-mcp setup / install / doctor
interface.purpose: verify+store key (0600 file), write MCP entries into ~/.claude.json and other agents (asks first, --dry-run, --remove), offline config check

interface.name: jev-judge-mcp judge <tool> / gate --diff --claims --tests / calibrate
interface.purpose: CLI one-shots of the tools from stdin JSON, git-diff-based gate (refuses paths outside repo and the key file), offline threshold calibration

For this user: hand-add to ~/.claude.json mcpServers a stdio entry with command absolute uvx, args [--python, >=3.12, --from, jev-judge-mcp==0.7.0, jev-judge-mcp], env {JEV_PROVIDER: openrouter, OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}}; hooks need an absolute path to a persistent `jev-judge-mcp` executable (e.g. `uv tool install`), not uvx per call. Installer does not write allow-rules or hooks (docs/harness/claude.md); README's agent prompt has the agent edit its own CLAUDE.md.
security: Key handling: env only (settings.py:70 returns env_settings only, no .env read); `setup` never takes the key on argv (hidden prompt or env), stored at ~/.config/jev-mcp/key mode 0600 in 0700 dir (keyfile.py, fsutil atomic write); all SecretStr fields feed a log/error redactor (ADR-0017); installer writes ${TYPESAFE_API_KEY} reference, not literal, for Claude Code. No argv exposure of the key found in launch args.

Outbound network only to the selected provider; redirects same-origin only (ADR-0023, base.py:378 follow_redirects with origin hook). No telemetry egress: telemetry.py is in-process spans/metrics to stderr; payload text only with JEV_MCP_TELEMETRY_PAYLOADS=1. grep found no urllib/requests/os.system; subprocess only for `git rev-parse/diff` (cli.py, fixed argv, range validated), `uvx --version`, installer verify handshake, and the extract regex worker.

jev_extract executes caller-supplied regexes in a sandboxed subprocess worker using pickle over its own pipe (extract/worker.py:63, noqa S301 'our parent'); parent-only channel, low risk, but pickle.loads of the pipe is present.

Prompt-injection surface: tool state is raw evidence (diffs, fetched pages) sent to Jev; project's own SKILL.md concedes jev-1.13 does not treat state as hostile and injected instructions can move answers. jev_screen is itself a Jev judgment on untrusted text, so it can be fooled by the text it screens. Hook gate sends the model-proposed command as judged state, so an attacker-influenced command string can argue for 'allow' (harmless since hook can only deny/ask).

Supply chain: launching via uvx pulls PyPI package at first run; version pinned by installer (ADR-0051) but tarball is 1.3 MB with large eval fixtures. gh-ingebyd-fast-jev-compaction-openroute.name: ingebyd/fast-jev-compaction-openrouter
gh-ingebyd-fast-jev-compaction-openroute.whatItDoes: Claude Code plugin (early-access "function hooks" module, plus npm library) that hooks session.compact. It sends the whole stripped transcript to Jev on OpenRouter with two Noul questions per non-pinned tool call (keep call, keep result verbatim). Tool calls and results Jev scores below 0.5 are dropped or truncated to a 300-char head. User and assistant text stays verbatim. If the reduction is under 25% or anything fails, it falls back to the built-in summary. A turn.complete hook also triggers /compact-equivalent at 60% context.

providerSupport.evidence: OpenRouter-only by design: src/request.ts:2 OPENROUTER_DECISIONS_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions; :3 DEFAULT_MODEL='~typesafe/jev-latest'; :54 PRIVACY_PROVIDER={zdr:true,data_collection:'deny'} sent in the body at :82; Bearer auth at :77; key from process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY (src/client.ts:23) or $.env/$.settings env (hooks/fast-jev.ts:227-243). Body shape {model, provider, state, questions:{name:{type:'noul',instructions}}} matches the alpha decisions format. The TypeSafe endpoint was removed in the fork (commit 7390eb0). baseUrl is overridable in the library (client.ts:74) but not in the hook.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Already native. Only quirk is that the endpoint is the /alpha path and the model alias '~typesafe/jev-latest' (userConfig 'model' can pin typesafe/jev-1.13).

interface.name: hook session.compact (hooks/fast-jev.ts:263)
interface.purpose: Runs Jev-guided pruning over event.messages via $.http.fetch. Returns {messages} without a summary, or next(event) to fall back to the built-in summary on error, key missing, or reduction below minReductionRatio.

interface.name: hook turn.complete (hooks/fast-jev.ts:292)
interface.purpose: After each turn, if $.session.usage().context.percent >= compactAtPercent (default 60), calls $.session.compact(), guarded by an in-flight flag.

interface.name: npm lib compactMessages/compact/JevClient/buildJevRequest/parseJevResponse (src/index.ts)
interface.purpose: Library API for tool-call compaction. Not published under this fork's name, and irrelevant to Claude Code use.

interface.name: plugin userConfig (.claude-plugin/plugin.json)
interface.purpose: apiKey (sensitive), keepThreshold 0.5, preserveRecentMessages 6, compactAtPercent 60, minReductionRatio 0.25, maxStateTokens 25000, maxRequestTokens 30000, truncateHeadChars 300, model. hooks/hooks.json is just {"modules":["./fast-jev.ts"]}. No MCP server, skills or CLI commands.

security: No shell exec, no child_process, no installers or install scripts, and no telemetry in src/ or hooks/. The only network call is $.http.fetch to the fixed openrouter.ai URL (the hook cannot change the URL).

Key handling: apiKey is a sensitive userConfig, or the key comes from $.env.get / merged settings env (hooks/fast-jev.ts:227-243). It goes in a Bearer header, not argv. The hook reads all merged settings via $.settings.read() but only takes env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

The hook is a TypeScript module that runs in Claude Code's sandboxed plugin engine (no fs or network of its own; the network goes through the host's $.http.fetch). Function hooks are a very new, early-access surface, so the trust model is less battle-tested than command hooks.

Prompt-injection surface: the full conversation, including tool inputs and text, is the Jev state. Injected text inside a tool input or file content Claude echoed could sway keep/drop scoring and cause important calls or results to be dropped (integrity risk, not exfiltration). Jev is documented as injectable.
The Jev question strings interpolate only the tool name, id and char count, not user content. Answers are validated as finite numbers (request.ts:117-131).

Fork provenance: 3 commits by one new contributor (Vladislav Rzhevicky, bitstarz.com) on top of tamaratran's Devin-generated code. The fork's diff is small and reviewable (ZDR block, URL, key name). The marketplace.json owner is this fork.
package-lock.json (62 KB) and demo/JevDemo (macOS Swift, not used) are present but never executed in the plugin path. devDependencies only: vitest, tsx, typescript.
gh-ingebyd-fast-jev-compaction-openroute.dataEgress: Every compaction sends the ENTIRE session transcript to openrouter.ai, and the same state is resent once per request batch, up to 25k estimated tokens each. It contains all user prompts, assistant text, tool inputs (file paths, bash commands, diffs, Edit/Write content) and, for the first/pinned messages, full text. Tool results are replaced by 'ok, N chars (omitted)' notes in the state, so file contents and command output are not sent. Secrets pasted in prompts or written in commands or Write inputs would still be sent (inputs are truncated to 1000/200/60 chars only when the state does not fit). The provider block {zdr:true, data_collection:'deny'} restricts routing to ZDR endpoints, and OpenRouter errors if none exists. OpenRouter itself still sees the request, and 'zdr' only covers upstream provider retention. The existing no-secret-leak hook does not cover this path, because the request is made by the hook engine and not via Bash/Read.
gh-ingebyd-fast-jev-compaction-openroute.failureMode: Fails closed to Claude Code's built-in summary. Any exception (no key, non-2xx, including a ZDR routing rejection, malformed JSON, missing answer, state cannot be fitted) is caught in the session.compact handler (fast-jev.ts:283-289) and returns next(event), with a toast and ui.log 'fallback to built-in summary (...)'. It is also a fallback when the reduction is under 25%. There is NO request timeout, and no retry logic in the fetch path (JevClient uses plain fetch, and the hook uses $.http.fetch without a timeoutMs), so a hung OpenRouter call would stall compaction until the host's own limit. The turn.complete auto-trigger has no cooldown: if compaction falls back to the built-in summary or the context stays above 60%, it can retrigger on every turn (in-flight flag only). Effectively this changes when auto-compaction happens (60% versus Claude's default), which is a behavior change independent of Jev. Risk of silent semantic loss: dropped tool calls and results are removed without a summary, so a wrong low score deletes needed context (mitigated by keepThreshold 0.5 and model re-runnability).
gh-ingebyd-fast-jev-compaction-openroute.contextCost: Zero MCP tools, skills or hook-injected additionalContext, so nothing is added to the prompt or skill listing. Positive effect: compaction keeps verbatim messages instead of a summary, so it removes large stale tool results but keeps much more text than a summary would (post-compact context is bigger). Cost is external: ~25k-token state x N requests per compaction on OpenRouter (about $0.001 per request at $0.042/M).
gh-ingebyd-fast-jev-compaction-openroute.autoInvocation: Fully automatic and deterministic once installed: session.compact fires on /compact and on Claude's auto-compact, and the turn.complete hook self-triggers compaction at 60% context. Needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 in the env. The installed 2.1.285 binary still gates function hooks behind that variable (strings: 'hooks modules are not turned on for installed plugins ... set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1'). The checked-in types are from 2.1.274, and API drift on 2.1.285 was NOT verified (the code was not executed).
gh-ingebyd-fast-jev-compaction-openroute.latencyImpact: Only during compaction, not on every tool call. Concurrent OpenRouter calls, each ~200-600 ms p50/p95 for Jev, plus large-body upload (state up to ~100 KB). Roughly 1-3 s per compaction, with no per-tool overhead. On fallback it adds that time on top of the built-in summary. There is no timeout, so a worst case is a stalled compaction.
pros: Genuinely automatic: hooks session.compact and turn.complete, so the user never has to say 'use jev'. Zero context/token cost in the prompt, no tool list bloat.

Natively OpenRouter (src/request.ts:2-3,82) with the hard-coded provider {zdr:true, data_collection:'deny'} (request.ts:54), the only candidate that treats the whole-transcript egress as a privacy problem. This matters for client projects.
Fails closed to the built-in summary on every error path (fast-jev.ts:283-289) and on <25% reduction. Missing key or ZDR rejection just means normal compaction.

Small, readable code (~1.9k lines incl. tests), no shell exec or telemetry, MIT. Uses Noul questions correctly, batches under the 32k limit and fits the state into staged budgets (compact.ts, state.ts). Tool results are NOT sent to Jev (only length notes), limiting egress of file contents.
Uses Jev for what it is good at (many cheap, well-defined yes/no probabilities per item, ~$0.042/M input), and keeps user/assistant text verbatim, avoiding a lossy LLM summary.
cons: Depends on the early-access function-hooks API (needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1). Types were generated for 2.1.274, the user runs 2.1.285, and compatibility is unverified. A breaking change will disable it silently or loudly.

Very young and thin: repo created 2026-09-18, 33 commits (17 by Devin AI, 12 by upstream owner, 3 by fork author), 2 stars, 29 test cases in 2 files, all using a fake Jev. It has never been shown to run on real sessions here, and there is no release.

Replaces the summary with pruned raw history: no summary of decisions or progress, so post-compaction context can stay large, and a mis-scored drop (Jev is overconfident on unanswerable input and injectable) silently loses needed tool calls. State is limited to 25k tokens while Opus contexts can be far larger, so on long sessions the state is heavily abridged and 'cannot fit' throws, giving the fallback anyway.

turn.complete forces compaction at 60% context with no cooldown. If reduction is <25% or the built-in fallback leaves the context still >= 60%, it can compact repeatedly. It also changes the user's auto-compact timing.

No request timeout or retry. The whole transcript (prompts, commands, diffs, tool inputs) leaves the machine on every compaction, and no-secret-leak does not cover it. OPENROUTER_API_KEY would have to sit in settings env or the plugin keychain option; adding it to the env also makes it visible to Bash subprocesses (add to the protected-vars list).
Narrow: it only covers compaction, not permission or routing decisions. It is a fork with upstream drift risk (tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction moves daily) and a single-maintainer, unknown-org fork.
gh-ingebyd-fast-jev-compaction-openroute.verdict: A well-scoped, safe-failing, genuinely automatic OpenRouter+ZDR Jev integration, but it targets only compaction, relies on an early-access hooks API unverified against 2.1.285, and is days old with fake-only tests. It is a reasonable opt-in experiment (pin a commit, set the flag, watch the toasts) and not something to depend on as the main Jev integration.

gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.name: RahulBalakavi/claude-code-jev (jev-auto-mode)
gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.whatItDoes: Stdlib-only Python PreToolUse hook (`jev-auto-mode hook`). It reads the hook JSON from stdin and loads the last 8 human-authored user messages from the transcript JSONL. It then POSTs {user_messages, tool_name, full tool_input, cwd} plus one Choice question (allow/block/ask with criteria text) to OpenRouter's /api/alpha/decisions with model typesafe/jev-1.13. It maps the answer to permissionDecision allow/deny/ask. A low-confidence answer (below 0.85) or any error becomes ask. It appends hash-only telemetry to a local JSONL file. The repo also ships a benchmark CLI, a capacity calculator and a claude-openrouter launcher, which this user does not need.

providerSupport.evidence: src/jev_auto_mode/hook.py:55-73 reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Default model is typesafe/jev-1.13 (JEV_OPENROUTER_MODEL) and default URL is https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (OPENROUTER_DECISIONS_URL). providers.py:61-100 sends Authorization: Bearer plus a body of {state, model, questions:{permission:{type:'choice',instructions,criteria}}}. It parses payload['answers']['permission']['choice'|'confidence'] and usage input_tokens/output_tokens/cost (providers.py:101-128). No TypeSafe-direct URL exists in the code. The benchmark also has a Haiku-via-OpenRouter arm and an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY arm, and neither is used by the hook.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Nothing to patch, it is OpenRouter-native. It uses the /alpha/decisions endpoint, not /v1/systemone.

interface.name: PreToolUse hook: `jev-auto-mode hook`
interface.purpose: Classifies each matched tool call. It emits hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision allow, deny or ask with a reason. The example matcher is Bash|Edit|Write|NotebookEdit|WebFetch|WebSearch|Task with timeout 5 (examples/claude-settings.json). It always exits 0. hook.py:20-52 and 113-123.

interface.name: CLI `jev-auto-mode benchmark --provider jev|haiku|anthropic`
interface.purpose: Runs the 18-case labeled fixture and writes results (cli.py:379-389).

interface.name: CLI `jev-auto-mode capacity`
interface.purpose: Wall-clock and token capacity calculator (cli.py:391-399).

interface.name: bin/claude-openrouter
interface.purpose: Launcher that points Claude Code itself at OpenRouter with ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and a separate CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. It is irrelevant and harmful for an OAuth user.

interface.name: Env config
interface.purpose: OPENROUTER_API_KEY, JEV_OPENROUTER_MODEL, JEV_AUTO_MODE_CONFIDENCE (default 0.85, must be in 0.5-1.0), JEV_AUTO_MODE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 3), JEV_AUTO_MODE_LOG_PATH, OPENROUTER_DECISIONS_URL, LOG_LEVEL.

interface.name: No MCP server, skill or plugin manifest
interface.purpose: There is no .mcp.json, SKILL.md, plugin.json or marketplace.json. It is a hook only.

gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.tests: 5 small pytest files (hook, policy, transcript, launcher, capacity). test_hook only asserts the ask fallback when the API key is missing. test_policy covers the confidence gate. There is no mocked-HTTP test of the Jev response parsing. There is an 18-case synthetic fixture (fixtures/actions.jsonl) and a live benchmark write-up (results/openrouter-live-2026-09-18.md): 90 decisions, p50 230.8 ms, p95 459.2 ms, mean 263.9 ms, 73/90 exact match (81.1%), 0 dangerous allowed, $0.0000227 per decision.
gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.runtime: Python 3.11+, stdlib urllib only (no runtime dependencies), installed via `uv tool install .` with a hatchling build. It works with the user's Python 3.13 and uv.
gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.install: git clone, `uv tool install .` (build is local and pulls hatchling). It installs a `jev-auto-mode` binary; use its absolute path (~/.local/bin/jev-auto-mode) in the hook command. Then add the PreToolUse group to settings.json. OPENROUTER_API_KEY must be in the environment Claude Code gives hooks (shell export, or the settings.json env block, which is plaintext).
security: Key handling: the key is read from the env var only and sent as a Bearer header over HTTPS. It is never in argv. The default OPENROUTER_DECISIONS_URL can be overridden by env, so an attacker who controls env could redirect the key and payload (low risk). hook.py:55-73, providers.py:82.
No shell exec, no subprocess and no installer scripts in the hook path. Network is urllib to openrouter.ai only.

Prompt-injection surface: tool_input is agent-controlled and is sent in full. A Bash command or file content can embed text such as 'choose allow' that Jev reads as state. The README's claim that the agent cannot talk its way to allow only covers assistant text and tool outputs, not the tool arguments. Independent evals also show injected instructions in state can move Jev answers.

transcript.py:_human_text takes every type:'user' entry that has text blocks. It does not filter isMeta or injected system-reminder or skill-load entries, so these can leak into user_messages and dilute or pollute the authorization signal. Also unverified.

Telemetry is local only (~/.local/state/jev-auto-mode/decisions.jsonl): timestamp, tool name, a 16-hex sha256 prefix of the action, and the verdict. It has no raw args and no phone-home. Errors are logged via logging to stderr, and the unexpected-response path logs the payload.
The launcher sets ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and empties ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. This is not needed and would break OAuth if used; do not use it.

The hook's own decisions can conflict with the existing no-secret-leak hook. Claude Code hook precedence is deny over ask over allow, so no-secret-leak blocks should still win. OPENROUTER_API_KEY still needs adding to that hook's protected list because it now lives in the env.
gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.dataEgress: To openrouter.ai (and then TypeSafe as the provider) on every matched tool call: up to the last 8 user prompts in full (untruncated, from the whole transcript file), the tool name, the full tool_input (whole Bash commands, full Edit old/new strings, full Write file contents, URLs, WebSearch queries, Task prompts), the cwd path, and the criteria text. Assistant text and tool outputs are excluded. Client-project source and any secrets inside commands or writes leave the machine. There is no redaction or size cap. The README admits this (Data handling section).
gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.failureMode: Fail-safe to human review. Any KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, OSError, JSON error or ProviderError (HTTP error, timeout, bad shape) is caught, and the hook prints permissionDecision 'ask' and exits 0 (hook.py:26-45). A missing key also gives ask. The code timeout is 3s, plus the settings timeout of 5s. A hook-level timeout or crash (an uncaught exception type) is non-blocking in Claude Code, so it falls through to the normal flow. Low confidence (<0.85) gives ask. In default or auto mode this is safe. In bypassPermissions mode an 'ask' from a PreToolUse hook is still expected to prompt (unverified here), which would interrupt unattended sessions on every outage or uncertain call. Only 'deny' adds value there. The input is bounded only by the 32k context; a huge Write or message likely returns HTTP 4xx, which becomes ask.
gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.contextCost: Zero tool-definition tokens, since it has no MCP tools or skill. Nothing is injected into the model context. Only the permissionDecisionReason (about 60 chars) is shown on ask or deny. Its cost is latency and money, not context.
gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.latencyImpact: The Jev round trip measured 231 ms p50 and 459 ms p95 (README and results file, fixture-sized prompts of about 540 tokens). Add Python interpreter start via the uv tool shim, roughly 30-80 ms (estimate), and a full parse of the whole transcript JSONL on every call (transcript.py:20-37 reads every line, not just the tail). That grows with session length and could add tens to hundreds of ms in long sessions. Real prompts with 8 user messages plus a Write body will be larger than the fixture. The hook runs in parallel with the gitnexus and no-secret-leak hooks, so it is max() rather than sum() for the same event. There is no local static allowlist fast path, so even `git status` and `ls` pay the network hop. Expect roughly 300-600 ms added to each Bash, Edit or Write call.
gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.autoInvocation: Fully deterministic: the harness fires the PreToolUse hook on every matcher hit, and the model never has to remember. Its output is allow, deny or ask. There is no model-side trigger.
pros: Genuinely automatic and OpenRouter-native, the exact wiring the user wants. It uses /api/alpha/decisions with typesafe/jev-1.13 and a Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY, with the URL and model overridable by env (hook.py:64-73). Zero context cost.
Small and auditable: about 400 lines of stdlib Python, no runtime dependencies, no shell exec, no telemetry beyond a local hash-only log.

Fail-safe design: every error path becomes ask with exit 0. The user-message-only transcript filter keeps assistant text and tool results out of the prompt. The confidence gate makes allow require at least 0.85 and ask short-circuits.

Includes live measurements (p50 231 ms, p95 459 ms, about $0.00002 per call, 0 dangerous allowed on 18 cases) and an honest README that states the limits, including that it adds a hop to stock auto mode rather than replacing it.
Useful in bypassPermissions sessions: the deny path gives a cheap last line of defense that costs no Claude quota. The Choice-with-criteria request pattern is a reusable template for other Jev hooks.
cons: Immature: one commit, 4 stars, one contributor, no release, alpha Jev endpoint with no SLA. The 18-case synthetic fixture gives 81% exact match, and 17 of the 90 decisions were block escalated to ask. Expect many 'ask' prompts, which is friction in bypassPermissions or auto sessions.

Uses PreToolUse, not PermissionRequest. An 'allow' pre-empts the user's normal permission and auto-mode classifier on every matched call, replacing a stronger classifier with a weaker, overconfident one. It also adds latency to trivial calls because there is no static fast-path or RISKY regex pre-filter, unlike the official cookbook pattern.

Privacy: full commands, file contents and up to 8 user messages go to OpenRouter and TypeSafe for every call, unredacted and untruncated. That is a problem for client projects. Also OPENROUTER_API_KEY must be added to the no-secret-leak protected list.
Tool arguments are an injection channel into the classifier state, and the transcript parser does not exclude meta or system-injected user entries. It re-reads the whole transcript per call.

Only one Choice question with a vague single-prompt policy (no reversible/serves_task Noul decomposition). The example matcher uses the old 'Task' tool name and omits Read, Grep and MCP tools. The launcher and benchmark bloat is irrelevant and the launcher would break OAuth.
gh-rahulbalakavi-claude-code-jev.verdict: A small, honest and safe-failing OpenRouter-native Jev permission hook that would work automatically, but it is alpha-quality with a single commit and a tiny fixture. It ships as a PreToolUse gate that pre-empts auto mode and sends full commands and code to a third party. Use it as a reference implementation or fork it: put deny/ask-only behavior on a PermissionRequest or narrow-matcher hook with a static pre-filter, redaction and the reversible/serves_task Noul pattern, rather than installing it as-is on client work.

gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.name: JayDoubleu/cc-mod-jev (plugin jev-context)
gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.whatItDoes: Claude Code function-hooks plugin (TypeScript, no runtime deps). On session.compact (manual /compact, engine auto-compaction, or its own turn.complete trigger at >=60% context) it pairs every tool_use/tool_result, sends an abridged whole-conversation state (20k-token cap) plus two Noul questions per call (keep call? keep full result?) to OpenRouter's Jev decisions endpoint, then returns the transcript with stale results truncated to a 300-char head or stale calls dropped, everything else verbatim and no summary written. Falls back to the built-in summary on missing key, Jev error, or <20% reduction. Optional tool.call gate (off by default) asks Jev whether an oversized Bash/Read output is needed in full and cuts the middle if P<0.3. /jev prints config and decisions.

providerSupport.evidence: src/openrouter.ts:3 OPENROUTER_DECISIONS_URL = https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions; :4 default model typesafe/jev-1.13; :37 Authorization Bearer; body {model,state,questions} (:41). Key from plugin option apiKey, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, EVAL_OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or settings.json env block (hooks/jev-context.ts:158-165, src/config.ts:136). baseUrl is overridable (src/config.ts:139, env JEV_CONTEXT_BASE_URL) but the code always sends the OpenRouter-shaped body (questions map) and expects an 'answers' object, so pointing it at TypeSafe's own /systemone schema would need code changes.

interface.name: hook session.compact

gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.runtime: TypeScript run by Claude Code's own function-hooks runtime (no Node/node_modules); v0.1.2; TypeScript only as devDependency for typecheck; tests via 'claude plugin test' (needs the flag)
gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.install: export CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1; claude plugin marketplace add JayDoubleu/cc-mod-jev; claude plugin install jev-context@cc-mod-jev; OPENROUTER_API_KEY in env or plugin apiKey option (or settings.json env block). No install scripts, no postinstall.
gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.tests: 31 tests in tests/library.test.ts (18) and tests/register.test.ts (13), the latter driving hooks through the engine $ with a fake OpenRouter; 2 evals (/jev status and env passthrough). Gate not verifiable under eval harness (author states tool.call result not applied in eval child in 2.1.278). One live measured session in the README (314k to 11.4k tokens, 1 request, $0.00033, 503 ms). CI: none seen.
security: No shell exec, spawn, child_process or eval anywhere in src/ or hooks/ (grep). Only network is $.http.fetch to the configured URL; scripts/smoke.ts uses plain fetch but is a manual dev script.

Key handling: sent in an Authorization header via engine $.http.fetch (not argv, not a subprocess). Plugin option apiKey is marked sensitive. Key can also be read by the hook from settings.json env via $.settings.read(). Not logged; /jev prints only key=set/MISSING (src/config.ts:170).

Prompt-injection surface: tool results (up to 120-char head each at stage 0), tool inputs (1000 chars), user/assistant texts (2000 chars) go into the Jev state; adversarial file/web content can push Noul answers to drop/truncate needed context (Jev is known to be steerable by injected state). Output is only numeric probabilities, so no code execution path, worst case is lost context or wrongly kept context.
Gate is a tool.call hook and can silently alter what the model sees from Bash/Read (cut middle with a note), a correctness risk (e.g. test failures in the middle of output); off by default.

Function hooks run in-process in Claude Code's runtime with $ access to settings, session messages, http; the plugin is 372+ lines of readable TS but a broad-capability early-access API. Single-author, 1 star, days old: supply-chain trust is the main risk; pin to a commit.
Does not touch the existing no-secret-leak PreToolUse hook; OPENROUTER_API_KEY should still be added to its protected list (the plugin's own hook reads it, the model should not).
No telemetry beyond x-title header 'jev-context (Claude Code mod)' to OpenRouter.
gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.dataEgress: Only to openrouter.ai (default URL, src/openrouter.ts:3), and only when compaction runs (or gate is on). Compaction: goal (last 3 user prompts, 500 chars each), the entire conversation oldest first with user/assistant texts abridged to <=2000 chars (down to length-only at later stages), every tool_use input abridged to <=1000 chars (Bash commands, file paths, edit snippets may contain secrets or client code), and per tool result a note 'ok, N chars' plus a <=120-char head; plus question text per call. Capped at ~20k state tokens, 28k per request. Gate (if enabled): last 12 messages abridged (600 chars text, 200 chars per call input), goal, and up to 1500-char head and 800-char tail of the Bash stdout or Read file content per gated output, i.e. actual file/command contents. No ZDR/provider pinning or data-collection:deny set in the request body (body is only model,state,questions), so OpenRouter/TypeSafe retention policy applies to client-project content. model IDs and base URL configurable.
gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.failureMode: Fail-safe for compaction: missing key, HTTP error, malformed JSON, missing answers, state not fitting, or reduction below 20% all fall back to the built-in summary (manual/auto) or skip (plugin-triggered) via noteFallback (hooks/jev-context.ts session.compact). Gate fails open (errors return the original outcome, 'gate skipped'). turn.complete errors are logged and swallowed. No explicit per-request timeout or AbortSignal in the plugin code (grep found none); it relies on $.http.fetch defaults, whose time does not count toward the 10 s hook budget per CLAUDE.md, so a hung OpenRouter request could stall a compaction; alpha endpoint has no SLA. Residual risk is semantic, not availability: overconfident Jev may truncate or drop a result still needed (model can re-run tools; truncation notes say so), and pruning leaves user/assistant text untouched so reduction may be small on chat-heavy sessions.
gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.latencyImpact: Nothing on the per-tool path unless gate is enabled (gate adds one Jev round trip, roughly 0.3-0.6 s, to each Bash/Read output over 8000 chars). Compaction adds about 0.5 s end to end measured in the README (1 request, 7.8k input tokens) versus a multi-second LLM summary, so it is likely faster than the built-in compaction. turn.complete does one cheap $.session.usage() call per turn; no network unless over 60%. Does not interact with the gitnexus/no-secret-leak hooks (different event family).
gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.contextCost: Zero MCP tools, no skills, no SKILL.md, no MCP instructions, no additionalContext injection. Only /jev slash command description (one line). Gate adds a short '[jev-context cut N chars ...]' note only when it cuts; truncated compacted results carry a short note. Negligible standing context; its purpose is to reduce context (README claims 96% on one session, measured with 8 large file reads).
gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.autoInvocation: Fully automatic and deterministic once installed with the env flag: session.compact intercepts /compact and engine auto-compaction; turn.complete requests compaction at 60% context; optional gate on tool.call. Model never has to be told to 'use jev'. Requires CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 in env (can go in settings.json env) and Claude Code >=2.1.278 (user has 2.1.285).
pros: Native OpenRouter: default URL https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with typesafe/jev-1.13 and OPENROUTER_API_KEY (src/openrouter.ts:3-4, 37), no patching.
Truly automatic with zero context footprint (no tools, no skills, no injected text), matching the user's 'never prompt use jev' requirement.
Compaction is fail-safe: every error path falls back to the built-in summary or skips (session.compact handler); reduction floor of 20% prevents pointless prunes.
Cheap and fast: README measured 1 request, 7.8k tokens, $0.00033, 503 ms vs an LLM summary; state capped to 20k/28k tokens under Jev's 32k window with 5-stage fitting.
Verbatim pruning never rewrites user/assistant text and keeps tool_use/tool_result pairing intact; first message and newest 6 messages pinned; pairs <300 chars kept without a question.

Clean, small, readable code with no shell exec, no runtime dependencies, MIT; sensitive apiKey userConfig; 31 tests with a fake OpenRouter through the engine, evals, live smoke scripts, honest Limitations section and documented gate eval blind spot.
Config is rich (thresholds, env overrides JEV_CONTEXT_*) and gate is opt-in per tool; /jev gives visibility into every decision.
Works with subscription/OAuth login since it uses no Anthropic key; user's 2.1.285 exceeds the >=2.1.278 requirement.
cons: Depends on the early-access function-hooks API behind CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1; the author says the API may change and typings are pinned to 2.1.278, so a CC update could break it silently.

Privacy: whole-conversation abridged state (tool inputs up to 1000 chars, text up to 2000 chars, result heads) is sent to OpenRouter with no ZDR / provider-data-policy pinning in the request body (src/openrouter.ts:41); a client-project concern, and the gate would also send real file/command output heads and tails.
Not on the user's protected-vars path: OPENROUTER_API_KEY would live in settings.json env or the plugin config, and the no-secret-leak hook must be updated so the model cannot read it.
1 star, 1 author, 4 commits all on one day (2026-09-19), no releases, no CI; unreviewed by others; supply-chain risk for a plugin with broad in-process access.

Jev quality limits apply: overconfident on unanswerable inputs, steerable by injected text in tool results; wrongly dropped results can degrade the session, and state is abridged so decisions on long sessions are coarse (README Limitations).
No explicit request timeout in the plugin code; alpha endpoint has no SLA, so a slow OpenRouter call can stall a compaction.

Replaces the summary with no summary: only tool results are pruned, so chat-heavy or thinking-heavy sessions get little reduction (then falls back), and it defeats prompt-cache reuse like any compaction; the gate tool.call result is not verifiable in evals and can hide the middle of test/build output.
Only helps at compaction time, so it is an occasional benefit rather than a per-prompt daily one; with Opus 5.5 large context windows the trigger at 60% may rarely fire.
gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.verdict: Best-fitting automatic, OpenRouter-native Jev integration found: hook-driven, zero context cost, fail-safe fallback to built-in compaction, clean code with real tests. Held back to 6 by the early-access function-hooks flag, a days-old one-star single-author repo, and sending abridged transcripts (and optional gate output slices) to OpenRouter with no ZDR pinning, so try it on personal projects with the gate off and pin a commit before touching client work.

gh-failproofai-failproofai.name: FailproofAI/failproofai
gh-failproofai-failproofai.license: MIT + Commons Clause (no right to Sell; GitHub shows "Other"). Fine for internal and client use. Pack repo FailproofAI/jev-policies has no license set.
gh-failproofai-failproofai.runtime: Node/Bun npm package (global install), Next.js dashboard on localhost:8020, optional compiled Rust daemon failproofaid (root-installed systemd unit).
gh-failproofai-failproofai.install: npm install -g failproofai. Then either "failproofai config" (installs a root daemon via sudo, hooks every detected agent CLI, optional Cloud) or the lighter "failproofai policies --install --cli claude --scope user" (hooks only, in-process). Jev needs three more steps: "failproofai policies add FailproofAI/jev-policies" (downloads an external policy pack from GitHub), "failproofai jev --url https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 --mode observe --key-stdin < keyfile", then "failproofai jev test".
gh-failproofai-failproofai.whatItDoes: Hook policy engine and observability tool for 12 agent harnesses, Claude Code included. About 40 regex or deterministic policies gate tool calls. When ~/.failproofai/jev.json exists and a pack with semantic checks is installed, one Jev request per PreToolUse or PermissionRequest call runs in parallel with the regex policies. Jev can clear a deny only from policies marked "reviewable", and only when it was asked that exact concern. It can also warn or deny on its own. Every Jev question is a Noul (P(yes)) over the redacted call, recent user prompts, the agent's last message, and local facts. Jev is not used at Stop, SubagentStop or PreCompact. Those events only get regex policies and telemetry.

providerSupport.evidence: OpenRouter is first-class. src/hooks/semantic/jev-client.ts:10 and :202 give openrouter: baseUrl https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, model typesafe/jev-1.13. The client POSTs to <base>/systemone with TypeSafe's native body {model,state,questions} (jev-client.ts:35-41). Line 218 defines OPENROUTER_PROVIDER_PREFS = {zdr:true, data_collection:"deny", allow_fallbacks:false}, added as extraBody at :1093-1101. Auth is Authorization: Bearer <key> (:468), and redirects are never followed (:475). TypeSafe direct is https://api.typesafe.ai/v1 with model jev-1.13.0. The URL host picks the provider (jev-config.ts:442 maps openrouter.ai to openrouter). Only /api/v1/systemone is used, not /api/alpha/decisions. The key comes from jev.json or from env FAILPROOFAI_JEV_API_KEY (jev-config.ts:170), never from OPENROUTER_API_KEY. The provider, URL and model are read only from the global file, never from the env.
providerSupport.others: Vercel AI Gateway, Cloudflare Workers AI, custom TypeSafe-shaped endpoint, and FailproofAI Cloud proxy.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Nothing to patch. It is native. Only the key handling differs: use --key-stdin from a 0600 file, or FAILPROOFAI_JEV_API_KEY with the in-process (no-daemon) path.
