Also the model name. The request is sent as one JSON string and refused if over 32,000 characters. No file contents or tool output. github.com via git for the daily update check unless disabled.
gh-abhishekvrshny-jevexec.failureMode: Provider failure is fail-open to the normal prompt. Timeout 15s (AbortSignal.timeout, jev.js:86), one retry on 429/5xx under the same 15s budget, hook timeout 20s. Errors become 'unavailable', which produces no output and lets the host decide. The exception is that cli.js:26-29 sets exit code 2 on any thrown error (bad stdin JSON, audit-file write failure such as a full disk or bad permissions in audit() at cli.js:56, unsupported event). Exit 2 from a Claude PreToolUse hook blocks the tool call, so those cases fail closed. A missing node_modules would crash on the static ink import in monitor.js (exit 1, non-blocking). Oversize payloads throw and defer to the host. With guardrails configured, an 'uncertain' Jev answer maps to 'ask' semantics but is emitted as nothing at PreToolUse, so the normal flow decides.
gh-abhishekvrshny-jevexec.contextCost: Zero MCP/tool-definition tokens and no skill listing. No additionalContext injection. The hook only adds a deny or ask reason text when it fires, plus the statusMessage 'jevexec: assessing action' in the UI on every tool call.
gh-abhishekvrshny-jevexec.latencyImpact: Node startup plus a static import of ink and react on every hook run (cli.js imports monitor.js at top level), roughly 100-250 ms per invocation on both PreToolUse and PermissionRequest, plus an audit-file append and rewrite. With no guardrails, PreToolUse makes no network call. With guardrails, every tool call (Read/Edit/Grep etc. are never locally allowed) adds a Jev round trip: p50 about 0.2-0.6 s, worst case 15-20 s. PermissionRequest calls Jev on every prompt. This stacks with the gitnexus and no-secret-leak hooks. In bypassPermissions, PermissionRequest never fires, so only PreToolUse applies.
gh-abhishekvrshny-jevexec.autoInvocation: Deterministic hooks on every tool call (PreToolUse) and every permission prompt (PermissionRequest). Fully automatic, no prompting needed. Value depends on the user having authored guardrails. With none, PreToolUse only enforces 6 regex hard-denies.
pros: OpenRouter is the native default: /api/alpha/decisions with typesafe/jev-1.13 and OPENROUTER_API_KEY (src/jev.js:3-10, 181-186). No patching. Base URL, model and provider are overridable.

Sensible design: typed score/noul questions, thresholds (allow only with risk < 0.35, authorization >= 0.8, no rule conflict), and unavailable/uncertain results defer to the normal prompt instead of allowing (core.js:43-69, adapters.js:174-194). It never returns allow at PreToolUse, so it can't override other hooks' denies.

Good key hygiene: header auth, not argv, 600 env file enforced, redaction of audit entries and error bodies, payload bound with no silent guardrail truncation (jev.js:82-85). Hook command written with absolute node path via shlex.quote (install.sh:221). Installer merges settings non-destructively and has an uninstall.
Zero context cost, purely deterministic invocation, MIT license, 4 mocked test files, and a useful audit log plus monitor for reviewing decisions.
The natural-language guardrail feature (e.g. 'never touch client X repo', 'no pushes to main') is a distinctive capability that pure regex hooks lack, for client-project safety.
cons: The authorization signal cannot work on Claude Code. cli.js:48 reads input.user_prompt, but Claude Code hook stdin carries no user prompt (grep: no transcript reading anywhere). The intent is always undefined, and the question defaults to 'missing intent = not authorized' (jev.js:57). So authorization is expected to stay below 0.8 and PermissionRequest will almost never auto-allow on Claude. That is my inference from Claude's hook input schema, not run-verified. The headline value (safe auto-approval) is therefore largely absent, and PermissionRequest reduces to deny-on-rule-conflict.

Does not fit this user's modes. Defaults are auto and frequent bypassPermissions, where PermissionRequest doesn't fire. Only PreToolUse remains, and it acts only on hand-written guardrails or six easily bypassed regexes. The cookbook pattern (static risky regex then reversible/serves_task Noul questions) is a better fit and lighter.

Repo is 4 days old, 1 author, 20 commits, 0 stars, no releases, package private, alpha /alpha endpoint. Behavior is calibrated only by guessed thresholds ('release calibration remains future work' in docs/architecture.md). Jev overconfidence and injected-instruction weakness apply directly to the allow decision.

Auto-update from the author's main branch inside the hook path (updater.js) plus curl|bash install and npm install is an ongoing supply-chain exposure for a security control on client projects. Must set JEVEXEC_AUTO_UPDATE=0 and pin a commit.

Robustness gaps: exit code 2 on internal errors blocks tools, and audit failure occurs after assessment and can block. Static ink/react import on every hook adds startup latency. matcher .* means every tool call pays Node startup, and with guardrails a Jev call, next to the gitnexus and no-secret-leak hooks.

hooks/claude.json uses ${PLUGIN_ROOT} with no plugin manifest, so it can't be used as a Claude plugin. The installer writes directly into ~/.claude/settings.json. Key stored in ~/.config/jevexec/env is not covered by the no-secret-leak hook (OPENROUTER_API_KEY still needs adding). A CLI-installed runtime lives outside plugin management.
gh-abhishekvrshny-jevexec.verdict: Well-structured, OpenRouter-native Jev permission hook with sane fail-to-prompt semantics, but it is 4 days old and its main value (authorization-based auto-allow) likely can't work on Claude Code because there is no user_prompt in hook input. It is also moot under the user's bypassPermissions sessions and adds per-call Node/ink startup, and it carries an auto-update-from-main risk. Better to copy the cookbook PermissionRequest pattern than adopt this, unless the user specifically wants NL guardrails, and then only with JEVEXEC_AUTO_UPDATE=0 and a pinned commit.

gh-kmasterrr-use-jev.runtime: Node (ESM, top-level await, global fetch; node:fs/child_process/os/path only; zero npm deps). Node 24 fine.
gh-kmasterrr-use-jev.tests: None. No test files, no CI, no releases. Only smoke-check is running an example JSON by hand. README benchmark is a self-described personal benchmark (~60 items, 1 item ≈ 1.7 points; 83% acc, 267 ms median, $0.017/1000 items vs Sonnet 5) by the author.
security: Key never on argv: read from env or file and sent only in Authorization header (jev.mjs:39-42,96); output never echoes key. Good.
Key file fallback ~/.claude/secrets/openrouter.key is plaintext 0600; set-key.sh uses hidden read, umask 077, sk-or- validation. User does not need it if OPENROUTER_API_KEY is in env.
Only shell exec is execFileSync('powershell') gated on win32 (jev.mjs:45-53), args array, apostrophe-escaped path: irrelevant on Linux. No shell=true, no eval, no child process on Linux.
No telemetry, no other network hosts; only openrouter.ai. install.sh is 10 lines of cp/mkdir, no curl|sh, no sudo, no rc-file edits.

Prompt-injection surface: whatever text Claude puts in `state` (file contents, diffs, web text) goes to Jev; per brief, injected instructions in state can move answers. SKILL.md mitigates by rule 'signal, not authority; does not grant permissions'. Answers are typed numbers/choices only, so Jev output cannot inject text back into Claude beyond choice keys chosen by the caller.

Skill rule 1 requires asking the user for an explicit yes before sending anything possibly private/credentials, and 'never send secrets'. This is model-enforced only, not deterministic; the existing no-secret-leak.cjs hook does not cover this script's stdin/file content and OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not in its protected list, and the script reads the key itself so a Bash call `node jev.mjs` would pass the hook.
Request files written to scratchpad/temp by Claude may contain sensitive state and linger on disk (.gitignore excludes request*.json in the repo only).
gh-kmasterrr-use-jev.dataEgress: Exactly the JSON body {model, state, questions} that Claude composes, POSTed over HTTPS to openrouter.ai (then relayed to TypeSafe), plus Bearer key. Content is whatever Claude chooses to put in `state` (could be code, diffs, emails, tickets). No file scanning, no automatic collection, no telemetry. Privacy gate is only a natural-language rule in SKILL.md that asks for user consent before possibly-private text, which conflicts with the goal of frictionless automatic use.
gh-kmasterrr-use-jev.failureMode: Script fails closed to an error object with exit 1 (no fake decision); SKILL.md rule 6 says show the exact error and do not imply Jev decided. 15 s default timeout via AbortSignal.timeout (jev.mjs:24,100), no retry; fallback to the second route only on 404 (:129). Since it is an on-demand skill and not a hook, a failed call cannot block or stall tool execution beyond up to 15 s in one Bash call. Confidence gating (0.6 choice/score; noul 0.35-0.65 uncertain) is advisory text; low confidence means 'Claude decided'.
gh-kmasterrr-use-jev.contextCost: Low. Skill listing entry ~ 420 chars description (~105 tokens) fits well in skillListingBudgetFraction 0.02. Full SKILL.md body (7.9 KB, ~2k tokens) loads only when the skill triggers. No MCP tool defs, no hook-injected text. Each use adds the request JSON + result to context.
gh-kmasterrr-use-jev.latencyImpact: None on ordinary turns. Each invocation costs one Bash tool call (node startup ~50 ms + Jev p50 ~200-270 ms, up to 15 s timeout), plus the extra model turn to write request.json and read output; total overhead is dominated by Claude's own writing of the file, so the win over just asking Opus is small for one-off judgments.
gh-kmasterrr-use-jev.autoInvocation: Model-discretion skill trigger only. The description is oriented to business workflows (triage, lead scoring, support routing, rerank, guardrails, 'ask Jev') rather than coding events, so for daily coding it will rarely fire without being told, and when it does, rule 1 makes Claude ask permission for anything not obviously public. No hook, so it cannot be a deterministic gate (e.g. no PermissionRequest integration). It does NOT meet the 'never prompt use jev' goal by itself; the user would need to rewrite the description and privacy rule and add hooks.
pros: Genuinely OpenRouter-native: hardcoded typesafe/jev-1.13, both /api/v1/systemone and /api/alpha/decisions, OPENROUTER_API_KEY from env (jev.mjs:19-23,39).
Tiny, auditable, zero-dependency script (141 lines), no argv key exposure, no telemetry, no shell exec on Linux, MIT license; installer is 10 lines of cp.

Reusable as a reference caller: request/answer shape for choice/score/noul with criteria formats is clearly documented in SKILL.md and examples, useful to build a PermissionRequest/Stop hook or a small MCP wrapper.
Sound safety stance: 'signal, not authority', explicit uncertainty thresholds, honest error reporting, no fabricated decisions on failure.
Very low context cost (~105 tokens listing entry) and no impact on latency of normal turns.
cons: Skill-only, model-discretion: not deterministic, no hook, and the description targets support/lead/inbox workflows, so it will not automatically add value in coding; fails the user's core 'automatic' requirement.

Rule 1 forces asking the user before sending possibly private content, which contradicts frictionless automation and, for client code, would fire constantly; enforcement is prose only, not a technical gate.
Immature: created 1 day ago, 4 commits, 2 stars, no tests/CI/releases; benchmark is author's small personal set (~60 items) on business text, not coding decisions.

Route ambiguity: sends the OpenRouter-prefixed model id to /v1/systemone (native schema per brief uses 'jev-1.13'), and falls back to /alpha/decisions only on 404; a 400 from route 1 would surface as a failure even if route 2 works. Unverified since nothing may be run.

Does nothing for the user's permission-automation goal (no PermissionRequest hook, no cookbook recipe); OPENROUTER_API_KEY not in no-secret-leak.cjs list, and the script would read the key from env/file outside that hook's view; secrets dir plaintext file convention duplicates key storage.
Each use costs a Claude turn to author JSON, so latency/cost saving vs. just deciding in-model is marginal for coding.
gh-kmasterrr-use-jev.verdict: Clean, safe, OpenRouter-ready reference script, but it is a business-workflow skill that only triggers at model discretion and asks for consent before sending private text, so it does not deliver automatic Jev use in daily coding. Worth reading as a request-format example (or cherry-picking jev.mjs), not as the integration itself; prefer the OpenRouter PermissionRequest hook cookbook for the automatic behavior.

gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.name: jev-claude-plugin (barretg)
gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.whatItDoes: Go CLI (jev find/ask/scan/lint/probe/gain/hook) packaged as a Claude Code plugin. It has one skill (skills/jev/SKILL.md) and one PreToolUse hook on Read (hooks/hooks.json, timeout 20 s). The hook reads the whole file, sends it to Jev with the user's last transcript message as the goal, and rewrites the Read to a narrowed offset/limit window (about 1/5 of the file, minimum 150 lines) for files of 400 lines to 80 KB. When confidence is below 0.60 it denies the Read up to twice per file and asks the agent to run `jev hook goal` first. find/ask send one request per file with skeletons and full contents, so the model is queried instead of the agent reading the files. An opt-in PostToolUse lint command exists in code (internal/run/lint.go) but is not wired in hooks.json.

providerSupport.evidence: internal/typesafe/client.go:26-30 has OpenRouterURL=https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions as the default endpoint and SystemOneURL=https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone. client.go:33-38 lets JEV_BASE_URL override the endpoint. Key lookup at client.go:43-50 checks OPENROUTER_API_KEY, JEV_TOKEN, then TYPE_SAFE_AI_KEY, TYPESAFE_API_KEY and TYPESAFE_AI_API_KEY. client.go:122 sends 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. DefaultModel is 'jev-latest' (client.go:29) and JEV_MODEL overrides it (client.go:77). The OpenRouter model slug in the brief is 'typesafe/jev-1.13'. The OpenRouter switch commit (6cd5570) changed the URL and key names but not the model id, and nothing in the repo shows 'jev-latest' being accepted by OpenRouter. Every bench script and test still uses 'jev-latest', which was the TypeSafe direct model name. It is unverified whether OpenRouter resolves that alias. If it does not, every call returns 4xx and the hook silently passes through. It is a one-line fix: set JEV_MODEL=typesafe/jev-1.13.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Trivial. Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY and JEV_MODEL=typesafe/jev-1.13 (env only), or edit the one DefaultModel constant. Run `jev probe` once to confirm the response shape (answers/noul/choice/score/usage) against OpenRouter's alpha/decisions schema.
providerSupport.others: No other providers. It is Jev-only.

interface.name: PreToolUse hook, matcher Read: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/jev hook read`
interface.purpose: hooks/hooks.json, timeout 20 s. Passes through when disabled, when the file is under 400 lines or over 80 KB, or when the agent set offset/limit (hook.go:99-141). Otherwise it reads the file, takes the last user message from the transcript JSONL (600 chars max, hook.go:232-291) or the recorded sharper goal, calls locateLine, then either returns updatedInput {offset, limit} with additionalContext, or a permissionDecision 'deny' asking for a sharper goal (hook_retry.go:137).

interface.name: skill `jev` (skills/jev/SKILL.md, 6.5 KB)
interface.purpose: Model-discretion trigger. It fires when locating a feature whose name is unknown, after an empty or noisy grep, or when checking a property across many files. It is also meant for auditing groups of files. It says not to use jev for an exact symbol, and tells the agent to tell the user if the key is missing.

interface.name: CLI jev find "<desc>" [path...]
interface.purpose: Ranks files by description in three passes: skeleton screen, full-content verify, chunk locate. Prints score and file:line. One request per file, so about 60 ms per file and 2.5 to 9 s per call.

interface.name: CLI jev ask "<yes/no>" <file|dir...> [-q]
interface.purpose: Per-file P(yes) plus line; -q lists only files answering yes.

interface.name: CLI jev scan [path...]
interface.purpose: Dry run showing bytes, tokens and cost with no API call.

interface.name: CLI jev hook goal --session <id> <file> <text>
interface.purpose: Writes a sharper goal to ~/.cache/jev/hook/<session>.json (mode 0600, 30 min TTL) for the next Read.

interface.name: CLI jev lint edit (PostToolUse, opt-in)
interface.purpose: Checks an Edit/Write/NotebookEdit diff against .jev-rules.json. Off unless JEV_LINT_ENABLE is set. Not registered in hooks.json.

interface.name: CLI jev probe / jev gain
interface.purpose: probe sends one 3-primitive request and prints the raw response (client.Debug = os.Stdout). gain reports local usage from ~/.jev/usage.jsonl.

interface.name: env knobs
interface.purpose: JEV_HOOK_DISABLE, JEV_HOOK_DEBUG, JEV_HOOK_MIN_CONF, JEV_HOOK_MIN_LINES, JEV_HOOK_NO_RETRY, JEV_BASE_URL, JEV_MODEL, JEV_STATE_DIR, JEV_DATA, JEV_NO_STATS, JEV_LINT_ENABLE.

interface.name: MCP server
interface.purpose: None. There is no .mcp.json.

gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.createdAt: 2026-09-26 (fork). The upstream Boris Lemeec commits date from 2026-09-18.
gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.runtime: Go 1.22+ per the README (go.mod says 1.26.1, which is unusually new). The binary must be built locally with `make build`; bin/ is gitignored. Standard library only, so there are no third-party dependencies.
gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.install: Clone, `make build`, `claude plugin marketplace add "$PWD"`, `claude plugin install jev@jev`. This builds and runs third-party binary code, and the plugin cache copy needs `make sync` after every rebuild. The key goes in the env (OPENROUTER_API_KEY or JEV_TOKEN). The hook command uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/jev, which is absolute and so is unaffected by the user's PATH override. The deny-retry text tells the agent to run `jev hook goal` as a bare command, which needs `jev` on the Bash PATH. That depends on the plugin bin/ being added to the Bash PATH and on the user's PATH env override not defeating it. Otherwise the agent could be stuck until the 2 retries run out.
gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.tests: 4 Go test files with 12 Test funcs: scan_test, hook_test, hook_retry_test, permute_test. There is nothing for the HTTP client, find, ask or lint. Benchmarks are committed under bench/ (RESULTS.md, RESULTS_ASK.md, RESULTS_HOOK.md, tokenecon/TOKENS*.md, TIMING.md). The find/ask query sets were labelled on private repos and are not published. The Hugo/Prometheus hook bench is reproducible. Sample sizes are small (30 queries, 9 questions, 50 windows, 7 paired runs, 3 audits).
security: Key handling: read from env only and sent as a Bearer header (client.go:122). It is never put in argv and never written to disk. `jev probe` prints raw response bodies (not the key).

Egress path: the URL is env-overridable via JEV_BASE_URL (client.go:34). A poisoned project env could redirect all file contents and the API key to another host. This is low risk for the user's own env.
Local writes: ~/.cache/jev/hook/<session>.json (0600, contains file paths and goal text, 30 min TTL) and ~/.jev/usage.jsonl (0644; counts only, no content). No telemetry beyond the OpenRouter call.

Shell exec: none in Go code (no os/exec). The deny message asks the agent to run a Bash command containing a %q-quoted absolute path and session id. The session id is validated against [A-Za-z0-9_-] (hook_retry.go:52-62), so path traversal is prevented.

Prompt-injection surface: file contents and the user's last message go into the Jev state. Jev returns only numbers, so the direct impact is limited to steering which window a Read shows, or forcing a deny. Injected text in a file could bias the located line and hide the real target. The additionalContext text is plugin-authored and constant.

Secret exposure: the hook does not exclude sensitive files. Any Read of a 400-line-plus file sends the whole content to OpenRouter, including a large secrets/config file the agent reads. The existing no-secret-leak PreToolUse hook may deny first, but hooks for the same event run in parallel, so ordering is not guaranteed. The scan for find/ask skips dot-files and dirs (scan.go:38-56, :122-130) but not credentials.json, *.pem, id_rsa or secrets.yml.

Installer risk: builds and runs a random third-party Go binary that sits in the Read path of every session. The fork has 0 stars and the author is not the original one. Reading the source shows nothing malicious.
Transcript access: the hook reads the whole session transcript JSONL (transcript_path) on every qualifying Read (hook.go:236-277) and sends the last user message, up to 600 chars, to OpenRouter.
gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.dataEgress: To openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (or JEV_BASE_URL) on every Read of a file of 400 lines to 80 KB that has no offset/limit set. The request carries the full file content (up to 80,000 bytes), the file basename, and the last user prompt (up to 600 chars) as the goal. Each find/ask request carries one file's skeleton or full contents, per file, across the whole scanned tree except skipped dirs and dot-files. The client sends the OpenRouter key in the Authorization header. The unit is roughly 30 tokens of instructions plus file content per question, and the result is numbers only. Client code and any secrets inside large source files therefore go to OpenRouter and on to TypeSafe. Source files under 400 lines are never sent by the hook, but find/ask sends everything.
gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.failureMode: Mostly fail-open for the Read hook. Unreadable payload, a missing key, a decode error, an API error or a low goal all call passThrough, which prints an empty decision and exits 0 (hook.go:103-168). Main errors exit 1 (non-blocking in Claude Code). Latency worst case is bad. The client has a 120 s HTTP timeout and 5 retries with backoff (client.go:65-88), but the hook's own limit is 20 s, after which Claude Code kills it and proceeds. That is up to 20 s of stall per Read during an OpenRouter/alpha outage. Two fail-closed-ish behaviours: on locate confidence under 0.60 the hook DENIES the Read up to twice per file (hook_retry.go:137-155), which costs extra turns and needs the agent to run a Bash command. This deny fires under bypassPermissions and auto modes as well. A narrowed Read silently hides about 80% of a large file. The agent is told via additionalContext, but an Edit based on a partial view is a real risk. There is no cap on total denies per session beyond 2 per file, and state is keyed on the session id. If the model id 'jev-latest' is rejected by OpenRouter, every call returns 4xx and the hook passes through with cost ~0 and benefit 0.
gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.contextCost: Very low: 0 MCP tools and no MCP instructions. The skill listing entry is about 590 chars (about 150 tokens) against the 0.02 skillListingBudgetFraction. The full SKILL.md is 6.5 KB (about 1.6k tokens) when triggered. The hook adds about 60 tokens of additionalContext per narrowed Read. A deny reason is about 150 tokens per event. Net context effect is negative (saves) on large-file reads.
gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.latencyImpact: The author measured +1.25 s per qualifying Read (bench/hook/RESULTS_HOOK.md:137) and says wall-clock is a wash (bench/TIMING.md). A find costs 2.5 to 9+ s per call (about 60 ms per file, linear). The hook re-scans the entire transcript JSONL on each qualifying Read, so overhead grows with session length. A typical p50 of about 200 ms per Jev call over OpenRouter is likely, but the hook makes 2 or more sequential calls (verify plus locate). Only Reads of 400 to about 2000 lines are affected. Small reads are untouched. It stacks with the gitnexus hook only on Grep/Glob/Bash, not on Read.
gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.autoInvocation: Yes for the Read hook: deterministic, fires on every Read without an offset or limit and needs no prompting. The find/ask CLI is model-discretion via the skill. The skill's description triggers are concrete but compete with gitnexus semantic search and Grep, and the model may prefer gitnexus, so the actual find/ask usage is uncertain. Nothing is wired for Bash permission gating, PermissionRequest or Stop.
pros: The Read hook is genuinely automatic (hooks.json PreToolUse Read, updatedInput offset/limit + additionalContext). It is the only candidate found that needs no 'use jev' prompt. It is well gated and fails toward passthrough (hook.go:99-141, 168, 183-185, 201).

OpenRouter is the default endpoint (client.go:27) with OPENROUTER_API_KEY read first (client.go:44). It is pure Go stdlib with no third-party dependencies, so the supply-chain surface is small. No os/exec, no argv secrets, no telemetry.

The author committed reproducible benchmarks (bench/RESULTS*.md, hook cases on public Hugo/Prometheus repos). Claimed numbers: find P@1 0.96 vs BM25 0.33 vs grep 0.08, ask F1 0.97, Read hook 50/50 targets kept and -41% billed tokens in paired runs. They are the author's own measurements and sample sizes are small, but the methodology is sensible (labellers forbidden from running jev, near-miss cases).

Sensible safeguards: explicit offset/limit is never overridden, files over 80 KB are refused because sectioned recall was measured worse (hook.go:138), the window is generous (min 150 lines), the agent is told how to re-read, there is a session-id validator, and JEV_HOOK_DISABLE is a one-line kill switch.
Negligible context cost: no MCP tool schemas, a 590-char skill description.
Cost per use is trivial ($0.042 per 1M tokens, about $0.0001 per narrowed read, $0.0025 per 434 KB find scan).
cons: Unverified OpenRouter compatibility: DefaultModel remains 'jev-latest' (client.go:29) while OpenRouter's slug is 'typesafe/jev-1.13'. The fork commit changed only URL and key names. The benches (bench/hook/measure_band.py:34) still use jev-latest, and there is no evidence of any OpenRouter run. The fix is trivial (JEV_MODEL), but it means the 'beta' label is optimistic.

Silent code hiding while editing: narrowing a Read to about 20% of a large file is dangerous for a user running bypassPermissions with the main model editing heavily. The agent sees only a note. The deny-retry loop can also block Reads, and with 'auto' or bypass modes there is no human to notice a miss.

Privacy: the whole content of any Read file of 400 lines or more, plus the user's last prompt, goes to OpenRouter/TypeSafe. There is no exclusion for secrets or client-confidential files. This conflicts with the client-project rules and with the no-secret-leak hook, and the user would need an allowlist/denylist wrapper. The mixed-parallel hook ordering with no-secret-leak is unspecified.

Latency: +1.25 s per qualifying Read per the author's own bench, two or more sequential API calls, the whole transcript re-scanned per Read, and up to 20 s when OpenRouter's /alpha endpoint (no SLA) is slow. Wall-clock benefit is described as a wash.

Requires building and installing an unaudited third-party Go binary. The fork has 0 stars, 8 commits, 3 committers and no releases. It was created 2026-09-26. bin/ is not committed, so `claude plugin install` from GitHub alone yields a broken hook, and rebuilds need `make sync`.

Thin tests (12 tests, none for the client, find, ask or lint). The find/ask query sets are private and unreproducible. Benchmarks are Go/Flutter-centric, so the author himself says other stacks are not covered.

Overlaps with gitnexus semantic query for find, and Claude Code's own subagents/Grep. The skill's find/ask relies on model discretion and is slow on big trees (linear per-file requests). The token-saving thesis targets API-billed context; the user is on a subscription where the saving is less directly valuable.
The retry deny asks the agent to run a bare `jev hook goal` command. This depends on jev being on the Bash PATH, and the user's PATH override in settings env may make that fail, wasting turns.
gh-barretg-jev-claude-plugin.verdict: Best-executed automatic Jev integration seen: it is a real deterministic Read hook with conservative gates, small context cost and OpenRouter as the default endpoint. Two things hold it at 6 for this user. The model id is unverified against OpenRouter. The hook hides ~80% of large files from an agent that edits in bypass mode, and it ships raw file contents to a third party with no secret or client-code filter. It is worth a read-only pilot (fork, set the model to typesafe/jev-1.13, add a path denylist, JEV_HOOK_NO_RETRY=1) before trusting it on client projects.

gh-gilbert09-jev-cli.name: jev-cli (Gilbert09)
gh-gilbert09-jev-cli.whatItDoes: TypeScript Claude Code (and Codex) plugin that wraps Jev in hooks. guard is a PreToolUse gate on Bash/Write/Edit that scores destructiveness with Score/Noul questions and returns allow, ask or deny. screen is a PostToolUse check for prompt injection in WebFetch/Read/Bash output, with modes warn, block or quarantine. done is a Stop hook that catches unsupported completion claims. rank is an MCP semantic-grep tool. guard and screen are on by default; done and rank are off. It calls Jev through @typesafe-ai/sdk POST /v1/systemone and caches answers on disk for 30 minutes.

providerSupport.evidence: The README-level triage said OpenRouter was 'no, needs a code patch'. Reading the code shows it works with configuration only. src/core/jev.ts:25 builds the client as `new TypeSafeClient({ apiKey })` with no baseURL, so the SDK reads its own environment variables. @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0 (npm tarball dist/index.mjs:56-62) reads TYPESAFE_API_KEY and TYPESAFE_BASE_URL (baseURL default https://api.typesafe.ai at line 513). systemOne() POSTs to `${baseURL}/v1/systemone` (line 554). Setting TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api therefore yields https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone, which is the OpenRouter endpoint. The Bearer key comes from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_TYPESAFE_API_KEY, then TYPESAFE_API_KEY, then ~/.jev/config.json apiKey (src/core/config.ts:131-134). The model is overridable with JEV_MODEL or config.model (config.ts:135); the default 'jev-latest' is not a known OpenRouter id, so set model to 'jev-1.13'. Requests use the TypeSafe schema {model, state, questions}, which matches OpenRouter's /v1/systemone. Not run live; static reading only.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Trivial, no code change. Set TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api, TYPESAFE_API_KEY=<OpenRouter key> (or the plugin userConfig field, or apiKey in ~/.jev/config.json), and JEV_MODEL=jev-1.13 (or 'model' in ~/.jev/config.json). Put the env vars in settings.json env so hook subprocesses and the MCP server inherit them. Caveats: the OpenRouter key would be copied into a second variable name, and OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not in the no-secret-leak protected list yet. Also verify that OpenRouter's response shape matches what normalizeAnswer expects (answers[k].noul/score/choice/probabilities/legend).
providerSupport.others: Codex is supported through --host=codex. Any model string is passed through, so nothing is hardcoded to jev-latest apart from the default.

interface.name: PreToolUse hook: jev guard (matcher Bash|Write|Edit, timeout 10s)
interface.purpose: hooks/hooks.json:4-13 and src/capabilities/guard/handler.ts. Sends the command (max 4000 bytes, redacted), cwd and repoRoot, or the file path plus a 4000-byte content or old/new_string preview. Jev answers about 10 questions, including danger Score, irreversible, escapesProject, exfiltrates and pipesRemoteCode. decide.ts returns allow, ask or deny. Any failure returns ask.

interface.name: PostToolUse hook: jev screen (matcher WebFetch|Read|Bash, timeout 10s)
interface.purpose: hooks.json:14-23 and screen/handler.ts. Sends up to 40 KB of redacted tool output (minimum 24 bytes) and the origin URL, path or command. Skips paths matching excludeGlobs (.env*, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa*, .git/**). On a detection it emits additionalContext and systemMessage, and optionally decision:block or updatedToolOutput quarantine. Fails silent.

interface.name: Stop hook: jev done (timeout 15s)
interface.purpose: hooks.json:24-33 and done/handler.ts. Reads the transcript summary and last_assistant_message, and may emit {decision:'block'} once per turn. Not documented as disabled in hooks.json, but returns none because config done.enabled=false. It still spawns node on every Stop.

interface.name: MCP tool: rank (stdio server 'jev' via bin/jev.mjs mcp)
interface.purpose: .mcp.json and rank/server.ts:80-121. Inputs are query, candidates[{id?, path, snippet?}] and topK. Returns a ranked file list plus a 'present' probability. readOnlyHint is true. The tool is registered even when rank.enabled=false, and a call then returns a disabled-type failure. The README reports 0 model adoptions in 18 sessions.

interface.name: CLI: jev install [--project] [--codex] [--dry-run]
interface.purpose: src/install.ts. Merges hooks into ~/.claude/settings.json without removing others, then spawns the guard with a fake `rm -rf /` payload to verify. The plugin route (/plugin install jev) does not need it.

interface.name: CLI: jev doctor
interface.purpose: src/doctor.ts. Checks config and live API access.

interface.name: CLI: jev guard|screen|done|mcp
interface.purpose: src/cli.ts:34-54. Subcommand dispatch. Each hook has a watchdog: guard 3000 ms, screen 3500 ms, done 4000 ms. On watchdog or crash, guard emits ask and the others emit nothing.

interface.name: Config: ~/.jev/config.json or JEV_CONFIG_PATH; env JEV_MODEL, JEV_SCREEN_MODE, JEV_DEBUG, JEV_FORCE_ENABLED, JEV_CACHE_DIR, JEV_STATE_DIR, JEV_CODEX_ASK
interface.purpose: src/core/config.ts. Per-capability enabled and timeoutMs. There is no per-tool or per-permission-mode switch.

security: No LICENSE file: gh licenseInfo is null. package.json and plugin.json declare MIT, and marketplace.json lists MIT, so the intent is clear but there is no legal grant in the repo.

No telemetry. The only network egress is the SDK call to baseURL. No fetch, exec or spawn appears in runtime code. The single spawnSync (src/install.ts:151) runs jev's own binary with a fixed payload in `jev install`.

The API key is never in argv. It comes from an environment variable, a plugin userConfig field (sensitive: true) or ~/.jev/config.json in plaintext. The hook command lines contain no secrets. The sdk sends it as an Authorization Bearer header.

Prompt-injection surface: the state sent to Jev contains untrusted command text, file content and web content. Jev's own evals say injected instructions in state can move answers. The guard input is agent-generated, so a compromised model could word a command to look benign. Per the Jev brief, calibration is imperfect. The guard also lets a benign-looking 'allow' skip nothing, since hooks only add gating, but a false allow while bypassPermissions is on has no other backstop.

When screen warns, the hook writes additionalContext into the model's context, and that text includes origin and a content excerpt. The excerpt is attacker-controlled, so this is a small secondary injection channel (screen/decide.ts:127; not deeply audited).

Redaction (src/core/redact.ts:10-28) covers sk-ant-, sk-, ghp_, xox, AKIA, PEM blocks, JWTs and KEY=value assignments. It would catch sk-or-v1-... OpenRouter keys through the sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{16,} pattern only if there are no hyphens after 'sk-or'. The hyphen is not in the class, so 'sk-or-v1-…' would NOT match that generic pattern, though the *_API_KEY=value pattern would. Redaction is regex best-effort and the README calls it 'not a guarantee'.
The on-disk cache (~/.jev/cache or CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA/cache, 30 min TTL, max 500) stores only sha256-keyed answers, not state. State dir stores a per-session done marker. Both are best-effort.

README says guard sends 'the command or file path ... Not file contents', but guard/handler.ts:104-111 sends up to 4000 bytes of Write content and Edit old_string/new_string. The docs understate egress.

Installer merges into settings.json and only replaces entries whose command matches jev.mjs. The plugin route runs dist/*.js committed to git, so users must trust the committed 125 KB bundle rather than a build they can reproduce. No postinstall scripts. package-lock is present. The sdk is MIT and from typesafe-ai (real org).
Single author (Tom Owers), 6 commits over 2 days (2026-09-19 to 2026-09-20), 1 star, no release, no issues history. Not battle-tested by other users.
gh-gilbert09-jev-cli.dataEgress: To api.typesafe.ai by default, or OpenRouter, and from there to TypeSafe, if the base URL is redirected. Sent per event: (1) guard, on EVERY Bash/Write/Edit call: the command text (max 4 KB), cwd, repo root, description, and for Write/Edit the file path plus up to 4 KB of new content or old/new string. (2) screen, on EVERY WebFetch/Read/Bash result of 24 bytes or more: up to 40 KB of the output or file content, plus the origin URL, path or command. In practice this is a large share of everything the agent reads and every command output in a client repo. (3) done, only if enabled: the last assistant message plus a transcript summary. (4) rank, only if enabled: candidate paths and file snippets. Everything is regex-redacted for credential shapes first; excludeGlobs suppress only .env*, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa* and .git/**. Source code, client business logic, DB query output and logs are NOT excluded and will leave the machine. Via OpenRouter the payload also passes through a second third party. Not suitable for client projects under NDA or DPA without explicit sign-off.
gh-gilbert09-jev-cli.failureMode: guard fails CLOSED to 'ask' on timeout (1500 ms per request, watchdog 3000 ms), a missing key, an API or malformed error, an unparseable payload, or a Write/Edit without a file_path (jev.ts, guard/handler.ts:134, cli.ts:35-43). It always exits 0 with JSON, so it never uses exit-2 blocking. Since guard fires on every Bash/Write/Edit, an OpenRouter outage, a 429 on the /alpha endpoint with no SLA, or a missing key turns into a permission prompt on every tool call. The guard ignores permission_mode (only typed at types.ts:13, never read), so it still runs in bypassPermissions and auto. Whether Claude Code honors a hook 'ask' under bypassPermissions is not verified here, but the risk is either constant prompts or a silent override. screen, done and rank fail OPEN and silent. done intervenes at most once per turn. The SDK has maxRetries 2 by default but is bounded by the AbortSignal and the timeout. Node 24 cold start is added on top of each call.
gh-gilbert09-jev-cli.contextCost: Low, and mostly deterministic: one MCP tool (rank), with a description of about 2.4k chars (questions.ts:139-160+) plus a schema of about 1k chars, so roughly 700-900 tokens, only if MCP tools are loaded rather than deferred. The tool is useless while rank.enabled=false, so it is wasted context, and the plugin has no way to drop it short of removing .mcp.json. No SKILL.md, no MCP instructions field and no SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit injection. Hook-injected text appears only on a screen detection (a short warning, possibly quarantined content) and on a done block (a reason). Zero cost on ordinary turns.
gh-gilbert09-jev-cli.autoInvocation: Fully deterministic for guard (every Bash/Write/Edit), screen (every WebFetch/Read/Bash) and done (every Stop, a no-op while disabled). This matches the requirement 'never having to prompt use jev'. rank is model-discretion MCP and was called 0 times in 18 benchmark sessions, so it is not effective. The tool description is well written, but does not help.
pros: OpenRouter is reachable with configuration only: the SDK honors TYPESAFE_BASE_URL and appends /v1/systemone (sdk dist/index.mjs:58,513,554), and src/core/jev.ts:25 passes only apiKey. Set TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api, the OpenRouter key as TYPESAFE_API_KEY and JEV_MODEL=jev-1.13. This corrects the README-level 'no' triage.

The only candidate with real end-to-end evidence: 1,176 Claude Code sessions, guard +29 pts and screen +33 pts on haiku (p<0.001), with raw JSONL in bench/results. It honestly reports done and rank as null and ships them disabled. It also documents its own benchmark artefacts and bugs.

Safe failure design: the wire contract is exit 0 plus JSON only, there is a per-hook watchdog, guard fails closed and screen fails open, and done intervenes once per turn. Unit tests cover the decision logic (about 260 test cases in 9 files across guard, screen, done, rank, hook, redact and cache), plus a 157-case live fixture suite and scripts/smoke.sh for wire contracts.
Compiled dist is committed, so the plugin works with `/plugin install jev` and no build. Config is per-capability, so you can run screen only, or guard only.

screen closes a gap the current setup does not cover: PostToolUse prompt-injection screening of fetched content and file reads, with an excludeGlobs list and a quarantine mode that replaces the tool output. The team's existing hooks are all pre-execution or regex-based.
Thoughtful decision logic: separate thresholds measured over multiple runs, probability mass and tail checks rather than a bare argmax, and a Codex output mapping pinned by tests.
cons: The benchmark applies to haiku and sonnet only. Sonnet shows -3 pts (p=0.388, no measurable benefit) and Opus is never tested. The user's main model is Opus 5.5, which likely has even less headroom, so most of the measured benefit probably does not apply, while the latency and egress costs do.

guard fires on every Bash/Write/Edit, ignores permission_mode, and fails closed to 'ask' on ANY timeout or API error. With an /alpha OpenRouter endpoint with no SLA, a p95 of 600 ms against a 1.5 s cap, and frequent bypassPermissions sessions, this creates either constant interruptions or unclear behaviour. The plugin has no way to disable itself in bypass mode.

Broad data egress: screen ships up to 40 KB of every Read, WebFetch and Bash output to a third party, and guard ships Write/Edit content. Only .env, .pem, .key, id_rsa and .git are excluded. The README also says guard sends 'not file contents', which contradicts guard/handler.ts:104-111. This is a real problem for client projects.

Overlaps and stacks on existing hooks: no-secret-leak (which fails closed), gitnexus (seconds) and existing permission classifiers. Three to four synchronous hooks per Bash call compound latency. The regex redactor does not clearly cover OpenRouter 'sk-or-v1-...' keys, and OPENROUTER_API_KEY would additionally need adding to the no-secret-leak protected list if it is stored as an env var.

No LICENSE file (licenseInfo null) despite MIT metadata. One author, 6 commits over 2 days, 1 star, no release, no external users or issues. The dist bundle is committed, so the audited src may not equal what runs (not verified; the bundle was not built or run here).

rank MCP is dead weight (~700-900 tokens of tool definition, 0 adoption in the author's own benchmark, disabled by default). done is disabled by default and hooks a no-op node spawn at every Stop. Neither the OpenRouter response schema nor jev-1.13 compatibility with these question rubrics has been verified; question wording was tuned against jev-latest on TypeSafe's API.

Jev's independent evals (overconfidence on unanswerable inputs, injections in state moving answers) apply directly: the guard judges attacker-influenced text, and a false 'allow' under bypassPermissions has no second line.
gh-gilbert09-jev-cli.verdict: Best-engineered Jev integration seen, with an evidence-backed benchmark and fail-safe hooks, and it switches to OpenRouter with env vars only (TYPESAFE_BASE_URL, JEV_MODEL=jev-1.13). For this user the benchmark benefit does not transfer (haiku-only, no gain on sonnet, Opus untested), guard fail-closed on every tool call under bypassPermissions plus the /alpha endpoint is a friction risk, and screen sends up to 40 KB of every read and command output off-machine, which is a problem for client projects. If tried at all, run a screen-only install on personal repos (guard disabled) after adding OPENROUTER_API_KEY to the no-secret-leak list, and treat it as an experiment.

gh-moukrea-automodel.name: moukrea/automodel
gh-moukrea-automodel.whatItDoes: Go binary (one binary: local proxy on 127.0.0.1:8788, hooks, statusline, ledger/eval). Installer sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to the proxy and adds a selectable model 'Jev (auto)'. For sessions on that model, the UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse[Agent]/PreToolUse[Workflow] hooks ask Jev on OpenRouter (Score over tiers, Noul per mode, warm-turn continue/informs Noul), and the proxy rewrites model and effort in the upstream request to api.anthropic.com (OAuth headers forwarded unchanged). Subagent model alias is rewritten via updatedInput, workflow agent() calls get injected model/effort, and 'ultracode' mode injects an additionalContext that pushes Claude toward Workflow orchestration.

providerSupport.evidence: internal/config/config.go:126 JevURL default 'https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions', key from config openrouter_api_key (config.go:65) or $OPENROUTER_API_KEY override (config.go:205); internal/jev/jev.go do() sends Bearer key, body {model,state,questions,session_id}; catalog.toml:11 jev_model='typesafe/jev-1.13'. jev_url is a toml key (config.go:40) so overridable. OpenRouter is the only supported backend by design.

Self-update every 6h, applied when idle (update.go, checksum only from the same GitHub release).

Not run (static audit). Also an eval package and labeled cases in testdata/eval; routing-quality research in docs/research.
security: Key handling: OpenRouter key stored plaintext in ~/.config/automodel/config.toml (0600); 'key set' reads from stdin (no argv exposure); installer reads key with stty -echo and pipes to key set; $OPENROUTER_API_KEY overrides. Key sent only as Bearer to jev_url. Proxy dump mode (AUTOMODEL_DUMP_DIR, off by default) redacts authorization/x-api-key/cookie headers but writes full request bodies to disk (proxy.go:153-165).

Proxy is a full MITM-position component for ALL Claude Code traffic (every session, including ones on plain opus, because ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is global in settings.json env). It sees OAuth bearer tokens and all prompts/code in plaintext over http://127.0.0.1:8788 (no TLS, loopback only by default; any local user/process could also use it as a forwarder to api.anthropic.com, but it holds no credentials itself).

Installer is curl|sh but does verify sha256 from the release checksums.txt; no signature/attestation, so a compromised GitHub release or account (single maintainer, 0 stars, 4 days old) means arbitrary code in the auto-updater path running as the user and sitting in the API path. Auto-update every 6h applies new releases unattended.

Installer modifies ~/.claude/settings.json (env, hooks, statusLine, permissions.allow adds blanket 'Workflow' allow) and adds slash commands; backs up first. It replaces user's statusLine command (chains old one via sh -c).

Hooks return permissionDecision 'allow' for Agent and Workflow PreToolUse (agent.go:94, workflow.go:~120), which bypasses permission prompts for those tools on jev sessions; combined with rewriting workflow scripts (jsscan-based regex injection) this is a script-mutating hook. Low impact for this user (auto/bypass mode) but a trust expansion.

Prompt-injection surface: prompt text, recent prompts, last assistant reply, compaction summary, first ~N chars of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, diff stat are sent to Jev; injected instructions there can bias the tier choice (worst case: wrong model/effort, or ultracode notice injected). Jev output is typed and validated, so no free-text injection back into Claude; only tier/mode. UltracodeOn additionalContext text is static, but Jev's Noul answer can turn on an instruction to 'Author and run a workflow for every substantive task', which raises token spend.

No telemetry per README; only GitHub releases API check every 6h and doctor key check to OpenRouter. Shell exec: git -C for repo signals, systemctl/launchctl/journalctl, ps, sh -c for chained statusline; no eval of remote content.

OPENROUTER_API_KEY is stored in automodel config, not in the user's env, so the existing no-secret-leak.cjs protected-vars list is not directly involved, but the config.toml path (~/.config/automodel/config.toml) would need protecting from Read/Grep by Claude.
gh-moukrea-automodel.dataEgress: To Anthropic: unchanged Claude traffic via local proxy (model/effort/max_tokens and effort-only system messages rewritten). To OpenRouter/TypeSafe per decision (privacy='full' default): truncated current prompt, last few prompts, start of last assistant reply, compaction summary after /compact, session size, repo signals (languages, file count, diff stat, head of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md via repo.go:73). For subagents: truncated Agent prompt; for workflows: agent() call site info. privacy='metadata' (config or per-repo .automodel.toml, which can only tighten) sends only sizes, kind hints, tier and languages. To GitHub: release check every 6h. For client projects, default full mode ships client prompt text and CLAUDE.md excerpts to a third party (OpenRouter -> TypeSafe); metadata mode would be required. Local ledger, per-decision states (2MB/session) and hooks.log stay on disk.
gh-moukrea-automodel.failureMode: Mostly fail-safe for Jev: hooks always exit 0 on error (hooks.go header, Run), Jev timeout 4s (config.go:127, warm 4s) then falls back to default tier with statusline warning; missing/rejected key, credit or rate-limit errors also fall back to the default tier. BUT the architecture adds a hard single point of failure: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points every Claude Code request (all sessions, all models) at http://127.0.0.1:8788, so if the proxy dies Claude Code stops working entirely; mitigation is SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hooks that redial (300ms) then restart the service once (4s) and otherwise BLOCK the prompt with instructions (guard.go), systemd user unit auto-restart, and 'automodel uninstall'. Mid-turn crash or a proxy bug (SSE tapping, body rewrite) would break in-flight requests. Without a systemd user session the proxy is not restarted after reboot. Because env is global, a crash affects sessions not on jev too.
gh-moukrea-automodel.latencyImpact: UserPromptSubmit blocks on the Jev call up to 4s (typical p50 ~200ms, p95 ~600ms per brief) on cold/initial turns plus Go binary startup and repo/git signal collection; warm turns can skip Jev (fast-path go-ahead, cost_aware gating) and switch cost logic reduces cache loss. Subagent and Workflow PreToolUse each add one Jev call per Agent invocation (a workflow with N agent() sites decides N sites, likely in parallel). The proxy adds a local hop, per-request JSON body parse/rewrite and SSE tap on every API call, negligible in ms but non-zero; README reports 98% cache hit over routed sessions but notes custom base URL disables server-side message threads and reduces early-session cache reuse. Hook timeout is 15s each.
gh-moukrea-automodel.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no tool definitions, no skills. Hook-injected text: only when ultracode mode fires (UltracodeOn ~700 chars, ~175 tokens, repeated after each compaction, plus an 'off' notice) and decision notices via additionalContext (decide.go:276). Two slash command files (/why, /flag) add small skill/command listing entries. Effort-only system messages are inserted into the API request by the proxy (cache-safe by design). Statusline segment is not model context. Net context cost is very small.
gh-moukrea-automodel.autoInvocation: Fully automatic and deterministic once installed AND the session model is 'Jev (auto)': hooks fire on every prompt/Agent/Workflow without the user asking. It does NOT provide 'Claude uses Jev when it adds value' generally; it only uses Jev for the single question of which Claude model/effort to run. It replaces the user's Opus 5.5 default when jev is selected (could be made default via settings 'model': 'jev'), and does nothing for permissions, risky-command gating or other Jev use cases (no PermissionRequest hook).
pros: OpenRouter-native and correct: uses https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with model typesafe/jev-1.13 and Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY (config.go:126, jev.go, catalog.toml:11); uses Score/Noul primitives well, one call per decision asking multiple typed questions with calibrated thresholds, cost-aware policy with confidence gating.

Careful failure handling for Jev itself: 4s timeout, fallback to default tier with visible statusline reason, hooks never fail the user action (hooks.go), proxy health check and auto-restart guard, doctor command, install --dry-run, settings backup, uninstall.

Substantial engineering for a 4-day-old project: ~11.8k LOC non-test Go, 31 test files, eval harness with labeled cases (testdata/eval), flag/report/why for measuring routing quality and savings, spend caps, privacy=metadata mode, per-repo .automodel.toml floors/ceilings, user override pins (/effort, [effort:X], [model:X]).

Keeps subscription/OAuth traffic on Anthropic unchanged; sets _CLAUDE_CODE_ASSUME_FIRST_PARTY_BASE_URL to preserve Opus 1M window; covers subagents and Workflow agent() sites, which is a genuinely automatic integration point not needing 'use jev' prompts.
Zero MCP/tool-definition context cost; MIT licensed; no telemetry claimed; checksum-verified binaries; the router is tunable via catalog (no hardcoded model IDs).
cons: Global ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL proxy is a single point of failure and total-visibility choke point for ALL Claude Code traffic including OAuth tokens and every prompt, for personal and client work; a bug or compromised auto-update (unsigned, same-release checksums, single maintainer, brand new, 0 stars, 113 commits in 4 days, v0.15.2 already) is high blast radius.

Solves a narrow problem for this user: model/effort routing. The user already runs Opus 5.5 by default in auto/bypass mode; value depends on unproven routing quality vs always-Opus and on savings; switching to 'jev' model replaces default and Haiku/Sonnet downgrades risk worse output. It does not address permission gating, risky-command review, or general 'Jev when it adds value' decisions.

Default privacy=full sends prompt text, recent prompts, last assistant reply, compaction summary and CLAUDE.md head to OpenRouter/TypeSafe on every decision; unacceptable for client projects unless privacy='metadata' is forced globally (reducing accuracy).

Auto-injects permissionDecision 'allow' on Agent and Workflow PreToolUse and adds blanket permissions.allow 'Workflow', rewrites workflow scripts by regex (jsscan.go), and its ultracode mode instructs Claude to run Workflows for every substantive task, which can inflate spend; stacks with user's existing hooks (gitnexus, no-secret-leak) in unknown ways and replaces the statusLine.

Adds latency to every UserPromptSubmit (up to 4s Jev + Go startup) and Jev calls per subagent/workflow site; /alpha endpoint has no SLA and Jev has known overconfidence and injection sensitivity; installer is curl|sh with self-updater running unattended; key stored plaintext in config.toml (0600) outside of no-secret-leak protections.
Windows/other paths irrelevant; without systemd user session no restart after reboot. Not runnable/verified here (static audit only), so quality claims (98% cache hit, accuracy) are author-reported.
gh-moukrea-automodel.verdict: Well-engineered, OpenRouter-native Jev router for model/effort selection that genuinely runs automatically via hooks and a local proxy, but it is a brand-new single-maintainer tool that puts a global unsigned-auto-updating proxy in front of all Claude traffic (including client work) and sends prompt text to OpenRouter by default, for a narrow benefit the user (already on Opus 5.5) may not need. Worth trying only in an isolated setup with privacy=metadata, pinned version and auto-update off; not recommended as the primary Jev integration.

gh-haystackeditor-stop-rules.name: stop-rules (haystackeditor)
gh-haystackeditor-stop-rules.whatItDoes: Per-repo Stop hook for Claude Code (and 13 other agents). On turn end it diffs the working tree against a stored baseline, cuts changes into git-diff hunks (or tree-sitter functions), attaches 25 context lines, and asks Jev one Noul question per hunk per rule from .stop-rules.md (up to 4 pieces per call). POSTs {state, model, questions} to /v1/systemone and reads answers[id].noul. Hunks at or above a bar (default 0.6) go back to the agent via exit 2 on stderr; asyncRewake wakes the agent in the background. A loop guard hands off to the user after 3 rounds. Optional OpenAI gpt-6-luna judge. Single committed 399KB bundled bin/stop-rules.mjs (11k lines), no npm install.

providerSupport.evidence: src/jev.ts:6-7 DEFAULT_ENDPOINT=https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, DEFAULT_MODEL=jev-latest. Request body is JSON.stringify({state, model, questions}) with Bearer auth (jev.ts send/fetchOnce); response parsed as answers[id].noul plus usage.input_tokens/output_tokens (jev.ts readAnswers/readUsage). This is the same TypeSafe schema OpenRouter serves at /api/v1/systemone. Local-mode override: src/credentials.ts:232-234 STOP_RULES_JEV_ENDPOINT is used verbatim as the POST URL (no path appended); model via STOP_RULES_JEV_MODEL (credentials.ts:160); key from TYPESAFE_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE (src/key.ts:15-19), else ~/.config/stop-rules/jev-key. The triage claim is wrong on one point: STOP_RULES_ENDPOINT (credentials.ts:146) is the TEAM-server endpoint, appends /v1/systemone and requires STOP_RULES_TOKEN; it is not the local override.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Config-only, no patch. Set STOP_RULES_JEV_ENDPOINT=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone, STOP_RULES_JEV_MODEL=jev-1.13, and TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=<file holding the OpenRouter key> (or TYPESAFE_API_KEY) in the env that reaches the hook process (Claude settings env block). Not tested by the author; I did not run it. 402/429/5xx/401 handling is TypeSafe-shaped but generic enough for OpenRouter.
providerSupport.others: Also OpenAI Responses API (gpt-6-luna) as alternative judge; team-mode self-hosted proxy (Cloudflare/Vercel/etc.) holding the key.

security: Key handling is good: key via env, key file, or stdin login (0600); never argv; redact() strips the key from error text (jev.ts). Only child process is git via execFile (git.ts), no shell strings.

Installer writes into the repo (.claude/settings.json, .stop-rules/ 390KB bundle, .stop-rules.md, other agent configs) and tells you to commit them; init is run by you, but a committed hook means anyone cloning runs a 400KB minified-ish bundle as a Stop hook. Review before use on client repos.

Bundle is committed and can only be checked via scripts/bin.mjs --check (byte-for-byte rebuild); I did not rebuild. Bundle contains a comment path from the author's Mac scratchpad (line 4145) - cosmetic.

Prompt-injection surface: code hunks are sent as Jev state, so injected text in changed files can push scores down (Jev brief) and silently suppress violations; feedback text returned to the agent contains rule text and line quotes only.

Adds OPENROUTER key exposure: key must be in hook env or a file; the existing no-secret-leak hook does not protect OPENROUTER_API_KEY yet. No telemetry found (grep for telemetry/analytics empty); only calls the Jev/OpenAI/team endpoint.
gh-haystackeditor-stop-rules.dataEgress: Every turn end: the added/changed hunks since last check (git diff vs baseline, including untracked non-ignored files), plus 25 unchanged lines above and below each change, plus your rule text, to the configured endpoint (OpenRouter -> TypeSafe). Lockfiles, .min, .map, .csv, .log, svg and data-only files are skipped (src/diff.ts:28-65) but there is no .env/secret-file filter; an untracked, non-gitignored .env or hardcoded key in a changed hunk would leave the machine. Answer cache (per piece) reduces repeat sends; state and cache live in the git dir, not the worktree. Client-project code goes to a third party on every turn.
gh-haystackeditor-stop-rules.failureMode: Fail-open and non-blocking. Cannot-run (network, 401, 402, 429 exhausted, 5xx, busy) returns exit 1 with a reason, which Claude shows as a hook error but does not block; baseline is held so the next turn retries the same change (holdsBaseline in jev.ts). Retries: 3 attempts with 1-16 s backoff, per-request timeout 90 s (jev.ts fetchOnce), hook timeout 120 s. Halves and resends on max_tokens_exceeded (relevant to the 32k OpenRouter context). Loop guard: 3 violation rounds then handoff to user (check.ts:53). Main risk is false positives waking the agent up to 3 times per change.
gh-haystackeditor-stop-rules.contextCost: Zero tool defs (no MCP, no skill). Hook text only enters context on violations: stderr report with hunk, rule, score, and quoted line, typically a few hundred tokens per violation. A wake-up also costs a full extra agent turn (main-model tokens) per violation round, up to 3 rounds.
gh-haystackeditor-stop-rules.autoInvocation: Fully automatic and deterministic: Stop hook fires on every turn end in any repo where init was run; asyncRewake runs it in the background and only re-engages the agent on exit 2. Independent of permission mode (auto/bypassPermissions do not affect it). Per-repo, not global: each repo needs init + .stop-rules.md, and the hook path uses CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, so a user-level settings install would need manual adaptation.
gh-haystackeditor-stop-rules.latencyImpact: Background (asyncRewake), so the turn is not blocked. Author-measured Jev ~0.55 s per check (README lines ~172), 0.20 s in demo; expected ~0.2-0.6 s on OpenRouter plus node startup and git diff. Cache makes repeat checks free. Adds no per-tool-call latency (unlike PreToolUse hooks).

OpenRouter works config-only: request/response schema in src/jev.ts matches OpenRouter /api/v1/systemone; STOP_RULES_JEV_ENDPOINT is taken verbatim and TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE avoids putting the key in env

gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.name: jev-gate (alexnarberhaus)
gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.whatItDoes: Stdlib-Python PreToolUse hook (matcher Bash) that auto-allows Bash calls Jev judges harmless. Order in gate.py evaluate(): skip unless permission_mode is default or acceptEdits (gate.py:31,313); check the user's allow/ask/deny rules (321); hard regex deny-list (239-248); one Jev call with 3 Choice questions (effect, network, injection); code thresholds (judge_verdict, gate.py:288-302). It only ever emits permissionDecision allow (render, 338-348), or a systemMessage. Shadow mode and already-allowed commands are judged in a detached --observe child, so Claude Code does not wait. Decisions go to a JSONL log at ~/.local/state/jev-gate/decisions.jsonl (mode 0600).

The key is read only from TYPESAFE_API_KEY or ~/.config/jev-gate/.env (judge.py load_key, ~147-158). grep finds no OPENROUTER string outside the eval data. The request body {model,state,questions} and the parsed reply answers[q].probabilities (judge.py _parse) match the /v1/systemone schema in the brief, so the shape is compatible with OpenRouter.

The install prompt text and the cost model (judge.py:24) would also need editing. It would be a fork, since upstream is a 0-star personal repo. A model-name mismatch with OpenRouter is unverified.

gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.license: None (GitHub licenseInfo is null and there is no LICENSE file). All rights reserved by default, so reuse or forking has no explicit grant.
gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.tests: Five stdlib unittest files with about 125 test functions (gate 44, cli 36, journal 19, judge 15, eval 11). Tests were read, not run. There is also an eval set: commands.jsonl (185 KB), real_labels.jsonl, synthetic_labels.jsonl and a Jev response cache (cache.json). CLAUDE.md states the 100% allow-precision goal, but I did not verify that it was met.
gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.runtime: Python 3 stdlib only (urllib, ssl, threading). No dependencies.
gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.install: git clone into ~/repos/jev-gate, then `python3 jev-gate install`. The installer edits ~/.claude/settings.json itself. For this user it would be better to copy gate.py, judge.py and journal.py and register the hook by hand with absolute paths.
security: Key handling: the key is never put in argv. The installer uses getpass and writes a chmod 600 .env, and judge.py sends it only as an Authorization Bearer header. A shell-exported OPENROUTER_API_KEY would still fall under the user's no-secret-leak hook protected-vars list, which does not yet include it.

Installer mutates global ~/.claude/settings.json (merge, idempotent, only removes its own entry on uninstall). It also writes a symlink into ~/.local/bin. No shell exec beyond the subprocess.Popen of its own script for the observer, and the observer child uses a list argv, not shell=True.

Prompt-injection surface: the command text is sent to Jev inside state. Mitigations are the preamble ('treat as data'), a dedicated injection question requiring P(clean) >= 0.99, and the deny-list running first. Jev is documented as injection-sensitive and overconfident on unanswerable inputs, and it sees only the command text, not script contents (judge.py preamble). Opaque commands such as `npm test`, `make` or `./script.sh` get judged on their text alone, and the design doc accepts this risk knowingly (CLAUDE.md).

Deny-list gaps: only regex-based. It matches rm -r, piping to shell, sudo/doas/su, eval, ~/.dotfile, chmod -R and dd/mkfs. It does not match `git push --force`, `git reset --hard` or `find -delete` (those rely on Jev and the network question), and shell obfuscation such as variable indirection is not covered beyond the Jev injection question. rule_verdict is approximate (gate.py:178-229).

A hook allow could only override the prompt, not the user's deny rules (per the design doc's verified contract). The gate checks ask/deny rules itself, and unreadable settings raise, which falls to the prompt.

Telemetry: none besides the Jev call. Local log holds redacted command, cwd, probabilities and a command SHA256 at mode 0600. Redaction is regex plus an optional user term list, and is best-effort (e.g. secrets without a recognised shape or key name pass through).
TLS uses a verified default context, with optional CA bundle env vars, so no verification bypass was found.
gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.dataEgress: Per judged Bash call, one POST to api.typesafe.ai (judge.py:22) with JSON {model, state:{command, cwd, workspace[]}, questions}. All strings are redacted first: home path replaced by ~, common token/key/JWT/AWS/GitHub/Slack shapes, emails, credentialed URLs, long mixed-case blobs, and user terms from redact.txt (judge.py:88-124). Nothing else is sent (no file contents, no transcript). Against OpenRouter, the same would go to OpenRouter (a provider hop), and OpenRouter's own logging or retention policy would apply. Best-effort redaction still leaves client paths, repo names and hostnames visible unless the user lists them in redact.txt.
gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.failureMode: Fail-open to the normal prompt, never fail-closed. Missing key, timeout, HTTP error, bad JSON, parse failure, malformed config or any exception ends with no output and exit 0 (gate.py:426-428). The Jev call has a 1.5 s total budget enforced by a thread join (judge.py _post_with_deadline, gate.py:38), inside a 5 s hook timeout. Under bypassPermissions or auto the gate does nothing, so it adds no protection there either.
gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.latencyImpact: Python startup is about 110-160 ms on the author's Mac, per the docs. In shadow mode and for already-allowed commands the Jev call is off the hot path (detached child), so the added latency is Python startup only. In auto mode a non-allowed command waits up to 1.5 s for Jev (p50 about 200 ms by the brief, plus TLS setup and process start). The existing gitnexus hook already adds seconds on Bash, and this hook would run in parallel with it, so the overall added time is small.
gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.contextCost: Zero tool definitions and no MCP server or skill. The hook injects nothing into context in shadow mode. In explain and auto modes it may emit one-line systemMessage text such as 'jev-gate: asking: ...' (roughly 30-60 tokens), shown to the user and not the model as far as I can tell.
gh-alexnarberhaus-jev-gate.autoInvocation: Deterministic PreToolUse hook on Bash, which fits the user's requirement that Claude Code uses Jev automatically without being told. Critically, evaluate() returns None unless permission_mode is 'default' or 'acceptEdits' (gate.py:31,313-314). The user runs defaultMode 'auto' and frequent bypassPermissions sessions, so the gate is inert in most of the user's sessions. Their permission_mode is auto or bypassPermissions, and Jev adds nothing there.
pros: Deterministic hook with a safe design: allow-only output, code owns the decision, fail-to-prompt everywhere, 1.5 s budget inside a 5 s timeout, and the user's ask/deny rules are honoured (gate.py:326-327).

Good egress hygiene: redaction runs before the send, with a user-defined redact.txt for client names, which suits the client-project use case. The log is chmod 600 and stores a hash plus a redacted command.
Includes an injection question (P(clean) >= 0.99), tiered thresholds, an eval harness with labelled real and adversarial commands plus a cache, and about 125 unit tests.

Stdlib only, small (about 2,000 lines of Python), and readable in an afternoon. Shadow mode with a live watcher lets you measure precision and prompt savings before enabling auto. Background judging keeps the hot path fast.
Needs only about 3 lines patched to move to OpenRouter's /v1/systemone, since the request and response schemas already match.
cons: Skips every permission mode except default and acceptEdits (gate.py:313). The user's defaultMode is auto and they often run bypassPermissions, so the gate would rarely fire. Removing the restriction would turn it into a model-based auto-approver in modes where Claude Code already decides, which the author explicitly refuses to do.

Its purpose is removing prompts, not adding safety or value beyond that. For a user already in auto or bypass mode, Jev's main possible value (a risk second opinion) would need to be reworked to deny or ask, and this code deliberately never does that.

security: No shell exec, telemetry or installer in runtime code. Runtime grep shows only process.env reads and the SDK fetch. Bun.spawn appears only in build/publish/audit scripts.

Key handling is clean: the key comes from env (TYPESAFE_API_KEY) and is sent only as a Bearer header by the SDK. It is never in argv or tool args. The docs say not to put credentials in tool parameters. src/index.ts sets logLevel off. Errors keep the provider error code but do not echo the full body (README).
providerFetch rewrites only for exact origins and paths (openrouter.ai, opencode.ai, ai-gateway.vercel.sh, api.cloudflare.com). Non-OK responses are passed through unmodified.

Prompt-injection surface: any content sent to Jev is untrusted data, and Jev is reported to be movable by injected instructions in state. Tool outputs are numeric or label only, with no free text. The main risk is a model treating a probability as permission. SKILL.md says 'Confidence is not proof or action permission'. MCP tool annotations are readOnlyHint true and openWorldHint true.

Supply chain: 3 runtime deps pinned exactly (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0, @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0 with npm provenance attestation, zod 4.6.5). bun.lock exists, CI uses --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts. The release branch ships an 800 KB prebuilt bundle with CHECKSUMS.sha256 and third-party-notices. I did not audit the bundle itself, only the source. The repo is 8 days old with 1 author, so the trust surface is a single new maintainer. Pin a release commit.
Installation for Claude Code is manual: clone or vendor the release branch and add an .mcp.json entry with command bun. Do not use the Codex marketplace commands.
gh-nshcr-jevs.dataEgress: Whatever the model puts in `content`, `question`, options and levels goes to https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (and on to TypeSafe via OpenRouter), together with the Bearer key and model name. Only agent-selected content is sent, and only when a tool is called. Nothing is sent automatically, and jev_guide and startup make no network call. For client projects the model can pass source code, diffs or commands as `content`, so this needs a policy. OpenRouter/TypeSafe retention terms apply. The README claims the service does not persist input, but that is unverified. The README says a timeout or cancellation does not mean the remote side did not run or bill.
gh-nshcr-jevs.failureMode: Tool-level fail-visible and never fail-open into a decision. Errors return isError with JSON {error:{code,action,retry}} (src/errors.ts). Codes seen: NOT_CONFIGURED (missing key or bad base URL), INVALID_REQUEST, INVALID_RESPONSE. The SKILL says never to treat an error as a negative judgment. The SDK timeout is 30 s per attempt (src/index.ts:19) with SDK default retries, so worst-case latency is well above 30 s when OpenRouter is down. The local scheduler admits 4 concurrent requests, queues 32, and rejects after a 1000 ms queue wait. A missing key does not crash the server: it starts, and tools error on first call. Startup errors give exit code 1 with a generic message. Since there is no hook, a failure just yields a tool error in the transcript and never blocks Claude Code.
gh-nshcr-jevs.contextCost: 7 tools. An estimate from the source, not measured: tool descriptions total about 2.3k chars, plus JSON schemas for five nested tools (item arrays with options/levels and descriptions) of roughly 10-14k chars, so about 3-4k tokens of tool definitions. Server instructions are about 640 chars (about 160 tokens). The skill jev-mcp is small (description about 170 chars; body 4.3 KB loaded only on trigger). Guide resources add about 22 KB but are read on demand. In Claude Code, MCP tools are deferred behind ToolSearch, so the resident cost is names plus instructions, and the full schema loads when used. There is no hook-injected text. Skill listing budget 0.02 is barely affected (one skill).
gh-nshcr-jevs.latencyImpact: Zero on non-Jev turns, since there is no hook. Each call is one HTTP round trip: Jev p50 about 200 ms, p95 about 600 ms per the brief, plus about 100-300 ms Bun cold start on first MCP connect. It does not fit as a synchronous gate on every tool call because there is no hook. assess_batch makes one upstream request per record (32 records at concurrency 4 means about 8 sequential waves). Worst case is 30 s timeout multiplied by SDK retries.
gh-nshcr-jevs.autoInvocation: model-discretion MCP tool plus a model-discretion skill (jev-mcp). MCP server instructions tell the model to use the tools for focused judgments, but nothing forces or triggers it. There is no hook, so 'automatically whenever it adds value' depends on the model choosing it, and the user would likely still have to nudge it, or add a CLAUDE.md rule or their own PermissionRequest/PreToolUse hook. It can be layered under a separate hook script (the cookbook pattern) but does not provide one.
pros: Real OpenRouter adapter in code: rewrites to /api/alpha/decisions, filters the typesafe/jev- catalog, sets the default model typesafe/jev-1.13, and rejects the null inputs OpenRouter disallows (src/provider.ts). Setup is env-only: TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api plus a key mapping.
Clean key handling (env only, Bearer header, never argv or tool args), no shell exec or telemetry in runtime code, exact-pinned deps, SDK with npm provenance.

Broadest generic tool surface: classify/score/check/assess_structure/assess_batch cover Choice, Score and Noul. It has concurrency limits (4 in flight, queue 32, 1 s queue timeout), strict zod validation and response-contract checks that turn malformed responses into INVALID_RESPONSE instead of fake numbers.
Well written caller guidance (SKILL.md and jev_guide) that tells the model not to treat probabilities as permission or errors as negatives, which suits a discretionary-use tool.
Fail-visible tool errors with structured retry hints. No blocking behaviour in Claude Code sessions. Prebuilt dist on the release branch means no npm install at runtime (Bun only).
MIT licence. About 47 test cases across 11 files, plus audit and governance scripts and CI on ubuntu and macos.
cons: OpenRouter path is untested live. The author's own docs say 'mock adapter tests only; not really called', and the /alpha endpoint has no SLA. The assumption that the SDK's TypeSafe-shaped body/response matches alpha/decisions is unverified by the author.
No hook and no permission-gating logic. It gives the model a tool but not automatic use, which misses the user's core goal. Nothing implements the cookbook PermissionRequest flow.

Requires Bun >= 1.4.2 (package.json engines), which is not in the user's stack (Node 24). Install is Codex-oriented (marketplace commands, .codex-plugin/plugin.json, env_vars key which is Codex-specific), so Claude Code needs a hand-written .mcp.json and a cloned release commit.

Env var name is hard-coded to TYPESAFE_API_KEY, so OPENROUTER_API_KEY needs the ${VAR} mapping. The mapped key is then in the MCP child env, which is exposure to consider alongside the no-secret-leak hook's protected-vars list.
Brand-new and tiny: created 2026-09-22, 10 commits, 1 contributor, 0 stars, 0 forks, no releases, no topics or description. Docs and code comments are largely Chinese. Version 0.1.3.

Model-chosen content leaves the machine to OpenRouter/TypeSafe with no redaction or size guard in the server. Client-project code could be sent by discretion. Independent evals say Jev is overconfident on unanswerable inputs and can be swayed by injected instructions in state.
Worst-case latency is unbounded-ish (30 s timeout times SDK retries). assess_batch sends N requests, and 32k context limits mean no large diffs.
Tool schemas are heavy for occasional use (about 3-4k tokens estimated when loaded) relative to a single-purpose Noul gate.
gh-nshcr-jevs.verdict: This is the cleanest and most configurable Jev MCP server, and OpenRouter works by env config alone (TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api, key mapped to TYPESAFE_API_KEY). But it is only a discretionary tool with no hook, its OpenRouter path has never been called live, and it needs Bun plus a hand-made Claude Code config. It is useful as the Jev tool layer under a separate PermissionRequest/PreToolUse hook, but on its own it does not deliver automatic use. Pin a reviewed release commit and add a data-egress rule for client repos.
