gh-greghavens-jev-scope-control.name: greghavens/jev-scope-control
gh-greghavens-jev-scope-control.whatItDoes: A single ~2270-line stdlib-only Python script (jev-scope-control) installed as a Claude Code plugin PreToolUse command hook (timeout 15s). It skips read-only tools and provably read-only shell commands in code. For Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit, non-trivial Bash, subagent launches (Agent/Task) and unknown tools such as MCP tools, it rebuilds the user's latest request, conversation and recent actions from the transcript. It sends them to the TypeSafe System One endpoint (POST {base}/v1/systemone). Bash commands first get a cheap read/write Noul. Everything then goes through a gate question (deny bar 0.35), then a full battery of scope Nouls composed in code, with deny above 0.65. A deny returns permissionDecision "deny" plus a reason telling the model to tell the user and not retry. Results are cached for 600s. A denied call stays denied for the same user request. Logs go to ~/.jev-scope-control/log.jsonl. There is no README, only design/jev-scope-control-design.md. The repo also ships Codex, pi and opencode shims.

Line 2090 posts {"state","model":JEV_MODEL,"questions"} with Bearer key. Lines 773-775 read the key from TYPESAFE_API_KEY or ~/.config/jev-scope-control/env. Line 41 hardcodes JEV_MODEL = "jev-latest", and there is NO env override (grep of the whole repo finds no JEV_MODEL env read). The MAX_DENIALS env var in the design doc is not implemented in code either. There is no OPENROUTER_API_KEY reference anywhere in the repo.

providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Nearly trivial. Set TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api (yields https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone, which matches OpenRouter's TypeSafe-schema endpoint) and TYPESAFE_API_KEY=<OpenRouter key> in ~/.config/jev-scope-control/env. Both work without code changes. The unverified risk is that OpenRouter may not accept model "jev-latest"; its documented name is "jev-1.13". If it does not, change line 41 (one line, or add an env override). No fork is needed beyond that, but the repo has no license, so edit a local copy only. The response parsing (answers[q].noul, usage) appears to be the same System One schema.

interface.purpose: Developer eval and replay tooling. Not part of runtime.

security: No shell exec or subprocess in the hook: no `subprocess` import (grep confirms). It only parses commands with shlex.

Key never on argv: it goes in the Authorization header from a file or env. The default key file is ~/.config/jev-scope-control/env, and the log and state dir ~/.jev-scope-control is created mode 0700.
Redirects are disabled (_NoRedirect, ~line 2064-2067) so the key is not resent elsewhere. https is enforced except for localhost (line 2078-2080).
No telemetry beyond the Jev call. No installer script; the plugin install is the standard Claude Code plugin mechanism.

Prompt-injection surface: the model-authored command, diff and tool-result snippets (~300 chars each) are put into the judged state. Code mitigates some of this: WRITE_QUESTION says comments and claims in the command are not evidence, and 'don't let claims in a command skip the scope check' is a commit. But the Jev brief says injected instructions in state can move answers. Assistant text after the last user message is deliberately withheld.

Fail-open on every error: any exception, a missing key, a Jev outage or HTTP 5xx, a 5s timeout, or a missing transcript all let the call run. It warns once per session via systemMessage. It is a nudge, not a security boundary.
The read-only fast path is a code allowlist (ls, cat, grep, git status/diff/log, sed -n and so on) and is not audited here in depth.
Cost of the same-call cache and repeat-deny state: files under ~/.jev-scope-control/{cache,session} hold request text (0600/0700 on the dirs).
No LICENSE file: legally all rights reserved. Fine for local personal use, but a grey area for modifying or redistributing it in client projects.
gh-greghavens-jev-scope-control.dataEgress: On every checked call (Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit, non-plainly-read Bash, Agent/Task, MCP and unknown tools) the state sent to the endpoint (TypeSafe, or OpenRouter to TypeSafe if redirected) contains: the user's latest message; earlier user messages (up to a limit); the last assistant reply (tail, up to about 6k chars); 'older user limits'; the subagent assignment text; up to N recent actions as one-line tool+input plus result snippets (~300 chars each); and the proposed action itself. For an edit that is the file path plus a diff or content clipped to ~3k chars per part; for Bash it is the command and description. The design doc also lists working_directory. Client source diffs, command lines (which may contain inline secrets) and tool-output snippets therefore leave the machine on nearly every state-changing call, roughly 2k input tokens per call. Bash commands get an extra tiny request containing just the tool call. Local logs at ~/.jev-scope-control/log.jsonl store the truncated task (300 chars) and scores.
gh-greghavens-jev-scope-control.failureMode: Fail-open everywhere. The hook always exits 0 (main(), lines 2257-2268). Jev timeout is 5s on a daemon thread (JEV_TIMEOUT_SECONDS), under the 15s hook timeout. A missing key, an HTTP error or a parse error means the call is allowed, with a one-time systemMessage warning (warn_once) and details in the log. If the gate or write question errors, it falls to risk=1.0 or writes=1.0 and proceeds to the full check; if the full check errors, it allows. Design-doc caveat: the documented 3-denial cap (JEV_SCOPE_CONTROL_MAX_DENIALS) is not in the code. Instead, an identical denied call stays denied for the same user request (run(), lines ~2196-2214). A false positive therefore costs a turn, and the model is told to ask the user, so the user's next message resets it. Denials are not hard-capped, so a misjudging Jev can repeatedly block different calls.
gh-greghavens-jev-scope-control.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no skills, so no tool-def or skill-listing budget cost. No additionalContext injection. The only model-visible text is the deny reason (~100 tokens) and a systemMessage. The plugin adds no per-turn context.
gh-greghavens-jev-scope-control.autoInvocation: Fully deterministic PreToolUse hook. It fires automatically on every tool call, is gated in code, and does not depend on the model choosing to call anything. It also fires in bypassPermissions/auto mode, because a hook deny overrides the permission mode. It covers subagent calls too (agent_id handling).
gh-greghavens-jev-scope-control.latencyImpact: The design doc reports 0.2-0.25s per checked call at ~1.9-2.1k input tokens on the TypeSafe direct endpoint. Bash commands that are not obviously read-only pay an extra write-question round trip; gate-then-full pays a second call only for suspect calls. Python startup plus transcript parse adds about 50-100ms. Reads and greps are free (skipped in code). A 5s worst case applies on an outage. Every Edit, Write and non-trivial Bash in a long session pays this, and it stacks with the existing gitnexus Bash hook. It is likely 0.3-0.8s through OpenRouter, given p95 of ~600ms. No cache is reused across different calls.
pros: Targets a real gap for a user in auto and bypassPermissions modes: it catches unrequested commits, pushes, deploys and out-of-scope edits (Bash, Edit, Write, MCP) that no static regex hook catches, and it is a deterministic hook, so the user never has to say 'use jev'.

Design is thoughtful and evidence-backed: gating in code (read-only tools and commands never hit the network), a two-stage gate/full check with composed decision scores, a 600s result cache, repeat-deny memory, subagent assignment handling, and tuning against 798 real sessions (1.1% denied, 1 known wrong denial). Docs claim 360/360 and 525/525 on labeled cases. Self-reported and not independently verified.

Low blast radius on failure: stdlib-only, fail-open with a one-time warning, no shell exec, key in a header (not argv) with redirects disabled and https enforced. Runs are logged to a 0700 dir. Zero MCP or context cost.
OpenRouter path is nearly free: the request is the exact System One schema, base URL and key are env-configurable, and the endpoint path matches OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone.
Sizeable test suite: 45 hook unit tests with a mock Jev server in test_hook.py, 5 e2e tests, 72 labeled scenario cases plus large probe and scenario JSON, and a real `claude -p` e2e script.
cons: Brand-new alpha: created 2026-09-29 (repo age about 1 day, 15 commits, 1 contributor, 0 stars, 0 forks, no release). It has no README and no LICENSE. The docs and code already drift: the design doc's JEV_SCOPE_CONTROL_MAX_DENIALS cap and the triage's JEV_MODEL override do not exist in the code.

Not OpenRouter-native: the model is hardcoded to "jev-latest" (line 41), not the documented "jev-1.13". OpenRouter may reject it, so a one-line local patch may be needed. The key variable is TYPESAFE_API_KEY, so an OpenRouter key would be stored in a second place (~/.config/jev-scope-control/env), not read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

Heavy data egress: user messages, assistant text, diffs and command snippets (possibly client code and secrets inside commands) go to a third party on almost every state-changing call. This is a real problem for client projects. Nothing redacts secrets before sending, and no-secret-leak.cjs does not cover it.

Fail-open with no hard denial cap and tuned thresholds. On an OpenRouter outage or missing key it silently stops checking (one warning per session). Independent evals say calibration is imperfect and injected text in state can sway answers, so it cannot be relied on as a security control. Known wrong denials and near-bar misses are acknowledged in the docs. In bypass mode a wrong denial is a new friction, and an `Agent` launch or unknown MCP call is also gated.

Overlaps with Claude Code's own auto-mode classifier and permissions, and adds per-edit latency (0.2-0.8s per Edit/Write/Bash, more through OpenRouter's alpha endpoint with no SLA) on top of the gitnexus Bash hook.

Depends on the transcript format: it reads transcript_path and waits up to 2s for the call to appear in it, so a Claude Code JSONL format change would silently degrade context, and it would fail open.
gh-greghavens-jev-scope-control.verdict: The most relevant and best-engineered candidate for guarding auto and bypass sessions: it fires deterministically and has a real design and test story. But it is a one-day-old, unlicensed, single-author alpha that is TypeSafe-only (hardcoded model "jev-latest", TYPESAFE_API_KEY). It needs a base-URL env plus probably a one-line model patch for OpenRouter, and it sends diffs and transcript text to a third party on every state-changing call, which is a real concern for client work. Trial it on personal projects after pinning a commit, patching the model, and adding OPENROUTER/TYPESAFE keys to the no-secret-leak list.

gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.name: yanmad27/ask-jev
gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.whatItDoes: Claude Code plugin (hooks.json, zero npm deps, Node ESM) that calls Jev via POST {state, model, questions} to a systemone endpoint. Hooks: (1) PreToolUse AskUserQuestion auto-answers questions via deny+reason when confident (>=0.8, non-destructive, grounded); (2) PreToolUse "*" permission gate that fast-allows a static read-only tool list and otherwise asks Jev safe+destructive Noul questions, each with an auto-generated mirror (null-hypothesis) twin reconciled toward the safe side, then returns permissionDecision allow/ask; (3) PostToolUse Bash result classifier that injects additionalContext when the outcome is not success at p>=0.8; (4) Stop gate that blocks at p>=0.85 for incomplete work and, in full autonomy, auto-answers the assistant's closing question and re-prompts (max 3); (5) UserPromptSubmit that injects a reminder each turn plus a literal/ambiguous prompt judgement; (6) SessionStart that injects a rule block and self-registers an AskUserQuestion hook into ~/.claude/settings.json. Also bin/jev.mjs CLI (stdin JSON -> raw answers, plus stats), a skill ask-jev, a stats log at ~/.claude/ask-jev.log, and a Paseo plugin. State sent to Jev is built from the transcript, CLAUDE.md, memory, git diff, and the permission lists.

providerSupport.evidence: lib/jev.mjs:9-12 PROVIDERS: typesafe = https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, model jev-latest, key env TYPESAFE_API_KEY; vercel = ai-gateway.vercel.sh legacy. lib/jev.mjs:117-119 endpoint() honors ASK_JEV_API_URL (or ASK_JEV_GATEWAY_URL) and ASK_JEV_MODEL. lib/jev.mjs:126-144 apiKey() reads ASK_JEV_API_KEY first, then TYPESAFE_API_KEY, AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, then ~/.claude/ask-jev.key. lib/jev.mjs:170-185 body for the non-vercel path is {state, model, questions} with booleans mapped to type noul, Bearer auth, and answers read from json.answers[k].noul (lib/jev.mjs:150-157,205). OPENROUTER_API_KEY is never read.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: No code patch needed if OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone matches TypeSafe's schema (as the brief says). Set ASK_JEV_API_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone, ASK_JEV_MODEL=jev-1.13 and ASK_JEV_API_KEY=<OpenRouter key> in the settings.json env block or a launcher. The provider auto-detects as typesafe since the key is not vck_. Alternatively put the OpenRouter key in ~/.claude/ask-jev.key. Remaining risk: response-shape parity (noul field, probabilities/choice) is not verified against OpenRouter here. The 70k-char state cap (context.mjs:10) is sized for a 32k token limit, which matches OpenRouter's 32k context.
providerSupport.others: Vercel AI Gateway (legacy, vck_ keys, ai-evaluation-model spec v4)

interface.name: PreToolUse AskUserQuestion -> hooks/ask-jev.mjs (10s timeout)
interface.purpose: Sends the question and options to Jev, denies the tool with the reason carrying the answer when confident (default ASK_JEV_ASK_THRESHOLD 0.8). Stands down under PASEO_AGENT_ID and when no key is set. Deduplicates via a tmp lock file.

interface.name: PreToolUse * -> hooks/gates/permission.mjs (6s timeout, 4s Jev budget)
interface.purpose: Returns allow (read-only fast path or Jev-judged) or ask. Skips itself when permission_mode is bypassPermissions (permission.mjs:21). Default autonomy is full, so allow threshold is 0.8, and if destructive p < 0.3 it allows even when safe p is below threshold (gate.mjs decidePermission). Destructive p >= 0.6 or missing always asks.

interface.name: PostToolUse Bash -> hooks/gates/bash.mjs (6s)
interface.purpose: Classifies command outcome (success, error, tests_failed, needs_attention) and injects a one-line additionalContext when it is not success at p>=0.8.

interface.name: PostToolUse AskUserQuestion -> hooks/ask-jev-answer.mjs (5s)
interface.purpose: Records which answer the user chose, for stats.

interface.name: Stop -> hooks/gates/stop.mjs (16s timeout)
interface.purpose: Blocks stopping at incomplete p>=0.85. In full autonomy also detects a closing question and, if Jev chooses yes_proceed at >=0.8, blocks with 'Jev answered your question: proceed', capped at 3 consecutive per session.

interface.name: UserPromptSubmit -> hooks/gates/prompt.mjs (6s)
interface.purpose: Injects a REMINDER (~1.2k chars) each turn unless ASK_JEV_REMIND=0, and judges prompt ambiguity (skipped for prompts under 12 chars or starting with /). Full mode injects 'proceed on assumption, do not ask'.

interface.name: SessionStart -> hooks/self-register.mjs and hooks/session-start.mjs (5s each)
interface.purpose: self-register.mjs writes a PreToolUse AskUserQuestion entry into ~/.claude/settings.json (silent on errors, rewrites path each session). session-start.mjs injects a rules block as additionalContext if a key exists.

interface.name: CLI bin/jev.mjs
interface.purpose: echo '{state,questions}' | node bin/jev.mjs returns raw answers. Also has a stats subcommand. bin/jev-eval.mjs replays logged decisions.

interface.name: Skill skills/ask-jev/SKILL.md
interface.purpose: Instructs Claude to consult Jev for judgement calls through the CLI. The description is a long trigger sentence.

interface.name: Env config
interface.purpose: ASK_JEV_AUTONOMY (full|safe, default full), ASK_JEV_GATES (default permission,stop,bash,prompt), ASK_JEV_ALLOW_THRESHOLD, ASK_JEV_ASK_THRESHOLD, ASK_JEV_STATE_CHARS, ASK_JEV_REMIND, ASK_JEV_LOG(_FILE), ASK_JEV_API_URL, ASK_JEV_MODEL, ASK_JEV_API_KEY, ASK_JEV_PROVIDER.

gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.license: None (GitHub licenseInfo null and no LICENSE file in tree), so all rights reserved by default
gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.runtime: Node >=18 ESM, zero dependencies (fetch, fs, child_process only; git executed via execFileSync with a 1s timeout)
gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.install: /plugin marketplace add yanmad27/ask-jev; /plugin install ask-jev@ask-jev; then a key in TYPESAFE_API_KEY, ASK_JEV_API_KEY or ~/.claude/ask-jev.key. For OpenRouter also set ASK_JEV_API_URL and ASK_JEV_MODEL. Hook commands use node from PATH, so the user's overridden PATH must include node, or a wrapper is needed. Plugin hooks use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}.
gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.tests: 12 files: 8 node:test files under hooks/*.test.mjs (about 1.5k lines; gates, context, autonomy, answer-policy, lint, reconcile), 1 shell test, and a Paseo TS test; CI runs node --check, manifest JSON validation, unit tests, and a hook-contract smoke test. Behavior evals (evals/*, evals.yml) exist. No live-API integration test, and release-please is automated.
security: Key handling is good: the key goes in the Authorization header via fetch, never in argv. It is read from env or ~/.claude/ask-jev.key, and there is no shell exec of user data. Only fixed git commands run through execFileSync (context.mjs:270; jev.mjs:61 execSync of a fixed 'git config --get remote.origin.url' string).
The key file is not created by the plugin and no telemetry endpoint exists. The only fetch is in lib/jev.mjs:172, to the configured URL.

self-register.mjs rewrites ~/.claude/settings.json on every SessionStart (line 43-63) to insert a PreToolUse hook pointing at the plugin cache path. It reformats the file with JSON.stringify and could clobber comments or ordering, and it is a persistent side-effect outside the plugin sandbox. It is justified in-code by claude-code#36397, which may be stale on 2.1.285. It also produces duplicate hooks, mitigated by a lock file.

Prompt-injection surface: the whole transcript, tool results (300 chars each), file diffs, CLAUDE.md and memory go into Jev's state. The permission gate turns Jev's probability into an allow that bypasses the user prompt. An injected instruction in a fetched page or file could raise p(safe) or lower p(destructive), and the brief notes injected state can move answers. The mirror/twin reconcile reduces but does not remove this. Allow is issued from PreToolUse, so it skips the permission dialog but should not override deny rules or the existing no-secret-leak hook's deny.

Default autonomy=full is aggressive: allow at destructive<0.3 even if safe<0.8, the stop gate auto-answers the assistant's own question and continues (up to 3 times), and the prompt gate injects 'do not ask, state assumptions and proceed'. This conflicts with a cautious posture on client projects.

Sensitive-file redaction is only for git diff hunks (SENSITIVE_PATH regex .env/.pem/.key/secret, context.mjs:254). Transcript text, CLAUDE.md and memory are sent verbatim, so any secret pasted or printed in the conversation reaches the provider. The tool-result cap is 300 chars.

Reads ~/.claude/settings*.json permission lists, memory and plans; logs commands (4,000 chars) and the repo remote URL (userinfo stripped) to ~/.claude/ask-jev.log. This log is plain text with no rotation, and a command containing a secret would be persisted there.
No license means unclear legal reuse, especially for client work. An unpinned marketplace install auto-updates from a 12-day-old, single-maintainer repo (supply-chain trust).
gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.dataEgress: On every non-read-only tool call (Bash, Edit, Write, MultiEdit, Agent, MCP write tools), each Stop, each UserPromptSubmit of 12 or more chars, and each Bash PostToolUse, it POSTs up to 70,000 chars of state to the configured endpoint. State comprises: CLAUDE.md files (project, user, memory; 8k budget), recent conversation turns and the last user messages, session_summary, the todo/plan file (4k), the action (full Bash command up to 4k; Edit/Write before/after contents up to 4k each; the final assistant message), git status, diff (6k, redacted for sensitive filenames) and ls-files (60 files), the allow/deny lists from settings.json, the cwd, and the plugin's own past decision log. It goes to api.typesafe.ai by default, or to OpenRouter once ASK_JEV_API_URL is set. This is much broader than the cookbook's two-question Bash-command-only check. Locally it writes ~/.claude/ask-jev.log and tmp lock/count files.
gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.failureMode: Mostly fail-open to the normal flow. Network error, 4xx, timeout, or a missing key all result in the hook printing nothing (`.catch(() => null)` / `main().catch(() => {})`), so Claude Code falls through to its normal permission prompt, the Stop proceeds, and the question reaches the user. The client retries 5xx/429 with backoff inside a 4s budget (jev.mjs:278-303), and the hooks.json timeouts exceed the budgets (6s vs 4s; the stop gate at 16s for up to 3 sequential 4s calls plus margin). A hook killed by timeout is also non-blocking. The safe-side asymmetry is real: the destructive floor at 0.6, mirror reconcile pulling toward the safe side, and undefined p means ask. The unsafe direction is when Jev returns confident-but-wrong (overconfident, per independent evals): a wrong allow silently skips a prompt, and a wrong stop block or auto-continue only costs a turn. Disagreement is not a loud failure, and the only trace is the log file. Skips the permission gate in bypassPermissions, but the ask, stop, prompt and bash gates still run in bypass sessions.
gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.latencyImpact: Adds 1 network call (p50 ~200ms, p95 ~600ms per the brief; the author's own log shows p90 about 1.5s for first-try success and 18% 503s on the Vercel path) to every non-read-only tool call in auto mode. Worst case is a 4s budget with a 6s hook timeout. Also 1 call at each prompt submit, 1 at each Stop (up to 3 sequential in full autonomy when the message ends in a question), and 1 after each Bash. That is roughly 2-4 Jev calls per turn in a busy session, plus ~1.2s Node startup overhead on top of the existing gitnexus hooks (PreToolUse runs in parallel, so wall clock is max not sum). PostToolUse Bash adds latency for every command even though it rarely produces output. Cost is negligible ($0.042/M input, and 70k chars is about 17k tokens max, so <$0.001 per call), though thousands of calls per day of large state are non-trivial for volume.
gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.contextCost: Zero MCP tools. The skill listing is one skill whose description is about 400 chars (~100 tokens, well under the 0.02 budget). SessionStart injects a rules block (~1.7k chars, ~430 tokens) once per session, and UserPromptSubmit injects the REMINDER (~1.1k chars, ~280 tokens) on EVERY user prompt unless ASK_JEV_REMIND=0, plus a one-line Jev directive in full mode. That is cumulative and it competes with the caveman additionalContext. The PostToolUse Bash hook adds a short line only when a command is judged not-success. The Stop hook's block reasons re-enter context as a new turn. Recommend REMIND=0 to remove the per-turn cost.
gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.autoInvocation: Deterministic hooks: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart fire automatically with no need to say 'use jev', which is exactly the user's goal. The skill and CLI path is model-driven and opt-in by reminder text. There are no MCP tools, so nothing for the model to forget to call.
pros: Fully automatic via hooks with no 'use jev' prompting (hooks/hooks.json), and covers AskUserQuestion auto-answering, permission gating, a Stop gate and Bash result classification in one plugin.

Endpoint and model are overridable (jev.mjs:117-119, ASK_JEV_API_URL/ASK_JEV_MODEL) and the wire format is the same TypeSafe systemone schema OpenRouter exposes, so it can be pointed at openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone with jev-1.13 with a settings.json env change and no code patch.

Better-than-cookbook safety design: static read-only fast-allow with no network, dual safe and destructive Noul questions with a 0.6 destructive floor, mirror/null-hypothesis twin questions reconciled toward the safe side (jev.mjs:247-261), and detailed destructive/reversible criteria (gate.mjs) that include credential exfiltration and ~/.claude/settings edits.
Fail-open-to-prompt on all errors, with timeouts budgeted below hooks.json timeouts. Self-skips the permission gate in bypassPermissions. Missing key means the plugin does nothing.

Zero dependencies, and the source is readable and heavily commented. 8 unit test files (~1.5k lines), CI, behavior evals, release-please, and an auditable decision log with a stats CLI. Active development (73 commits in 12 days, v1.5.0) and it reads user allow/deny lists to avoid flagging allow-listed commands.
Secret-aware diff redaction, and the git remote URL has the token stripped before logging.
cons: Default ASK_JEV_AUTONOMY=full allows any tool with destructive p<0.3 even when p(safe) is under threshold, auto-answers the assistant's own questions in the Stop gate, and injects 'do not ask, proceed on assumptions' every prompt. This deviates from the cookbook's allow-only-if-both>=0.9 and from the candidate summary, which mis-states the default. Must be set to ASK_JEV_AUTONOMY=safe for parity, and even then the allow threshold is 0.9 on safe only.

Matcher '*' on PreToolUse fires on every non-read-only tool including Edit, Write, Agent and MCP calls, adding a network round trip each time and sending Write/Edit contents and a 70k-char state to a third party each time. That is a wide egress surface for client projects, with the secret redaction covering git diffs only.

Allow comes from PreToolUse, which skips the prompt (auto mode's classifier and user prompt), so an overconfident or injected Jev wrongly approves silently. No PermissionRequest integration that would leave the normal prompt as the fallback, unlike the cookbook design.

self-register.mjs mutates ~/.claude/settings.json on each SessionStart based on a claude-code#36397 workaround that may be obsolete on 2.1.285 and creates duplicate AskUserQuestion hooks. It also conflicts with a hand-managed settings.json.
Per-turn UserPromptSubmit reminder and an extra Jev call per prompt/Stop/Bash-result add latency and context that the user likely doesn't want. The bash and prompt gates are low value.

No license, 0 stars, 12 days old, single maintainer, Vietnamese-language code comments; no OpenRouter mention and OPENROUTER_API_KEY is never read (needs ASK_JEV_API_KEY duplication), so the key must be duplicated into a key file or env, and the existing no-secret-leak hook's protected-var list should cover ASK_JEV_API_KEY as well. Hook commands use bare 'node', which needs the user's PATH.
Independent Jev caveats (overconfidence on unanswerable inputs, prompt injection sensitivity, /alpha no SLA) apply to a plugin whose main effect is turning probabilities into auto-approval.
gh-yanmad27-ask-jev.verdict: Closest existing match to 'Claude Code uses Jev automatically': deterministic hooks, OpenRouter-switchable via ASK_JEV_API_URL/ASK_JEV_MODEL/ASK_JEV_API_KEY with no code change, a safer-than-cookbook decision design, fail-open behavior and real tests. But it ships a too-permissive default (autonomy=full), a wide '*' PreToolUse egress of up to 70k chars per call, a settings.json-mutating self-register, and no license. Adopt only as a reference or a fork/pinned vendor copy, configured with ASK_JEV_AUTONOMY=safe, ASK_JEV_GATES=permission (and maybe stop), REMIND=0, and a narrowed matcher (Bash), rather than installing as-is.

gh-jevcomp-jevcomp.name: jevcomp/jevcomp
gh-jevcomp-jevcomp.whatItDoes: Replaces Claude Code's model-written compaction summary. A plugin function hook (session.compact, early-access, needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1) shells out to node dist/cli.js claude-compact with the transcript on stdin. For each completed tool call, Jev gets two Noul questions (drop_<id>, truncate_<id>: would deleting or shortening lose needed info). Outputs with risk below 0.5 are dropped or cut to 300 chars, and user/assistant text stays verbatim. It falls back to native compaction on any error, on a reduction under 15%, or when the transcript is unsupported. A SessionStart hook starts a detached local dashboard on 127.0.0.1:43127 and edits ~/.claude/settings.json. It also proxies Codex and Antigravity, which are irrelevant here. This is compaction pruning, not a general Jev decision helper.

providerSupport.evidence: src/provider.ts:24-25 DIRECT_URL=https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone and OPENROUTER_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions. Line 126-133 providerConfig: OpenRouter default model '~typesafe/jev-latest' (env OPENROUTER_JEV_MODEL), URL override OPENROUTER_JEV_URL, and for TypeSafe JEV_BASE_URL and JEV_MODEL. Line 198-202 sends Bearer auth plus an x-openrouter-title header. Key order (94-114): explicit apiKey, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY_FILE, JEVCOMP_KEY_FILE, ~/.config/jevcomp/openrouter_api_key. Request body is {model,state,questions} (line 213). Timeout 20s, 1 retry.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Already native OpenRouter and the default provider in plugin.json userConfig. Only caveat: the model alias is '~typesafe/jev-latest' rather than the pinned 'typesafe/jev-1.13', so pin it with OPENROUTER_JEV_MODEL. The provider is auto-selected TypeSafe-first when both keys exist (resolveProvider, lines 116-124), so set JEVCOMP_PROVIDER=openrouter.
providerSupport.others: Also Codex local proxy (jevcomp codex) and experimental Antigravity MITM proxy (agy-proxy.ts, openssl CA cert). Both are not applicable to this user.

interface.name: hook: SessionStart (startup|resume)
interface.purpose: hooks/hooks.json runs node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/dist/cli.js hook (30s timeout). It binds the audit source, writes CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 into ~/.claude/settings.json if missing (src/hooks.ts:75-91), warns if no API key, spawns the detached dashboard on 127.0.0.1:43127, and returns a systemMessage.

interface.name: function hook module: hooks/claude.js on('session.compact')
interface.purpose: Runs in Claude Code. It skips 'precompute' triggers, spawns `node dist/cli.js claude-compact` with a 300s timeout, sends the transcript, provider and plugin apiKey on stdin, and applies Jev's dropped/truncated ids. On any failure it calls next(e) to get native compaction.

interface.name: CLI: jevcomp install/uninstall/doctor/settings/dashboard/codex/agy/compact/claude-compact/hook/audit
interface.purpose: Setup, diagnostics, settings menu (pin-recent-messages=6, loss-threshold=0.5, min-reduction-ratio=0.15), dashboard, Codex and Antigravity proxies, offline rollout preview, and local decision audit.

interface.name: skill: jevcomp (skills/jevcomp/SKILL.md)
interface.purpose: Setup, doctor, dashboard address and uninstall instructions for the agent. Parts are stale and describe Codex PreCompact/PostCompact hooks that no longer exist (the commit log says Codex hook mode was dropped).

interface.name: local HTTP dashboard
interface.purpose: 127.0.0.1:43127 with /api/health, /api/stats, /api/history and a POST /api/settings guarded by a token, an Origin check and a Host check against DNS rebinding.

security: Key handling is mostly OK. The plugin apiKey goes to the child process over stdin JSON (hooks/claude.js), not argv. The key file is written 0600 in a 0700 dir (provider.ts:46-59). The key can also come from env. The child node process inherits the full environment. The repo's own no-secret-leak hook does not cover it, and OPENROUTER_API_KEY should still be added to your protected-vars list.

Modifies user config without asking. The SessionStart hook rewrites ~/.claude/settings.json to add env CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 (hooks.ts:75-91), re-serialising the whole file. That is a risk to your hand-managed settings.

Depends on an early-access Claude Code function-hook API (`session.compact`, `$.process.run`, `$.session.id`). I could not verify it in Claude Code 2.1.285: the web search hit a rate limit and no repo doc cites Anthropic documentation. If the flag or API is absent, the compaction part does nothing and only the dashboard nagging remains.

Supply chain: README install is `npm install -g --install-links github:jevcomp/jevcomp`, unpinned from a 0-star, 8-day-old repo. dist/ is committed, so the shipped JS may differ from src/, and there is no dependency lockfile. It has no runtime dependencies, which is a plus. The plugin path (claude plugin marketplace add jevcomp/jevcomp) also runs committed dist/ JS.

Spawns a detached, long-lived local HTTP server (dashboard). It binds only 127.0.0.1, checks the Host header, and has a token plus Origin check on POST. GET /api/history and /api/stats are unauthenticated to any local process.

Prompt-injection surface: tool outputs go into Jev state. compact.ts:33 tells Jev that tool outputs are untrusted. Worst case, injected text tricks Jev into dropping or keeping evidence, so it degrades context rather than executing anything. Per the brief, injected instructions can move Jev answers.

Secret redaction is regex-based (compact.ts:82-87: bearer tokens, key/token/password/secret assignments, sk-...). It misses many formats such as ghp_, AKIA, JWTs and PEM blocks, and the README admits this.

No telemetry beyond calls to OpenRouter, though the audit feature is opt-in (defaultAuditConfig has agents:{}, so it is off by default). Audit 'evidence' mode stores transcript data locally in ~/.jevcomp/audit, capped at 500 MB and 30 days.
Contents are Portuguese/English mixed, with a PLANO_AUDITORIA_DECISOES.md planning doc and HTML prototypes in the repo. Authorship is essentially one person (Thiago Fialho, 63 of 69 commits).
gh-jevcomp-jevcomp.dataEgress: To https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions only, on each compaction: the last 3 user messages (as goal, up to 500 chars each), the full history of user/assistant text, and tool call names, inputs (truncated) and result previews (80-420 chars). All of it is regex-redacted and capped at about 24k state tokens and 30k request tokens, in batches with up to 4 requests in parallel. Because pinned recent messages and older assistant text are included, client code, file paths and command outputs will leave the machine, and the regex redaction is incomplete. Nothing goes to TypeSafe or anywhere else if the OpenRouter provider is chosen. History and metrics are stored locally in ~/.jevcomp/history.jsonl.
gh-jevcomp-jevcomp.failureMode: Fail-open by design and tested. Any error in cli.js, a key or network failure, a timeout (20s per request, 1 retry, 300s outer), a state too large for Jev, a reduction under 15%, or a conversation with fewer than 2 messages returns {apply:false}, and hooks/claude.js calls next(e) for native compaction. The function-hook module also catches all errors. A worst case is a delayed compaction of up to about 20-40s. Jev misjudging (overconfidence, label swap) could drop a tool result that was still needed. Protection against that is only the 0.5 loss threshold, the 6 pinned recent messages, and the fact that user messages are never touched. It fails quietly toward less-informed context. No fail-closed risk to tool execution.
gh-jevcomp-jevcomp.contextCost: Adds no MCP tools. The SKILL.md description is about 190 chars (about 50 tokens) against a listing budget of 0.02, so negligible. The SessionStart hook only emits a short systemMessage, and it stays silent when everything is configured. It injects no additionalContext. Compaction output is verbatim conversation minus dropped or shortened tool results, and it removes the summary request. The saving is real but only when compaction triggers.
gh-jevcomp-jevcomp.autoInvocation: Fully automatic and deterministic, and it needs no prompting: the session.compact function hook fires on every auto or manual compaction (except 'precompute' triggers, which are skipped). It does nothing else during coding, so it is not a general 'use Jev when useful' integration. It is one narrow decision point (which old tool outputs to keep at compaction) and adds no per-tool-call value.
gh-jevcomp-jevcomp.latencyImpact: Only at compaction: a node spawn plus several batched OpenRouter calls (about 200-600 ms p50/p95 each, 4 in parallel, 20s timeout, 1 retry). Expected 1-5s, worst case tens of seconds, and it saves the summary generation call. SessionStart adds a node startup plus dashboard health check (1s fetch timeout) or dashboard spawn (up to 15s on the first start). The hook timeout is 30s, on top of the caveman and gitnexus session cost. There is no per-tool-call latency.
pros: Native OpenRouter support with correct endpoint /api/alpha/decisions, Bearer key, x-openrouter-title header and model/url env overrides (provider.ts:24-25,126-133,198-202). Key via stdin, env or plugin sensitive userConfig, never argv.

Genuinely safe failure mode: every failure path returns to native compaction (hooks/claude.js, claude-compact.ts, cli.ts:294-300). User messages are never removed, recent 6 messages are pinned, and outputs are only kept, shortened or dropped when Jev risk is below 0.5. The prompt tells Jev tool outputs are untrusted data.

Uses Jev well as a typed-decision engine (Noul questions per tool call with criteria), batched and budgeted, with zero third-party runtime dependencies and 2000+ lines of tests using a fake Jev (tests/claude.test.mjs covers registration, settings edit, and cut application).
Fully automatic once installed: no need to prompt 'use jev'. It also saves the summary request, and dropped commands are re-runnable. Dashboard and local audit give observability of what was cut.
cons: Depends on unverified early-access Claude Code function hooks (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS, session.compact, $.process.run). I found no confirmation in Claude Code 2.1.285 docs, since web search was rate-limited. If it is unsupported or changes, the value is zero. The plugin also auto-edits ~/.claude/settings.json without consent (hooks.ts:75-91).

Sends transcript content (user and assistant text, tool inputs and result previews) to OpenRouter's alpha endpoint (no SLA). That is client data for a user with client projects, protected only by an incomplete regex redaction. It needs a client-consent decision.

Value is narrow for this user: it only affects compaction and never helps decide permissions, routing or risk. With a subscription login there is no per-token saving, and Opus 5.5 context loss from Jev's overconfident pruning is a quality risk that is hard to detect (irreproducible outputs, e.g. one-off test failures).

gh-danielhirt-truthsayer.name: danielhirt/truthsayer
gh-danielhirt-truthsayer.whatItDoes: Rust workspace (library crate `truthsayer` + CLI binary `truthsayer`) shipped with a Claude Code plugin. The plugin registers hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse on Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit, PostToolUse *, PostToolUseFailure *, Stop) that pipe the event JSON to `truthsayer hook`. The binary builds a redacted, capped observation (task from transcript, constraints from config, tool input/output, up to 12 earlier calls), sends 1-2 requests of Jev Noul questions ({model,state,questions}) to TypeSafe or OpenRouter /alpha/decisions, applies threshold rules from JSON rubrics in code, and in enforce mode emits deny/ask/additionalContext/block/system messages. Rubrics: edit (changes_behavior, violates_constraint, outside_task), tool-result (failed, relevant, injected_instructions), progress (repeating, momentum), turn-end (claims complete, unverified_claim, needs user). Also has replay/label/report/eval tooling for threshold tuning from recorded JSONL.

Config keys backend/api_key_env/model/endpoint in ~/.config/truthsayer/config.toml (docs/claude-code.md:75-81); model can be overridden to e.g. typesafe/jev-1.13. OpenRouter path is only tested against a local mock HTTP server (http.rs tests l.338,368); the published live eval (evals/runs/2026-09-26-jev/run.json) ran via TypeSafe direct, so the `~typesafe/jev-latest` alias on OpenRouter is unverified by the author.

BOOKKEEPING_TOOLS (TodoWrite, Task*, AskUserQuestion, Plan mode, ToolSearch) skipped (hook.rs:34-45)

security: Key handling: API key read only from env var (hook.rs judge_from l.449-455, http.rs bearer_auth); never on argv and not written to records; the detached log-mode child inherits env. Consequence: OPENROUTER_API_KEY must sit in Claude Code's own environment, so the agent's Bash can read it via env/printenv; add it to no-secret-leak.cjs protected vars (and consider a dedicated low-limit key).

Egress control: project .claude/truthsayer.toml cannot set backend/endpoint/model/api_key_env/timeout; a project file containing them is ignored entirely (docs/claude-code.md:99-101; config.rs test with attacker.test endpoint l.323). Good defense against malicious repos redirecting data.

Shell exec: none of the model output is executed. The only spawn is Command::new(current_exe()) for log-mode background (main.rs:432-459) with fixed args. Shim script only execs TRUTHSAYER_BIN, PATH truthsayer, or ~/.cargo/bin/truthsayer; a PATH-planted binary would run as hook, standard risk.

Installer: cargo install --git HEAD of a 0-star, 11-commit repo, no release/tag, so unaudited supply chain and floating HEAD unless pinned with --rev; Cargo.lock committed and --locked used. No install.sh, no telemetry besides the Jev call, no other network endpoints found in source (grep).

Prompt-injection surface: tool outputs (web pages, files) are fed to Jev as state; injected text can try to suppress the injected_instructions flag (per Jev brief, injected instructions in state can move answers). Since code rules decide and the model only returns probabilities, the blast radius is limited to missed/false flags, not arbitrary actions. Findings returned to Claude are prefixed as automatic, possibly-wrong checks (hook.rs for_claude).

Redaction is regex best effort (sk-*, apikey_, gh tokens, AWS, Slack, Google, JWT, PEM, URL creds, NAME=value with SECRET/TOKEN/PASSWORD/API_KEY etc, Bearer/Basic) and secret files (.env, *.pem, *.key, .netrc, .pgpass) are withheld only when the tool path names them (hook.rs withhold_secret_files). Bash `cat .env` or secrets in code/prose outside those patterns still leave the machine. Authors state redaction is not exhaustive.

Local records: records.jsonl (default ~/.local/state/truthsayer/, 0600, rotate 50 MB x5) stores the full redacted state (prompts, tool inputs, 4000-char outputs), a growing on-disk copy of client code snippets; hook.log 0600.
gh-danielhirt-truthsayer.dataEgress: Per checked event, to OpenRouter (then TypeSafe): current user prompt capped at 2000 chars, configured constraints, tool name and tool input (each string capped 4000 chars, secret-file content withheld), tool output/error capped at 4000 chars (head+tail kept), up to 12 earlier calls in the turn (name/input/output each string capped 200 chars), and at Stop the final assistant message capped 4000 chars; all passed through regex redaction. X-Title: truthsayer header sent. For PostToolUse * this means source code from Read/Grep/Bash output, diffs and command output of client projects are transmitted on essentially every tool call except bookkeeping tools. Mitigation: mode=off in .claude/truthsayer.toml per client project (a project file can lower mode) or globally off and enable per personal project via TRUTHSAYER_MODE. Cost approx $0.00003 per check per README.
gh-danielhirt-truthsayer.failureMode: Fail-open everywhere: any error (missing key, timeout, HTTP error, bad JSON, missing answer, missing binary) prints nothing and exits 0 (hook.rs header, main.rs hook_main, docs/claude-code.md Failures section; shim exits 0 if binary absent). Judge timeout 8000 ms default inside a 15 s hook timeout; HttpJudge retries 429/5xx up to 3 times with 0.8/1.6/3.2 s backoff or retry-after up to 10 s (http.rs:25-27,185-200) but the outer tokio timeout caps total at timeout_ms. Reqwest client timeout 30 s but outer cap dominates. Enforce-mode false positives are the real failure: edit rule violates_constraint >=0.7 denies edits, uncertain (0.3-0.7) asks the user; repeating judge false-positives on verify-after-change calls (0.78-0.88 in author eval) produce warn noise; injected_instructions >=0.7 escalates and can decision:block PostToolUse. Caveat I could not verify (docs fetch hit rate limit): emitting hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext with hookEventName Stop and relying on it to make Claude continue once (hook.rs:373-380) may not be honored by Claude Code 2.1.285, since Stop is documented to continue via decision:block/reason; test in log/advise before trusting the stop-verifier behavior.
gh-danielhirt-truthsayer.contextCost: Zero MCP tools, zero skills, no SessionStart context injection (only a user-visible systemMessage on misconfig). Hook-injected text only when a finding acts (mode enforce): about 250-500 chars (~60-125 tokens) per finding set, e.g. the 'truthsayer, an automatic check by a separate model...' preamble plus reason and hint lines. Log/advise modes inject nothing to the model. Negligible skill-budget impact.
gh-danielhirt-truthsayer.latencyImpact: log mode (default): PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure/PreToolUse return immediately after spawning a detached process (still a fork+exec of a Rust binary and transcript read per tool call, few ms); Stop check runs inline once per turn (~0.5-1 s). advise/enforce: each matched event blocks on the Jev call, author measured 500-650 ms per check including a fresh TLS handshake (each hook is a new process, so no connection reuse), worst case 8 s timeout; runs on every non-bookkeeping tool call, adding roughly 0.5 s serial per Bash/Read/Grep/Edit, comparable to or worse than the existing gitnexus hook stack, and multiplied in parallel-tool-call bursts (hooks run concurrently but each waits). Jev p50 200 ms is /alpha with no SLA.
gh-danielhirt-truthsayer.autoInvocation: Fully deterministic hook: triggers automatically on every matched tool event and Stop with no user prompt or model choice. Matches the user's wish for automatic use, but Claude never 'uses' Jev; the harness does, and only enforce mode feeds results back to Claude.
pros: OpenRouter is first-class in code: /api/alpha/decisions with Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY, model/endpoint overridable in user config (http.rs:36-57, config keys in docs/claude-code.md:75-81); no patching needed.

Safe rollout by design: default mode log (background, records only, no behavior change), then advise, then enforce; per-project mode=off and TRUTHSAYER_MODE env override give a cheap kill switch for client repos.
Strong fail-open behavior and shim no-ops if binary missing; project config cannot redirect endpoint/key/model (config-injection defense with a test), Stop nudge limited via stop_hook_active.
Redaction plus secret-file withholding before send and before record; records 0600; key only via env, never argv.
Zero MCP/skill context cost; injected text only on findings and clearly labeled as fallible automatic check.

Covers ground the user lacks: Stop verification of unsupported success claims, injected-instruction detection in tool output, constraint enforcement on edits, loop detection; includes replay/label/report tooling to tune thresholds from own sessions with no extra judge calls.

Decent engineering hygiene for a new repo: CI with clippy -D warnings, shellcheck, MSRV, SHA-pinned actions, mock-server HTTP tests, published eval run with honest caveats (14 misses listed, synthetic labels admitted).
cons: Brand new and unproven: 0 stars, 1 author, 11 commits over 9 days, no releases or tags; cargo install from git HEAD builds unaudited third-party code (pin --rev if used).

OpenRouter path never exercised live by the author: eval and README examples used TypeSafe direct; default OpenRouter model alias `~typesafe/jev-latest` unverified against the user's brief (typesafe/jev-1.13), so set model explicitly and test with `truthsayer doctor` plus a log-mode run.

Data egress is broad for client work: prompt, tool inputs and up to 4000 chars of every tool output (file reads, Bash output) go to OpenRouter then TypeSafe on almost every tool call; regex redaction is admittedly incomplete; also duplicates content into a local records.jsonl.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY must be in Claude Code's own environment, exposing it to agent Bash; user's no-secret-leak.cjs does not yet protect it. Also TypeSafe key silently wins if both set.

In advise/enforce every PostToolUse adds ~0.5 s (new process and TLS handshake each time) on top of existing gitnexus hooks; log mode has no latency but then Claude gets no benefit, so value only appears after enforce, which risks false-positive denies/blocks from an alpha-endpoint, imperfectly calibrated model (author's own repeating false positives 0.78-0.88; eval labels model-written, synthetic).

The Stop-hook re-prompt relies on hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext for Stop, which I could not confirm Claude Code honors (Stop normally uses decision:block); PreToolUse 'ask' decision behavior under bypassPermissions/auto is also unclear, so parts of the enforce design may be no-ops for this user's frequent bypass sessions.
Author explicitly says no evidence yet that it improves cost, speed or task success (benchmark only planned).
gh-danielhirt-truthsayer.verdict: Best-in-class conceptual fit (automatic hook-driven Jev checks, native OpenRouter, fail-open, log-first rollout), but it is a 9-day-old single-author alpha whose OpenRouter path is only mock-tested, sends up to 4000 chars of every tool output off-machine, and needs a cargo build plus the API key in Claude's env. Reasonable to trial in log mode on personal projects (pinned commit, explicit model, mode=off for client repos, add OPENROUTER_API_KEY to no-secret-leak.cjs) rather than enforce it.

gh-griffinwork40-claude-jev.name: griffinwork40/claude-jev
gh-griffinwork40-claude-jev.whatItDoes: Claude Code plugin (marketplace name claude-jev, v0.27.0) that hands small judgments to Jev via typed questions: UserPromptSubmit routing hint (intent/scope/needs_tools), PreToolUse Agent|Task model-tier pick via updatedInput plus a brief-completeness check that can deny a spawn once, per-edit PostToolUse judging of edits against rules parsed from CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.claude/rules (blocks at >=0.80 with file:line), Bash git-worktree snapshots so the Stop hook can judge turn-level rules, and an experimental session.compact function hook that replaces the compaction summary with Jev-selected verbatim transcript rows. The GitHub repo is a fork whose HEAD (44b6ff3) is the same as upstream 0x7067/claude-jev v0.27.0. Griffin Long authored only 4 commits (docs and the AFK adapter, upstreamed as PRs) and none of the code is fork-original. Runtime is now TypeScript on Node with --experimental-strip-types (commit 3a393b7 "The plugin runtime is TypeScript"); the README still says "Python stdlib". Python remains only for register.ts pane helpers, stats and evals.

providerSupport.evidence: Dual provider in code. adapters/afk/src/shared/jev-client.ts:70-81 defines PROVIDERS: typesafe https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (any key) and openrouter https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone (key prefix sk-or-, var OPENROUTER_API_KEY). resolveKey() at :119-133 reads TYPESAFE_API_KEY first, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then the saved plugin option, and picks the provider from the sk-or- prefix. CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_PROVIDER pins a provider (:89). systemoneBackend at :223-236 allows a JEV_BASE_URL override. A second backend 'decisions:<model>' hits https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (:150, :239-249) but is opt-in only. Default model is 'jev-latest' (:50). CHANGELOG line 40 says a 303-record eval was served from OpenRouter with jev-latest, and the OpenRouter Jev doc lists ~typesafe/jev-latest as an alias. Python mirror: scripts/jev.py:44-47, 166.
providerSupport.openrouterPatchability: Nothing to patch. Export OPENROUTER_API_KEY (sk-or-...) and it works. Only gotcha: if TYPESAFE_API_KEY is also set, it wins in auto mode, so pin provider=openrouter or leave TYPESAFE_API_KEY unset.

interface.name: UserPromptSubmit -> src/prompt-router.ts
interface.purpose: One Jev call per prompt (intent choice, scope score, needs_tools noul, with the previous turn as context). Injects a one-line additionalContext hint only for lookup/fix, or when needs_tools <= 0.1. Silent below 0.75 confidence.

interface.name: PreToolUse Agent|Task -> src/subagent-router.ts
interface.purpose: Picks the cheapest model tier (haiku/sonnet/opus/fable) where P(needs stronger) <= 0.10 and sets model via updatedInput, unless a model is already set. Checks the brief for paths, acceptance, verification and commit policy, and denies the spawn once via permissionDecision deny when parts are missing.

interface.name: PreToolUse Bash -> src/rules.ts
interface.purpose: Snapshots the git worktree (scratch GIT_INDEX_FILE, git add -A, write-tree) before each command.

interface.name: PostToolUse Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit -> src/rules.ts
interface.purpose: Judges the edit hunk against rules from CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/* and .cursor/rules/*. Sends at most 40 rule questions per edit. Emits decision:block with file:line at >=0.80. Blocks the same file at most twice per session. Uncertain results are surfaced as a systemMessage only.

interface.name: PostToolUse Bash and PostToolUseFailure Bash -> src/rules.ts
interface.purpose: Re-snapshots the worktree and diffs it against the earlier snapshot to record hunks made by shell commands.

interface.name: Stop -> src/rules.ts
interface.purpose: Judges the turn's hunks against whole-turn rules such as minimal-change and no-refactor, and can block the stop, max 2 blocks.

interface.name: session.compact function hook (hooks/register.ts) -> src/compactor.ts rows
interface.purpose: Experimental. Needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1. Asks Jev keep/truncate/drop over the newest 150 rows plus 150 more for the constraint check. Kept rows become the post-compaction context in place of a summary. Falls through to the built-in summary on error.

interface.name: /claude-jev pane (hooks/register.ts)
interface.purpose: Settings pane, also flag-gated. Saves the key, pins the provider, toggles hooks, shows the last call and stats. Runs python3 scripts/jev.py status and stats.py.

interface.name: plugin.json userConfig
interface.purpose: typesafeApiKey, provider, promptRouter, subagentRouter, rules, compaction toggles, all default on.

interface.name: scripts/jev.py CLI (ask/choose/noul/score/intent/status)
interface.purpose: Manual and eval client. Not wired to Claude Code as a tool.

security: Key handling: Bearer key is sent only in an Authorization header via fetch (jev-client.ts:~176), never in argv or logs. jev-calls.jsonl logs provider, model, ms and error only, with the error truncated to 300 chars. The key is read from the environment, or from a plugin userConfig field 'typesafeApiKey' (plugin.json) that lands in Claude Code's plugin option storage. plugin.json does not set a sensitive flag, so where it is stored is up to Claude Code. Prefer the env var.

No secret redaction anywhere: grep of src/, hooks/ and adapters/afk/src/shared/ finds no redact/secret/.env filtering. Edit hunks, Bash-produced diffs, the previous turn and user prompts go to the provider verbatim, so any secret in a diff or prompt leaves the machine.

Prompt-injection surface: file content, hunks, prompts and CLAUDE.md text are placed into Jev state. Injected instructions can move scores. Consequences are bounded: worst cases are a false block or a suppressed rule check, a wrong subagent tier, or a deny-once. Jev cannot execute anything.

Blocking behavior: rules.ts emits decision:block on PostToolUse (edits are already written, so this only feeds a repair reason back to the agent) and on Stop (max 2 per session). The README's own numbers show 23/247 (9.3%) of previously accepted real edits blocked, i.e. measured false positives. docs/stop-hook-false-positive.md records a real incident with two false Stop blocks caused by stale hunks.

Shell exec: fixed argv git commands via spawnSync (rules.ts:330), no shell string interpolation of tool input. Bash snapshot runs 'git add -A' against a scratch GIT_INDEX_FILE, which writes loose blob objects into the repo's .git/objects on every Bash call, with two or three runs per call. It leaves object-store garbage in client repos, and hashes untracked non-ignored files such as a stray .env.

Installer or downloader: an optional detached process downloads a 51MB ast-grep 0.45.3 release to ~/.claude/jev-bin, sha256-pinned, the first time an edit needs it. A background network fetch of a binary that then executes on user files.

Telemetry: none to the author. Local logs only: ~/.claude/jev-calls.jsonl, jev-router-log.jsonl, jev-compact-log.jsonl, jev-rule-blocks/ state, and a rules cache. Prompt content may sit in the local router logs.

Function-hook compaction relies on an undocumented Claude Code flag and runs plugin JS inside the host process, unlike the other hooks which are separate node processes. Loaded only in trusted workspaces per the README.
The fork could diverge from upstream and receive unreviewed changes. Currently identical to upstream HEAD, but that is a supply-chain reason to install upstream.
gh-griffinwork40-claude-jev.dataEgress: To https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone (Jev pricing is about $0.042 per 1M input tokens). (1) Every prompt: the prompt plus up to 300 chars of the earlier user message and the last 600 chars of the assistant reply (prompt-router.ts buildState). (2) Every edit: the old->new hunk (max 2000 chars), the 4 lines around the edit (max 1200 chars), the last prompt tail (max 400 chars) and rule texts; sibling module names for import rules. About 14% of edits get a second call that adds the enclosing function read from disk. State is capped at 8000 chars. (3) Every Agent/Task spawn: the subagent brief. (4) Stop: up to 16000 chars of turn hunks, including Bash-produced diffs. (5) Compaction: up to 300 transcript rows, 1200 chars each, roughly 200k+ chars. No redaction. Client-project code and prompts therefore reach OpenRouter and TypeSafe. Check client contracts before enabling on client repos. If the only per-call token cost matters, the cost is trivial. The bigger issue is confidentiality.
gh-griffinwork40-claude-jev.failureMode: Fail-open by design. Each entry point wraps main() in try/catch that swallows errors (rules.ts:1186-1205, subagent-router, prompt-router, compactor). A missing key raises and produces no output. Hook timeout is 10s in hooks.json, with an internal budget of 9s for rules (HOOK_BUDGET). The Jev client timeout is 8s (jev-client.ts DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS), 4s for compaction chunks. Compaction falls through to the built-in summary. Caveats: (a) Bare 'node' in the hook command, so with PATH overridden in settings env node may not resolve and the hooks silently never run. Use an absolute path via an override or a wrapper. (b) It fails open only on errors. It does fail closed in the sense of intentionally blocking: PostToolUse edit blocks and Stop blocks (max 2 per file per session, 2 for Stop), and the brief check can deny an Agent spawn once. In bypassPermissions sessions, decision:block still feeds feedback to the model. (c) A Jev outage costs up to about 9s per edit plus retries, which is a latency failure, not a hard failure.
gh-griffinwork40-claude-jev.contextCost: No MCP server, so zero tool-definition tokens. No skills are shipped by the plugin (the .claude/skills dir at repo root is for repo dev only). Hook-injected text: a one-line routing hint (about 15-25 tokens) only on lookup/fix prompts and some no-tools prompts, silent otherwise. Rule block reasons appear only on violations (up to 3000 chars each). Subagent deny reasons and systemMessages are rare. Compaction replaces a summary with about 3.2-3.9k tokens of verbatim rows (per README), which is comparable to a normal summary. Each does git rev-parse, an index copy, 'git add -A' on a scratch index, 'ls-files --others --ignored' and write-tree, with a 4s per-git-command timeout. This is cheap on small repos and can be seconds on large repos or ones with big untracked trees. That stacks with the existing gitnexus Grep|Glob|Bash hook. Per Agent spawn: one call. gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.name: agent-reflex (rutvikchandla3)
gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.whatItDoes: Zero-runtime-dependency TypeScript PreToolUse hook (matcher "*") for Claude Code. Order: config regexes, then hardcoded catastrophic-deny and read-only-allow rules (rules.ts), then ONE POST to {base}/v1/systemone with a compact state (action, project_dir) and ~10 typed questions: risk Score 0-4, category Choice (11 options), 8 Noul signals (7 for non-edits, plus removes_safeguard for edits), and on_task fed with the last user prompt read from the transcript. policy.ts thresholds the answers into allow/ask/deny. Any error returns defer (empty stdout), so Claude Code's normal flow applies. It also has an optional local dashboard/HTTP server, a JSONL decision log, and a 100-case bench.
gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.runtime: Node >=20, ESM, must be compiled with tsc first (dist/cli.js). No runtime deps; devDeps are only typescript 5.9.3 and @types/node. No MCP server, skill or plugin manifest.
gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.install: git clone, npm install (its `prepare` script runs tsc), then hand-write a PreToolUse entry with an absolute node path: node /abs/dist/cli.js hook claude-code. `agent-reflex install claude-code` rewrites ~/.claude/settings.json with JSON.parse/stringify and hardcodes `node` (relies on PATH), so hand-editing is safer. Needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY exported in the shell that launches Claude Code.
gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.tests: 5 test files with about 17 test() cases (policy 7, action 5, questions 3, claude-code 2), plus test/rules.test.js, which my grep counted as 0 test() calls and I did not open. Nothing covers jev.ts. bench/ has 60 tuning cases and 40 holdout cases, run against live Jev, with self-reported 98% exact agreement and 0 dangerous allowed. I did not run any of it, per the hard rules.

interface.name: PreToolUse hook: agent-reflex hook claude-code
interface.purpose: Reads the hook JSON from stdin (tool_name, tool_input, cwd, transcript_path). Emits hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision allow|ask|deny with a reason, or nothing on defer. Deny text tells Claude to ask the user to run the command themselves. Installed with matcher "*" and timeout 15 (adapters/claude-code.ts:20-41, 79-91).

interface.name: agent-reflex check <cmd> [--task --explain --json --stdin]

interface.name: agent-reflex install claude-code [--project]

interface.name: agent-reflex serve [--port 7373]

security: Key handling is good: the key comes only from env and goes only in the Authorization header, never argv. Errors echo at most 300 chars of the response body.

Project-level config is trusted (config.ts:165): a cloned repo's .agent-reflex.json is merged over user config. A hostile client repo can set allowPatterns (auto-allow any matching shell command, reflex.ts:166), onError:"allow", or loosened thresholds. A crafted denyPatterns/allowPatterns regex is compiled with new RegExp on every call, so it is a ReDoS surface, and an invalid one throws outside the try block. Relevant to the user's client projects.

Silent-allow risk: an `allow` from PreToolUse skips the permission prompt. In the user's defaultMode "auto" (my inference, not verified against Claude Code docs) this likely replaces the built-in classifier with an overconfident, steerable Jev.

Prompt-injection surface: the agent-authored Bash `description` is forwarded as agent_says_it_is (action.ts:70), and command and file content are clipped to 2000-2500 chars into state. The agent, or a poisoned README that steers it, can therefore write text aimed at the judge. The README concedes Jev can be steered.

Read-only fast path holes (rules.ts:214-217): rg --pre, fd -x/--exec, sort -o, tree -o, git diff/log --output and --ext-diff are unblocked allowlist commands that can run code or write files, and are auto-allowed with no model call. `task` (subagent spawn) and exitplanmode are always allowed (rules.ts:208-211).
Catastrophic-deny is narrow (rm on / or ~ only, mkfs, dd, fork bomb). Anything else depends on Jev.

No shell exec, no installer beyond the settings.json rewrite, no telemetry. Logging is local only: ~/.agent-reflex/decisions.jsonl holds 400-char command summaries and the task, unredacted, so it can contain secrets. The dashboard binds 127.0.0.1 but sends CORS *, so any web page could POST to it while `serve` runs.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not in the user's no-secret-leak protected-vars list yet. The hook process inherits it, but this tool never prints it.
gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.dataEgress: On every non-fast-path tool call (all non-read-only Bash, Write, Edit, WebFetch, MCP tools, and so on), the following go to the configured base URL, which would be OpenRouter and then TypeSafe: (a) the full Bash command up to 2000 chars plus the agent's description; (b) Write content up to 2500 chars, or up to 5 edit hunks as added/removed lines (200 chars each, 40 lines max) plus any patch up to 2500 chars; (c) WebFetch url plus prompt; (d) other tools' full input JSON up to 2000 chars; (e) file paths and project_dir (the absolute cwd); (f) the user's last prompt in full, read from the transcript tail, as the on_task instruction (questions.ts:248-256). File contents on Read are not sent, but Write and Edit contents are, which can include secrets and client code. No data goes to any other endpoint.
gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.failureMode: Defaults to defer (config.ts:148), which prints nothing so Claude Code's normal permission flow applies. The missing-key, network, HTTP and timeout cases all end up in the try/catch at reflex.ts:147. A hook crash exits 70, which is non-blocking in Claude Code. Timeouts: 4s per attempt, 2 retries with backoff on 429/5xx (jev.ts:76-105), so the worst case is about 12-13s against the 15s hook timeout, and an OpenRouter outage stalls each tool call by that long. Config can set onError to allow or deny. The failure mode is safe to the prompt, but not fail-closed.
gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.latencyImpact: Fast-path calls: node startup, roughly 50ms. Others: one Jev request, self-reported p50 of about 350-390ms (bench at concurrency 8). OpenRouter adds a hop, and the brief gives p50 ~200ms and p95 ~600ms. It blocks each edit, non-trivial Bash call and MCP call; it runs in parallel with the existing hooks (gitnexus, no-secret-leak). Degraded case as under failureMode. One request per call, so about 1-1.5k input tokens per call, cost negligible at $0.042/M.
gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no skill. The hook returns no additionalContext. Only the deny or ask reason string is surfaced (deny goes to Claude, and the reason is short). No token cost in the main context.
gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.autoInvocation: Deterministic PreToolUse hook on matcher "*", so it fires on every tool call with no model prompting. This is the closest match to the user's "never say use jev" requirement among Jev integrations, but it is a gate, not an assistant.
pros: Broadest coverage of Jev-as-gate: matcher "*" covers Bash, Write/Edit, WebFetch and MCP tools. The official cookbook only covers Bash.

Well-structured design: typed questions with signals, thresholds and invariants in code (writes outside the project always ask, jev/policy.ts:266-326, reflex.ts:141), secret exfiltration and on_task checks, code-computed diffs. Deterministic rules run before any model call.
Base URL is env-configurable and the client matches OpenRouter's /v1/systemone path, so it can be pointed at OpenRouter with no code edit (jev.ts:74).
Safe default failure: defer on any error, and no context tokens injected. Zero runtime dependencies, key never in argv, no telemetry, local-only logging.
Has unit tests plus a 100-case bench with holdout, and configurable thresholds and patterns.
cons: Very immature: 1 commit, 1 contributor, 0 stars, 3 days old, no release. The 98% bench accuracy is self-reported and was never run on OpenRouter.
Model default "jev-latest" is unlikely to work on OpenRouter and is not env-overridable. It needs a config file, plus a key-mapping wrapper because it reads only TYPESAFE_API_KEY/JEV_API_KEY.
Silent allow on steerable, overconfident Jev output, and the agent's own description is fed to the judge. In auto or bypass sessions an allow may override the built-in safeguards (my inference).
A project-level .agent-reflex.json in a cloned repo can override allowPatterns, onError and thresholds. This is a real hazard for client and untrusted repos.
Sends command text, Write/Edit contents and the user's full last prompt to a third party (OpenRouter and TypeSafe) on every gated call. That is a client-confidentiality concern.

A retry-heavy timeout profile (~13s worst case) blocks tool calls when OpenRouter's /alpha endpoint is down. Read-only allowlist has code-exec/write holes (rg --pre, sort -o, fd -x). No test for jev.ts.
gh-rutvikchandla3-agent-reflex.verdict: Best-designed general Jev permission gate found so far and it can be pointed at OpenRouter with an env wrapper plus a one-line config, with safe defer-on-error and zero context cost. But it is a 3-day-old, single-commit repo that would silently allow on a steerable model and trusts per-repo config, so it needs hardening (pin the model, ignore project config, run it in ask-only or shadow mode first) before running it on client projects.

gh-nafiurrahmanniloy-jev-guard.name: jev-guard (nafiurrahmanniloy)
gh-nafiurrahmanniloy-jev-guard.whatItDoes: Two stdlib-Python Claude Code hooks. guard.py (PreToolUse, Bash) regex-prefilters commands (commit, push, force-push, PR create/merge, DB write, ssh remote write, paid API); only matches go to Jev in one POST with per-action noul questions ("does the command really do this", "did the user ask or agree", read from the last 3 user messages, the last Claude message and any approved plan in the transcript tail). Below the per-action threshold it emits permissionDecision "ask" and never "allow". For commit, PR create and PR merge it also sends message plus diff (git diff --cached, gh pr diff, capped at 60k chars) with a "diff contains unrelated changes" noul (>=0.5 means ask). Regex-only hard stops deny `git add -A/.` and `git commit -a`. pick_rules.py (UserPromptSubmit) asks Jev one noul per saved memory file (projects/*/memory/*.md) and injects the full text of up to 3 rules scoring >=0.85 as additionalContext. Default mode is "watch" (log only) and must be switched to "enforce" in questions.json.

No OpenRouter string anywhere in *.py or README. Request body is {model,state,questions:{id:{type:'noul',instructions,criteria}}}; response parsed from resp['answers'][id]['noul'|'probability'] and usage.input_tokens (guard.py:385-392, 413-420). This is the /v1/systemone TypeSafe schema, which OpenRouter also serves.

Bearer auth already matches. Wire format looks identical per the brief but is unverified end to end; check that OpenRouter returns answers[id].noul in this shape. Model string differs (jev-1.13, not jev-latest). Tests use a fake endpoint so they would not catch a schema mismatch.
