interface.name: guard.py (PreToolUse, matcher Bash, README timeout 15)
interface.purpose: Approval check plus change check on risky Bash commands; emits ask/deny JSON via hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision; exit 0 always.

interface.name: guard.py --stats
interface.purpose: Summarise log.jsonl (decisions, errors, latency, picker stats).

interface.name: guard.py --replay [N]
interface.purpose: Re-run past risky commands from ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl through Jev (sends real history externally, needs key); writes replay.jsonl.

interface.name: pick_rules.py (UserPromptSubmit, timeout 5)
interface.purpose: Asks Jev which memory/*.md rules apply to the prompt and injects up to 3 as additionalContext.

interface.name: pick_rules.py --try "msg" [transcript]
interface.purpose: Dry-run the rules picker.

interface.name: questions.example.json (copy to questions.json)
interface.purpose: All config: mode watch/enforce, scope (default ~), 8 actions with regex, questions and thresholds (0.7 to 0.85), 2 hard stops, change_check (0.5, 60k chars), rules_picker, on_error 'ask', timeout_seconds 3, recent_messages 3.

security: No shell=True. subprocess is used only for git and gh with list args and short timeouts (guard.py:233, 248). The model-supplied command is never executed, only regex-parsed. However git diff/gh pr view run in a folder derived from the command's `cd X &&` / `git -C X` (guard.py:221-228), so the hook reads state from wherever Claude points it.

API key is sent only as an Authorization Bearer header via urllib (guard.py:406-411). It is not on argv and never printed. It is read from os.environ or a chmod-600 .env in the hook dir. Reusing an env var from settings env is cleaner than the .env. The user's no-secret-leak hook does not yet protect OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so add it.

Redaction is best effort regex (guard.py:57-67): DB URLs, Bearer/Token, *_KEY/*_TOKEN/*_SECRET/*_PASSWORD=, sk-/pk-/rk- (covers sk-or-v1-), GitHub and Slack tokens, JWTs, any 40+ char base64-ish blob. Applied to command, user messages, Claude message, plan, commit description and diff. Code, names and business details are not redacted, so client source diffs leave the machine in plaintext. Secrets in a diff that match no pattern (short passwords, split PEM lines) leak.

Prompt-injection surface: state includes the command text, user messages, claude_last_message and diff, all attacker-influenceable when Claude processed hostile content. Injected text can push 'approved' above threshold (suppress the ask) or push 'unrelated' below 0.5; the brief confirms Jev is steerable by instructions in state. The guard only lowers privilege (ask/deny, never allow), so in default/auto mode the normal permission system still backs it, but in bypassPermissions it is the only gate and is evadable by design: the README itself says a pattern miss (script calling git push internally) escapes it.
Gate is regex on the raw command with heredoc bodies stripped; `bash -c`, scripts and env indirection evade it. Only tool_name Bash is covered.
Local plaintext logs in the hook dir: log.jsonl, replay.jsonl (user messages, redacted), rules_log.jsonl (first 160 chars of every prompt). Git-ignored but persist on disk.

No telemetry beyond the Jev call; no installer script (manual clone plus settings edit); no network besides the one POST and gh/git. Repo has 5 commits by one author, created 2026-09-29, 0 stars, so trust rests on reading about 1000 lines yourself. Pin to a commit.
gh-nafiurrahmanniloy-jev-guard.dataEgress: Only for regex-matched risky Bash commands (never ls, tests, etc.) inside `scope` (default the whole home dir, so all personal and client repos unless narrowed). Per Jev call: redacted command (3000 chars), folder relative to ~, git branch, last 3 user messages (600 chars each; an approved plan up to 4000), Claude's last message (800 chars), and for commit/PR create/PR merge the redacted message plus full diff up to 60,000 chars (merge pulls title, body and diff via gh). With pick_rules enabled, EVERY user prompt (1500 chars redacted) plus Claude's previous message (1200 chars) plus a description line for every saved memory file (each becomes a question, up to 220 chars) is sent on every message, in all scoped projects. For client work the picker should be off and the guard scope narrowed to personal repos, or client contracts checked.
gh-nafiurrahmanniloy-jev-guard.failureMode: Mostly fail-safe toward asking, with holes. Jev unreachable, HTTP error, timeout (3s config), bad JSON, missing key or hook crash gives decision "ask" (on_error "ask") with a visible reason, on risky commands only (guard.py:eval error path, hook() crash handler). Broken config, bad stdin, non-Bash tool or top-level exception exit 0 silently (fail-open, hook() and __main__). Holes: (1) merge path runs gh pr view (10s) plus gh pr diff (15s) sequentially, plus up to 8s git diffs, which can exceed the recommended 15s hook timeout; a Claude Code hook timeout is a non-blocking error, so the command then runs unguarded. (2) Default mode is "watch" so nothing happens until switched to enforce. (3) With defaultMode auto and bypassPermissions sessions, the repo never demonstrates that a hook "ask" still prompts; "deny" (hard stops) is reliable; test this before relying on it. (4) Approval check misses casual yeses: README reports only 54 of 80 clear approvals passing, so expect frequent false asks on commits. (5) Picker: any error means nothing is injected and the prompt proceeds untouched (safe, silent).
gh-nafiurrahmanniloy-jev-guard.latencyImpact: Non-risky Bash: a Python startup plus regex (~30-60 ms) on every Bash call. Risky commands: one Jev call, README reports median 0.33 s (0.3-0.5 s typical), 1-2 s for merges (gh reads), 3 s hard timeout then ask. Picker: about 0.5 s added to every user prompt (5 s hook timeout). Runs alongside the gitnexus and no-secret-leak PreToolUse hooks (Claude Code runs matching hooks in parallel), so no serial stacking expected.
gh-nafiurrahmanniloy-jev-guard.contextCost: Zero MCP tools and no skill or tool definitions, so no listing cost and no interaction with skillListingBudgetFraction. Guard emits text only when it asks: a one-line permissionDecisionReason (~40 tokens). Picker (optional) injects a header plus up to 3 memory bodies of up to 1500 chars each, about 1.2k tokens max per prompt, only when a memory scores >=0.85 (README: ~17/25 first-pick relevance). Overlaps in purpose with Claude Code's own auto-memory loading and caveman's per-prompt additionalContext.
gh-nafiurrahmanniloy-jev-guard.autoInvocation: Fully deterministic hook, no prompting needed. PreToolUse on Bash fires on every call (cheap regex short-circuit) and calls Jev only for risky commands; UserPromptSubmit fires on every prompt if configured. Needs one settings.json edit with absolute python path, a questions.json copy and a key; ships in watch mode so it does nothing visible until "mode":"enforce". It is a PreToolUse hook, not PermissionRequest, so it fires in auto and bypass modes too (unlike the official cookbook pattern).
pros: Only candidate that judges intent: 'did the user actually say yes to this commit/push/merge' from transcript history (guard.py:135-217 parses user turns, rejections, approved plans, queued commands, skips system reminders and task notices), which static allow rules cannot do; directly relevant to auto and bypass sessions where Claude drifts from 'fix X' to push/merge.
Never emits allow (only ask/deny), so it can only tighten; regex prefilter means most Bash never leaves the machine; ask on any Jev error; crash handler converts to ask rather than silent pass.

Diff-vs-description check catches unrelated changes in commits/PRs before merge; README reports 30/30 planted unrelated changes caught with 0/30 false alarms and a replayed real incident (self-reported).

Brand new and unproven: created 2026-09-29, 5 commits in a few hours by one author, 0 stars, 0 forks, no releases; all accuracy numbers are self-reported from one developer's history. Approval check let through only 54/80 clear approvals, so it will over-ask on commits.

Heavy data egress: diffs up to 60k chars and conversation text go to a third party with scope '~' by default; the rules picker sends every prompt. Unsuitable for client repos without narrowing scope or disabling the picker; redaction does not cover code or business names.

Weak as the sole gate in bypassPermissions: regex prefilter is evadable, Jev is injection-steerable and overconfident on unanswerable inputs per the brief, and the repo never demonstrates that a hook 'ask' is honored under bypass/auto modes. Hard stops on `git add -A`/`git add .` and `git commit -a` deny outright even without Jev; likely frequent friction for some habits and must be edited in questions.json.

Rules picker overlaps Claude Code auto-memory and caveman context injectors, adds ~0.5 s and an external call to every prompt, and its one-question-per-memory design may hit request-size limits with hundreds of memories (README tested 152).
Another Python process on every Bash call in an already busy hook chain (no-secret-leak fail-closed, gitnexus multi-second); local plaintext logs of prompts and commands accumulate in the hook dir.

Marker files are keyed by session_id, so subagents and headless or workflow runs that share the session_id can consume or trigger the denial. Every subagent or automation that greps pays an extra failed call, even with no benefit.

jev_search uses ripgrep with .gitignore/.ignore honoured and hidden files skipped, so it searches a different file set than the native Grep. Missed hits are silent, and this is on top of Jev's probabilistic-ranking recall risk.

The user's no-secret-leak hook does not protect ~/.config/jev/api_key or OPENROUTER_API_KEY (the brief notes the latter is not in its list). The key file is 0600 and the server denies reading it, but Claude's own Read/Bash tools are not blocked by this plugin.

The npm package named 'jev-mcp' (v0.5.1, rashedInt32) is a different, older project from this plugin repo; the repo says it started from that project. Install via marketplace only; do not npx jev-mcp expecting this code.

corrections.actual: Only HTTP 429/529 responses are retried. A hung or timed-out request makes c.HTTP.Do return an error, which is returned immediately with no retry. A hung endpoint therefore stalls one call for at most 60s. The ~4 min figure needs four consecutive slow 429/529 responses, which is an unlikely case.

'Actively maintained: 121 commits in 13 days' as a pro is weak. It reflects a single-author burst on a brand-new repo with 12 releases and API churn (env vars TYPESAFE_MODEL and TYPESAFE_MAX_ITEMS were added in the last few releases).
addedCons: The binary has no non-MCP query mode. Its only subcommands are mcp, setup, update and version (main.go:103-113), so hooks cannot call it as a CLI. Claude Code 2.1.x does support `type: "mcp_tool"` hook handlers (server, tool, input with ${tool_input.command} substitution), but the tool's text output is treated as hook stdout. Jev's raw JSON is not a valid PermissionRequest decision (hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior allow/deny), so replicating the OpenRouter cookbook gate needs a wrapper script that calls the API directly. This connector does not deliver that deterministic path.

Hardcoded floating alias ~typesafe/jev-latest (main.go:156) and no env override on the OpenRouter route. Probabilities and any thresholds you tune (e.g. 0.9 gates) can silently shift when TypeSafe bumps the model, and pinning typesafe/jev-1.13 requires passing `model` on every call.

OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not in the existing no-secret-leak.cjs protected list, and `setup mcp` writes the key into ~/.claude.json in plaintext. Any Read/Grep of ~/.claude.json by Claude is a leak path unless that file is protected. Add the key to the hook's list, or better, keep it out of ~/.claude.json via an env wrapper.

The MCP call is not a hook and is not deterministic. In defaultMode auto, a first call to mcp__evaluate__evaluate may still prompt, or an auto-mode classifier may object to sending code or logs to a third party. In bypassPermissions it runs silently, so client-project code and diffs can leave the machine with no gate. Add a permission allow/deny rule deliberately and decide per client project whether this MCP is enabled (unverified: how the auto classifier treats external-egress MCP calls).

Blocking update check plus GitHub API call at every MCP server start (up to 2s, update.go:146-158) sits on the session-start path alongside the gitnexus and caveman startup costs. It is avoidable with --no-update-check, which is a hidden flag.

Go toolchain requirement go 1.27.1 (go.mod:3) makes `go install` from source non-trivial on a machine without that toolchain. The audit mentions it but does not weigh it against its own 'build from source' recommendation.

Sole-maintainer, unaffiliated individual account for a component that will receive client code. The audit says affiliation is unverified, and I confirmed the GitHub profile carries no company or affiliation ('I build stuff').
gh-itsmostafa-typesafe-mcp.note: Re-queried and verified the key facts. Repo is itsmostafa/system-one-connector (renamed from typesafe-mcp), 337 stars, 37 forks, MIT, not archived, created 2026-09-17, last push and v0.4.8 on 2026-09-30, 12 releases. OpenRouter support is real in code: main.go:152-158 POSTs to https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY and model ~typesafe/jev-latest. TYPESAFE_API_KEY takes precedence if both are set (main.go:135). The endpoint answers (401 without a key, not 404), and openrouter.ai/~typesafe/jev-latest exists (HTTP 200). There is one tool, `evaluate`, ReadOnlyHint true (tools.go). No shell exec outside setup (exec.Command only in setup.go), no telemetry, and the only extra egress is the GitHub releases check. The key-in-argv and plaintext ~/.claude.json claims are confirmed (setup.go:231 `-e kv`). The audit was largely accurate, with these errors: the 4-minute hang claim is wrong (max 60s per hang, since only 429/529 are retried), the release count is 12 not 8, the contributor count is inflated by a duplicate identity, and the update-notice channel is a slightly bigger injection surface than 'harmless'. Score lowered from 7 to 6.5. It is the best fit for Jev and OpenRouter, small in context, and fails open. But it does not meet the user's headline requirement of automatic use without prompting. That would need CLAUDE.md steering, or a hook that Claude Code's `mcp_tool` handler cannot turn into a valid PermissionRequest decision without a wrapper. It also has a floating model alias, a 13-day-old single-author repo, no test gate in CI, and no egress control for client code, notably under bypassPermissions. Recommended install stays as the audit says: pinned tag, manual registration with the key kept out of argv and ~/.claude.json, --no-update-check, TYPESAFE_MAX_ITEMS low, and an OpenRouter spend cap on the key. Files: <scratch path>,client.go,setup.go,update.go,tools.go}.

corrections.claimed: Audit does not mention the request-size budget mismatch
corrections.actual: The budget planner hardcodes TOTAL_TOKEN_LIMIT=64_000 and STATE_PLUS_QUESTION_LIMIT=32_000 (TypeSafe direct limits). OpenRouter lists Jev with a 32k context window. corrections.claimed: Redaction misses 'export FOO=bar with a non-keyword name' and business data, but masks key/token/secret/password/bearer/authorization followed by a value.
corrections.actual: The gap is wider. SECRET (blastgate.py:66-67) uses \b(key|token|...)\b. Underscore is a word character, so there is no boundary inside names like API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN or DB_PASSWORD. `export API_KEY=abc123 && curl -X POST x` is sent unredacted. For `Authorization: Bearer abc123def` the regex consumes 'Authorization: Bearer' as keyword plus value, so it prints 'Authorization: <redacted> abc123def' and the actual token leaks unless it starts with sk-/ghp_ etc. or is 40+ chars. `mysql -pHunter2` and `postgres://u:pw@h/db` are also unredacted. The unit test only covers an sk- token and a standalone TOKEN=.
corrections.evidence: My re-implementation of the SECRET regex run on those strings (no candidate code executed). Source: blastgate.py:66-67, 72; test/test_blastgate.py test_redact.

corrections.claimed: The redirect rule at line 53 excludes only targets starting with '/'. Listed gaps: `> /abs/path`, inline interpreters, `docker compose down -v`, `curl | sh`, `bash script.sh`.
corrections.actual: Missed gap: ALL append redirects (`>>`) are never flagged, including `echo x >> ~/.bashrc` and `>> ./f`. The pattern `(^|[^>&2])>\s*[^&>\s/]` cannot match the first '>' (followed by '>') or the second (preceded by '>'). Absolute-path `>` such as `echo hi>/tmp/x` is also unflagged. The preceding-char class also excludes '2', so text such as `script2>out` is missed.
corrections.evidence: My regex re-test: 'echo x >> f', 'echo x >> ./f' and 'echo x >> ~/.bashrc' give no match. 'echo x > ./f' matches. Source: blastgate.py:53.

corrections.claimed: Worst case it blocks the Bash call for 30 s, and the install snippet sets no hook timeout.
corrections.actual: Partly right, but 30 s is a per-socket-operation timeout (HTTPSConnection(timeout=30), line 99), not a total deadline. The connect, send and read steps can each wait up to 30 s, and DNS resolution is not covered by it. The Claude Code command-hook default timeout is 600 s, so with no hook timeout set, the real ceiling is well above 30 s. Setting timeout ~10 in settings is therefore more important than the audit implies. On a hook timeout Claude Code treats the hook as a non-blocking error, so the command proceeds unprompted and the risky command is not gated.
corrections.evidence: blastgate.py:97-99. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks: 'Defaults: 600 for command...'. Non-zero or timed-out hooks are non-blocking errors.

corrections.claimed: Audit says it did not verify that PreToolUse 'ask' forces a prompt in bypassPermissions.
corrections.actual: Only partly resolved. Docs confirm that PreToolUse hooks fire before any permission-mode check in every mode, and that a hook 'deny' blocks even in bypassPermissions. Docs also say auto mode still shows prompts forced by a hook. The docs do not explicitly say a hook 'ask' prompts in bypassPermissions, so the value there is still unconfirmed.
corrections.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide ('PreToolUse hooks fire before any permission-mode check, in every permission mode... deny blocks the tool even in bypassPermissions'). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes ('auto mode still shows you those prompts' for hook-forced prompts).

corrections.claimed: This adds nothing while the no-secret-leak and gitnexus hooks run alongside it, since hooks run in parallel.
corrections.actual: Correct that matching hooks run in parallel. But the tool call waits for the slowest hook. The gitnexus hook can take seconds, but blastgate's 21% Jev path (about 0.3-0.7 s cold TLS per the audit) is hidden only if it is shorter than that hook. The 60 ms per command in the README is a batched figure (8 commands per request in eval.py), not the single-command hook case.
corrections.evidence: eval.py run_batch/BATCH=8; hooks docs 'All matching hooks run in parallel'.

refutedPros: Redaction keeps secrets from leaving the machine. The pro 'Jev is used well... fast, cheap' is fine, but the README-implied claim that secrets are masked is overstated: API_KEY-style names and the token after 'Authorization: Bearer' are not masked.

The cost and speed pro ($0.018 for 881 commands, 60 ms per command) comes from README figures measured with batches of 8 commands per request. The hook sends one command per request, so it is not directly representative.
addedCons: Redaction misses env-var names that embed a keyword after an underscore (API_KEY=, GITHUB_TOKEN=, DB_PASSWORD=) and the token in 'Authorization: Bearer <tok>' (verified with the regex). Real secrets in risky commands (curl -X POST with a bearer, export FOO_KEY=...) can go to OpenRouter and TypeSafe.
All `>>` appends (for example `>> ~/.bashrc`, `>> .env`) and absolute-path `>` redirects are never sent to Jev and never gated (regex line 53).

A hook timeout or crash is a non-blocking error in Claude Code, so it does not gate anything. Only Jev errors inside the script return 'ask'. The 30 s socket timeout is per operation, and the default hook timeout is 600 s.

For this user, auto mode already has a classifier, and the docs say hook-forced 'ask' prompts still appear in auto mode. blastgate therefore adds prompts (about 19% of the 21% pattern hits, roughly 4% of commands) rather than removing them. It is a net friction add unless the user wants a stricter second layer.
If TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set globally, it wins over OPENROUTER_API_KEY (load_key, line 81) and is sent as the bearer to openrouter.ai, producing 401 and constant 'ask'. The user must leave it unset.

The 58/176 HTTP 403s at the provider edge were observed in the author's own eval with the same http.client and no User-Agent. It is the only evidence of real-world reliability, and it looks like a 33% failure rate. The audit mentioned it but under-weighted it.
The test suite mocks all network calls and never exercises the real request or response schema. It has not been tested by us against live OpenRouter.

corrections.claimed: '~typesafe/jev-latest' would trip the model-family check (modelFamily gives 'jev-latest' vs response family)
corrections.actual: modelFamily() returns the text before the FIRST '-' after stripping everything up to the last '/'. '~typesafe/jev-latest' gives 'jev-latest', then 'jev'. Family is 'jev', so it matches any jev-* response. The MODEL_MISMATCH fear is unfounded. The default model 'jev-latest' also passes.
corrections.evidence: src/client.ts modelFamily (~line 466): lowered.slice(lastIndexOf('/')+1), then slice(0, indexOf('-')). Doc comment there says 'jev-latest' and 'jev-1.13.0' both belong to family 'jev'.

corrections.claimed: OpenRouter System One response schema compatibility is unverified and the strict validator may fail on drift
corrections.actual: OpenRouter docs say responses have model, answers, usage in TypeSafe's shape, plus extra id, provider and usage.cost. The validator (validateTypeSafeResponse) copies only model/answers/usage.input_tokens/output_tokens and drops extras, so the extras are harmless. Both 'typesafe/jev-1.13' and 'jev-1.13' are accepted on OpenRouter's /api/v1/systemone. A config-only switch is therefore documented as supported, though still no live call was made and the plugin has zero OpenRouter code, docs or tests. 'partial' is the right label; risk is lower than the audit implies.
corrections.evidence: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/community/typesafe-sdk (baseURL https://openrouter.ai/api, model jev-1.13 or jev-latest, extra id/provider/usage.cost); https://github.com/gitmoot/workspace-janitor/issues/18 (POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone with model typesafe/jev-1.13); src/client.ts validateTypeSafeResponse returns only model/answers/usage.

corrections.field: pros: 'Complements bypass/auto permission mode ... semantic ask safety net where the user has permission prompts off'
corrections.claimed: Enforce mode adds an 'ask' net in bypass/auto sessions
corrections.actual: The plugin deliberately suppresses 'ask' in bypassPermissions and dontAsk. isPromptHostAvailable() returns false for those modes, and with the default blockWithoutUI:false the hook returns null (nothing, fail open). Only blockWithoutUI:true makes it 'deny', a hard block with no prompt. Claude Code's own docs say a hook 'ask' would still prompt under bypassPermissions, so the plugin gives up a capability the harness offers. Only 'auto' mode gets a real ask. This is a major point for a user who frequently runs bypassPermissions. Audit's own failureMode field states the fail-open, so the audit contradicts itself.
corrections.evidence: src/hooks/pre-tool.ts:55-62 (mode dontask/bypasspermissions -> false) and 177-190 (blockWithoutUI false -> return null; true -> permissionDecision deny); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (PreToolUse ask escalates to user regardless of mode).

corrections.field: security: 'Plugin never returns allow ... so it cannot weaken existing permission rules'
corrections.claimed: Cannot weaken rules
corrections.actual: True for allow, but a repo-controlled project config (.claude/claude-jev.json) IS still merged for gate.* settings (only transport/secret keys are locked). Cloned client repo can set gate.enabled=false, raise thresholds, change tools or mode, and silently turn off the guard. The 'project config cannot ...' pro is narrower than presented: it protects the key and endpoint, not the guard's effectiveness.
corrections.evidence: src/config.ts:224-260 (gate block merged with no allowTransport check), :333-341 (project layer allowTransport:false, allowSecretSources:false only).

corrections.claimed: Egress is cwd, tool name, truncated tool_input, user prompt; PostToolUse output sent only on prefilter match or failures
corrections.actual: Additions. (a) The prefilter is very broad and recall-favoring: any output matching /(api_key|secret|token|password|auth...)[:=]value/i, a 32+ char mixed-case token, or a command containing env, set, .env, credentials, .key or .pem triggers a remote send of up to 2000 chars. Ordinary source dumps (cat config.ts with 'token: ...') will be sent. (b) PreToolUse Write/Edit content (400 chars/arg) can itself contain secrets and is sent BEFORE any local secret check, so the leak guard is not local-first. (c) Prompts are persisted to disk in ~/.cache/claude-jev (mode 0600, retention sweep) unless scratchpad_dir is supplied; the audit does not mention local persistence of prompts and cached verdicts. (d) Subagent tool calls are gated too (agent_id handled), multiplying calls.
corrections.evidence: src/output.ts:88-150 (patterns and SECRET_READING_COMMAND); src/state.ts:48-51 (1200/400/8000 caps); src/hook-io.ts:163-176 (fallback ~/.cache/claude-jev); src/hooks/user-prompt.ts:45 (store.setPrompt).

corrections.claimed: Hooks are plain 'node' commands, portable
corrections.actual: hooks.json uses exec form: command 'node' with args [...], which relies on `node` being resolvable on the hook process PATH. The user overrides PATH in settings env (and needs absolute paths for hooks), so bare `node` may not resolve. The failure is non-blocking but silent, so the guard would be inert. README requires Node >=22.6 on PATH. Audit missed this.
corrections.evidence: hooks/hooks.json (all four entries, command:'node'); README.md:379; Claude Code hooks docs: exec form runs args with no shell.

corrections.field: failureMode (outage in bypassPermissions/dontAsk becomes a hard deny)
corrections.claimed: In bypassPermissions or dontAsk mode an ask is converted to deny by default, so an outage or a borderline call turns into a hard block.
corrections.actual: Only model-scored asks are converted. An outage, timeout, HTTP error, missing key or malformed answer goes through failMode() and returns verdict=policy.fail_mode ('ask') directly. The unattended ask-to-deny conversion runs only at the end of the model-scored path. So an outage in bypass mode emits a plain ask plus '[toolgate] NOT gating', not a deny. What Claude Code then does with a hook 'ask' in bypassPermissions is not documented. The hook docs page (fetched via WebFetch) suggests the decision is ignored there, which would make an outage fail-open in the user's frequent bypass sessions. That is unverified and the reverse of the audit's claim.
corrections.evidence: src/engine.ts:107-109 (catch -> failMode), :249-251 (failMode returns policy.fail_mode with source fail-mode), :210-214 (unattended conversion happens only after model scoring); src/hook.ts:75-76 (fail-mode ask is not converted); README.md:45 and :57 (the table only covers model asks).

corrections.claimed: Not mentioned. Only the 24-40% ask rate was noted as the friction.
corrections.actual: Input over limits.input_chars (default 40000 chars of serialized tool_input, so large Write/Edit calls) is never allowed. An 'allow' becomes 'ask' with 'input too large to evaluate in full'. In bypassPermissions/dontAsk that ask is then converted to a deny (truncation check at engine.ts:189-192 runs before the unattended conversion at :210). So large Writes/Edits in the user's bypass sessions are hard-blocked by default.
corrections.evidence: src/engine.ts:189-192 and :210-214; src/state.ts:5 (input_chars 40000) and :237-240 (truncateMiddle); test/engine.test.ts:406-411 (input_chars honored -> ask); README.md:39 ('input too large ... only asked about').

corrections.field: security / latency (hook fires on every tool call)
corrections.claimed: Adds no latency to Read, Grep, Glob; static rules and passthroughs cost about 90 ms.
corrections.actual: The audit's own install snippet registers PreToolUse with matcher '*' and three post-event hooks (PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionDenied) with matcher '*'. That means a fresh node process runs on every tool call, including Read/Grep/Glob, both before and after. The ungated tools skip only the model call, not the process spawn. The ~90 ms figure is the maintainer's own number, not independently measured. It stacks with the user's existing gitnexus Pre/Post hooks, no-secret-leak and the plannotator plugin. Hooks in the same event run in parallel, so the cost is not strictly additive.
corrections.evidence: src/install.ts:37-52 (matcher '*' for PreToolUse and POST_EVENTS), :101-104 (installInto pushes matcher '*'); src/engine.ts:80-83 (ungated tools return after the static rules).

corrections.field: security (Claude Code interaction not covered: auto-mode classifier)

corrections.actual: README.md claims the two are independent, and the hook docs say a hook 'allow' bypasses the normal permission flow (docs are ambiguous on auto-mode ordering). If a toolgate 'allow' pre-empts Anthropic's auto-mode classifier for Bash and Write, the user's default auto mode could end up relying on the weaker Jev gate (independent evals: accuracy a bit below mid-price LLMs, overconfident on unanswerable inputs, injection-sensitive) for those calls. The audit does not verify or flag this. I could not confirm it from the docs.
corrections.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes ('How the classifier evaluates actions' lists allow/ask/deny rules but not hook decisions); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks ('allow ... bypassing the normal permission flow'); README.md:63-65.

corrections.claimed: Key never in argv, stored 0600 in ~/.toolgate/env.
corrections.actual: Accurate, but the audit omits that the user's no-secret-leak.cjs does not list OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and Claude could read ~/.toolgate/env, since the Read matcher is only path-based. loadEnvFile() also imports every var in that file into the hook's environment. Hand-merging the snippet with the key supplied through a settings env would avoid the file but expose the key to the settings env. This is a user-side gap, not a toolgate bug.
corrections.evidence: src/policy.ts:210-218 (loadEnvFile); user brief on no-secret-leak.

refutedPros: Fail-safe, visible failure handling ... internal errors become an ask, never a silent allow. Partly refuted: this holds only where the user answers the prompt (default and auto modes). In bypassPermissions/dontAsk, whether Claude Code honors a hook 'ask' is undocumented, and the docs summary suggests it is ignored, so an outage may fail open there. Do not present it as 'safe failure modes' for the user's bypass sessions.
Zero context-token cost / no latency on Read/Grep/Glob. Context cost is fine, but the latency half is misleading: a node process still spawns for every tool call, Pre and Post, since matcher is '*'.

Genuinely automatic / no model-discretion dependence. True mechanically, but it delivers safety gating only, and the audit's phrase 'best-fit for the requirement' overstates the fit to 'uses Jev whenever it adds value'.
addedCons: Outage behaviour in bypassPermissions/dontAsk is inconsistent with the audit: the fail-mode ask is not converted to deny (src/engine.ts:249-251). Claude Code's handling of a hook 'ask' in bypass is undocumented and may be ignored, which would make outages fail-open in the user's bypass sessions.
Any Write/Edit/Bash whose serialized input exceeds 40,000 chars is downgraded to ask, and hard-denied in bypass/dontAsk, so large generated files or big diffs get blocked with no human in the loop.

matcher '*' spawns a fresh node process for every tool call, both Pre and Post (three extra post-event hooks), with ~90 ms of self-reported overhead. Model-path calls run about 0.7-1.2 s synchronously on top of the user's slow gitnexus hooks.

Possible interaction with auto mode (the user's default): a hook 'allow' may short-circuit Anthropic's classifier, so Jev, which the independent evals rate below mid-price LLMs and injection-sensitive, could become the effective gate for gated calls. Unverified, but it needs an empirical check before trusting it.

Client-project egress: full Bash commands, full Write/Edit content (up to 40k chars) and the last 3 user prompts plus session goal go to OpenRouter's /api/alpha endpoint and then to TypeSafe on every gated call. Redaction is regex/key-based and the README itself calls it only a courtesy. This needs an OpenRouter data-policy or ZDR check for client work.

Evaluation evidence is maintainer-run on TypeSafe direct, not OpenRouter. The challenge sets were authored and labeled by ChatGPT and frozen by the maintainer, with 19/20, 20/24 and 19/22 headline scores. The documented misses include a Ruby exfiltration ask at 0.84 vs a 0.85 deny line, and npm-script and Bash-side-write gaps in the ledger, so it is not a security boundary. No independent adoption: 2 stars, 0 issues, 1 contributor, 20 npm releases in 10 days, including two retracted stale-dist releases (0.8.0, 0.9.0).

Key precedence hazard: auto mode prefers TYPESAFE_API_KEY over OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and loadEnvFile() imports every var from ~/.toolgate/env, so a stray TYPESAFE key silently bypasses OpenRouter unless backend.provider: openrouter is pinned.

Git shows 74 commits, and npm has 20 versions with latest 0.15.0. The npm package has no install scripts (only build/test/prepublishOnly), and its only dependencies are ai and yaml. Confirmed in source: src/backends/openrouter.ts:13-16 uses OPENROUTER_API_KEY, POSTs to https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with model typesafe/jev-1.13, sends the key in a Bearer header (not argv), and applies a 5 s AbortController timeout. The audit's inventory (provider support, interface, stats, install, latency numbers, pros/cons) is otherwise accurate. Score drops from 7 to 6: it is the only truly automatic, OpenRouter-native Jev integration, but it delivers safety gating rather than coding value. It is very immature with single-maintainer evaluations, and it has real friction and failure-mode surprises in the user's bypass workflow. It also sends client code and prompts off-machine on every gated call. Recommend only as an opt-in, narrowed gated_tools trial with unattended.ask: ask, backend.provider: openrouter pinned, and a check of how Claude Code treats a hook ask in bypass mode.

/compactio:setup (and the README's step 3) auto-enables the Sweep once a key exists. That sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, which disables MCP tool search (the user's gitnexus and playwright tools load upfront) and Remote Control. The user's no-secret-leak hook does not yet protect OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so add it to the protected list. The key is global to all projects, but a project-level `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=""` env override disables Jev per client repo (endpoint() checks truthiness, jev.ts:29).
Egress includes playwright, gitnexus and WebFetch/WebSearch content and any `git diff`/`cat` output through Bash, not only test logs.
The model alias ~typesafe/jev-latest floats. Behavior and calibration of the 0.6/0.8 thresholds can shift silently on a Jev release. Pinning needs COMPACTIO_JEV_MODEL=typesafe/jev-1.13.

Cut/tombstone notes embed a plugin-cache path (`node ".../cli.ts" show ID`, hook.ts:128). It is version-specific and breaks after a plugin update or cache GC. In auto or default modes the agent needs a Bash permission for a node call outside the project, which may prompt.
Unlocked session-file writes race under parallel tool calls (store.ts:28-39).

Same-event PostToolUse rewriters run in parallel and the last rewrite wins (docs: 'another hook's rewrite replaces it'). Interaction with the user's gitnexus PostToolUse hook on Bash and Grep is unverified.
The value is token and context savings, not better decisions. It replaces output that Opus would otherwise see with a lossy view, in a user who runs Opus 5.5 with a large window.

refutedPros: Overstated: 'Only candidate that judges intent' is a comparative claim about other candidates in the set that this review cannot verify, and the README itself says the approval check passes only 54/80 clear approvals at 85%.

Overstated: 'README reports 30/30 planted unrelated changes ... and a replayed real incident' is accurate as a report, but it is one developer's history with planted synthetic changes and self-labelled data, so it is weak evidence of real-world precision.

Partly overstated: 'crash handler converts to ask rather than silent pass' holds only for crashes inside the try after the risky-command match. Config load errors, bad stdin, and any exception in the pre-match path exit 0 silently (fail-open, guard.py:536-551, 664-667).
addedCons: TypeSafe direct signups were paused as of Sept 2026 and some Vercel AI Gateway users saw 429s, per the README's own 'why you might not want it'. OpenRouter is therefore likely the only practical path, which makes the local ENDPOINTS patch a requirement. The audit omitted this.
With only an OpenRouter key and no patch, enforce mode prompts on every risky command (commit, push, PR) with a 'could not reach Jev' reason, not just some of them.

Picker request size: build_questions emits one noul question (instructions plus criteria) per memory. I measured about 83k characters (about 20k tokens) for 152 memories. That is close to the 32k-token context limit on OpenRouter and costs input tokens on every prompt (about $0.0009 at $0.042/M). A few hundred memories would exceed the context limit, and any error means nothing is injected.
Picker in the shipped config sends every scoped prompt to Jev in watch mode with no benefit until mode is set to 'on'.

Missing-config case: guard.py load_config falls back to questions.example.json when questions.json is absent, so the guard is active in watch mode from a bare clone, logging (with redacted commands) and sending risky commands to Jev without any deliberate opt-in beyond registering the hook and setting a key.

A commit with many `git add` paths can issue up to about 20 extra `git diff --no-index` calls (pending_commit_diff, guard.py:294-308), which stack against the 15s hook timeout. refutedPros: '31 tests' is wrong: 29 tests (README says 28). Test coverage claim still holds directionally, with a fake OpenRouter through the engine.

'Cheap and fast ... README measured 1 request, 7.8k tokens, $0.00033, 503 ms' rests on a single self-reported session (8 largest file reads, 22 calls, 541k chars of results: a best case for pruning). 'Config is rich ... /jev gives visibility into every decision' overstates one point: /jev keeps only the last compaction's decisions and the last 20 gate decisions, held in memory for the activation.
addedCons: Key exposure path: if OPENROUTER_API_KEY goes into settings.json env (as the README suggests), Claude Code exports settings env to the Bash tool's child processes, so the model could `printenv` it. Under bypassPermissions the no-secret-leak hook is the only barrier. Prefer the sensitive plugin `apiKey` option (which takes precedence, src/config.ts:136) and still add OPENROUTER_API_KEY to the protected list.

The always-on `session.compact` `{trigger:'precompute'}` hook returns skip. It disables the engine's background precompute of the built-in summary for every session. Whenever Jev fails, is missing a key, or reduces less than 20%, the fallback summary must then be computed synchronously, so the fallback path is slower than stock Claude Code (d.ts ~8523: precompute result is 'kept for the compaction that comes').

The session.compact hook also receives subagent transcripts when the engine compacts them (README Limitations), so subagent content (tool inputs and results) egresses to OpenRouter too, not only the main conversation.

Reduction is judged in characters, not tokens, and chat/thinking-heavy transcripts are barely reduced. Every such compaction still costs a Jev round trip, then falls back to a full LLM summary, and plugin-triggered attempts are retried every +10 context points.

Function hooks are documented in the 2.1.285 binary and d.ts as needing CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1 (verified), but the plugin's types are pinned to 2.1.278 and the README says the API may change. A silent CC update break is plausible. Hook failures are skipped and reported by name, so the failure mode is benign (built-in compaction).

The gate's Read cut discards the entire remainder of a file after about 4000 chars, not just the middle. A wrong P<0.3 call on a file to be edited silently hides the code being edited, though the note gives the offset to re-read from. This is riskier than the audit's description of 'cut the middle'.
gh-jaydoubleu-cc-mod-jev.note: The audit is mostly accurate. Verified independently: the endpoint https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (src/openrouter.ts:3), model typesafe/jev-1.13, and the Bearer header, with the key read from the plugin apiKey option, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then the settings.json env block. The body is {model,state,questions} and the response must contain `answers`, so the TypeSafe /v1/systemone schema would need code changes, as the audit says. The hooks session.start, session.compact (incl. precompute), turn.complete, tool.call and command.run all exist in hooks/jev-context.ts. The event names and the SessionCompactTrigger values (manual/auto/plugin/precompute) match the CC 2.1.278 d.ts, and the flag string is present in the local 2.1.285 binary. There is no shell exec, spawn, child_process or eval in src or hooks, and no install scripts. package.json has only a typescript devDependency; scripts/smoke.ts is a manual bun script that uses plain fetch. Egress figures (goal 3x500, text 2000, tool input 1000, result head 120, 20k/28k caps) match src/state.ts and src/config.ts. All fallbacks return next(e) or skip, and the gate fails open. Errors found: the test count (29, not 31), the gate default tools and Read semantics, two line references, the code-size figure, and the timeout framing. The plugin cannot set a timeout because HttpInit has none. Score stays 6. It fits the 'automatic, zero context cost, OpenRouter-native' brief better than anything else in the category. It is held below 7 by the one-evening, one-star, one-author repo with no CI, the early-access flag, ungated egress of tool inputs and result heads to a no-SLA alpha endpoint, and the key-exposure and precompute side effects. Recommendation: try it on personal projects with the gate off, pin the commit 9c526c2, put the key in the plugin apiKey option rather than settings env, and add OPENROUTER_API_KEY to the no-secret-leak protected list before using it on client work.

corrections.actual: OpenRouter's System One endpoint accepts TypeSafe's bare IDs and maps them: 'jev-1.13' -> typesafe/jev-1.13, 'jev-latest' -> ~typesafe/jev-latest, and prefixed IDs are used as-is. The qs.mjs default 'jev-latest' (qs.mjs:65) therefore works on OpenRouter with no QUICKSILVER_MODEL. Setting it is optional and worthwhile only to pin 'jev-1.13' and avoid silent alias upgrades.
corrections.evidence: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/community/typesafe-sdk.md section 'Model IDs'. Bare 'jev-1.13' is also the documented example model in the same page.

corrections.claimed: partial: `status`/`setup` call GET /v1/models, which OpenRouter serves with different content, and only an HTTP 200 is checked.
corrections.actual: It is worse than a shape mismatch: OpenRouter's /api/v1/models is public and returns 200 even for a bogus Bearer token (I curled it with a fake key and got HTTP 200). With QUICKSILVER_API_BASE=https://openrouter.ai/api, `qs status` and `qs setup` print 'ready' / 'key verified' for ANY key, so the 401/403 rejection branches (qs.mjs:543, 560) can never fire. A wrong or expired key only surfaces on the first real /v1/systemone call as exit 3. The skill's first-run flow ('Run qs status first; ready means go') is therefore unreliable on OpenRouter. OpenRouter's own doc says the TypeSafe SDK's models.list() is rejected against OpenRouter because /api/v1/models returns OpenRouter's shape.
corrections.evidence: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-or-v1-bogus' https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models returned 200. skills/quicksilver/scripts/qs.mjs:542-544 and 556-561 check only res.ok. OpenRouter typesafe-sdk.md 'Supported endpoints' says only POST /api/v1/systemone is supported.

corrections.actual: That works (qs.mjs:61 reads JEV_API_KEY, then TYPESAFE_API_KEY), but qs never reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so the key must be duplicated under another name. Putting it in settings.json env exposes it to every Bash command and child process. Neither JEV_API_KEY nor TYPESAFE_API_KEY is in the user's no-secret-leak protected-vars list, and OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not either. QUICKSILVER_API_BASE is also undocumented in README and SKILL.md (it appears only at qs.mjs:10), so the switch is known only from source. There is no host allowlist, so a mistyped base URL would send the Bearer key there.

corrections.claimed: A dead endpoint costs around 5 minutes wall clock per request.
corrections.actual: http() makes 6 attempts (attempt 0..5). Each timeout is 60 s plus back-off sleeps of 0.5+1+2+4+8+16 s, so the worst case is about 6.5 minutes for hangs; fast 5xx/429 failures take about 30 s. Claude Code's Bash tool default timeout is 2 minutes, so the tool call usually times out first and the process is killed. Output is only printed at the end of a run, so a timed-out scan yields nothing. Claude then has to fall back or retry with a larger timeout or run_in_background.

refutedPros: 'Only candidate that is a working, end-to-end Jev integration ... works purely from source-verified schema' is overstated. Nobody ran it, and there is no OpenRouter call in the repo. The OpenRouter path rests on OpenRouter's docs, which say the shapes match (request: model, state, questions; response: model, answers, usage, plus extra id/provider/usage.cost). That is reasonable evidence but not tested.

'Sensible safety defaults: secret-file name regex' is only partly supported. The regex misses many common secret-bearing filenames (see corrections), and --items, stdin and `find` (uncapped) have looser handling.

'OpenRouter switch is config-only ... QUICKSILVER_MODEL=typesafe/jev-1.13' overstates the work. Model needs no change (bare jev-latest is mapped by OpenRouter), but `status`/`setup` become meaningless and the key must be duplicated under JEV_API_KEY.
The '~260 tokens always-on' and '~1.7k tokens on trigger' figures are both off (about 190 and about 2.2k respectively).
addedCons: `qs status`/`qs setup` on OpenRouter return 'ready' for any key because GET /api/v1/models is unauthenticated, so the skill's mandatory first step gives false assurance. A dead or wrong key shows only on the first real call.

Key handling mismatch: qs ignores OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Putting a duplicate JEV_API_KEY in the settings.json env block exposes it to all Bash/child processes, and that name is not in the user's no-secret-leak protected list. Safer options are an exported var in a shell profile, or ~/.quicksilver/config.json (0600) written with a hidden-prompt `setup` run in the user's own terminal, keeping in mind that `status`/`setup` cannot validate the key on OpenRouter.

Secret-guard gaps are larger than the audit lists. No match for .git-credentials, .pgpass, *.tfstate/*.tfvars, service-account JSONs, .docker/config.json, kubeconfig, *.env, wp-config.php, or ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.claude.json. `find` has no per-file size cap beyond 2 MB and sends whole files. For client/NDA repos this is a real leak path that the existing no-secret-leak hook does not cover, because it does not inspect what qs uploads.

No allow rule or `allowed-tools` frontmatter: every `node .../qs.mjs` call is a Bash call that needs approval. In defaultMode 'auto' the permission classifier may prompt or block a script that uploads file contents to an external host (untested here). That undermines the 'automatic, never prompt' goal unless the user adds a Bash allow rule for the exact qs.mjs path.

Unpinned floating alias: the default model 'jev-latest' maps to ~typesafe/jev-latest on OpenRouter, so behaviour and calibration can change silently. Pin 'jev-1.13' for reproducibility. Independent evals also report overconfidence on unanswerable inputs and injection sensitivity, and the author's own bench shows weak spots (BGL F1 23% vs 54%, commits 76% vs 83%, security 89% vs 100%).

Bash timeout interaction: default 2-minute tool timeout versus a 6.5 min worst-case retry loop and output only at the very end. Large scans (3k lines took 64 s; the default --limit is 5000 items) need an explicit timeout or run_in_background.

Docs drift inside the repo: SKILL.md says 8 parallel while code uses 16, and plugin.json version is 0.1.0 while package.json is 0.2.0. There is no CI, tests, releases or issues, 2 commits and 1 contributor, and the package is not on npm (404), so the only install paths are the unpinned GitHub npx or a clone.
gh-uditakhourii-quicksilver.note: Re-queried now: 90 stars, 4 forks, MIT, not archived, created 2026-09-25, 2 commits (2026-09-25), 1 contributor, 0 releases, 0 issues, no tests or CI, not on npm. All of these match the audit. I read all 590 lines of qs.mjs, SKILL.md, bin/quicksilver.mjs and the install scripts. There is no OpenRouter string in the repo, but OpenRouter support is real via QUICKSILVER_API_BASE=https://openrouter.ai/api plus a key in JEV_API_KEY. OpenRouter's docs say its /api/v1/systemone implements TypeSafe's request/response shapes, and qs.mjs uses exactly that shape (state, questions, and answers.*.noul/choice/probabilities/confidence/score/legend, usage.input_tokens). I could not make a live authenticated call, so the OpenRouter response envelope is doc-verified, not tested. The audit's biggest error was claiming the default model 'jev-latest' is invalid on OpenRouter; it is mapped to ~typesafe/jev-latest, so the model env var is optional (pin jev-1.13 anyway). The largest missed gaps are that status/setup cannot validate a key on OpenRouter (the public /models endpoint returns 200 for a fake key), the key must be duplicated under JEV_API_KEY with the protected-vars gap, `find` sends whole files uncapped, and the secret regex misses many secret filenames including the user's own ~/.claude credential files. Auto-invocation is still only model-discretion via a 764-char description. The score stays at 6.5: it is the lowest-overhead, hook-free and MCP-free option, with good ergonomics and honest guidance, but it is a 5-day-old, single-author, untested alpha with an unreliable key check on OpenRouter and a weak egress guard. Recommend a locally pinned copy, model jev-1.13, a Bash allow rule for the exact qs.mjs path, and adding the key env name to the secret-leak hook before use on client repos.

Prompts and raw tool outputs are never written. cache/ is used only by bash-guard (opt-in). Diff/code excerpts (proof/*.json, last-proof.json) exist only when JEV_GATES_PROOF=on.

corrections.actual: Hooks inherit the Claude Code process environment (shell env if launched from it, plus settings.json env). The reason given is wrong. The recommendation also has a side effect: a settings.json env var is exported to every Bash tool call, hook and MCP child, and Claude can print it. It should be added to the user's no-secret-leak.cjs protected-vars list, or the 0600 ~/.config/typesafe/key file used (which also needs to be blocked from the Read tool). Also, spawnBroker only deletes TYPESAFE_API_KEY and JEV_API_KEY from the detached broker's env, so an OPENROUTER_API_KEY exported for other reasons is copied into the long-lived broker process env.
corrections.evidence: lib/jev.mjs:83 (key lookup order TYPESAFE_API_KEY, JEV_API_KEY, then file); lib/broker.mjs:77-80 (env copy, only two vars removed).

The user's settings env overrides PATH and the user notes absolute paths are needed in hook commands. If node is not on that PATH the hook exits 127 (non-blocking error) on every Stop, so the plugin silently does nothing. That is fail-open, but it defeats the purpose. Likely fix: make sure the overridden PATH contains the node dir, or bypass the plugin's hooks.json and wire the Stop hook by hand in settings.json with an absolute node path (the path then contains the versioned plugin cache dir).

A broker call that was accepted and then times out throws and does not retry directly (about 8 s).

refutedPros: 'Uses Jev for what it is good at ... keeps user/assistant text verbatim, avoiding a lossy LLM summary' is only half true: dropping the summary means no record of decisions or progress. A wrong low score deletes tool calls silently, and the messages the hook rebuilds carry no engine handle (types/claude-code.d.ts:7203-7208), so they are reconstructed from role, text and tool blocks only.

'Genuinely automatic ... zero context cost' holds only after setting CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS=1. Without the flag the 2.1.285 binary refuses to load hook modules for installed plugins, so it is a silent no-op. Its automatic behavior is also broader than 'on compaction': it fires on speculative precompute dispatches.

'Hard-coded ZDR is the only candidate that treats egress as a privacy problem' is a comparison claim about other candidates that this check could not test. It is also overstated on a plain reading, because the whole transcript still goes to OpenRouter on every run.
addedCons: The hook never filters on event.trigger or event.agentId, so it also runs on the engine's speculative 'precompute' compactions (binary logs 'precomputed compact ... attempt N') and on subagent/fork transcripts. Whole-transcript egress and Jev cost can happen without a user-visible compaction, and possibly several times per session.
$.http.fetch (HttpInit) offers no timeout option, so the missing timeout cannot be fixed inside the hook, only by the host.

Compaction is atomic across batches: Promise.all means one failed batch (ZDR reject, 429, malformed answer) discards all Jev work and falls back to the built-in summary. On transient OpenRouter errors the user pays latency for nothing, and there is no retry.

Given defaultMode 'auto' and frequent bypassPermissions sessions, tool inputs (bash commands, Write/Edit content, diffs, file paths) for client projects leave the machine to OpenRouter. The hook sends them without user-visible consent or a per-project opt-out, and the hook has no allow/deny list.

Reduction is measured in characters (messageChars), not tokens, and uses a fixed 25% floor. If the context stays above 60% after a kept-history compaction, turn.complete retries with no cooldown. Each retry re-sends up to ~25k-token states, so a long session can burn repeated OpenRouter requests and toasts.
Upstream popularity (7.2k stars) does not transfer to this fork: it is a 3-commit detached copy pushed once, with 0 issues and 0 releases and nothing run on real sessions.

OPENROUTER_API_KEY must be in the environment of the process that starts the hook. The audit's suggestion of the settings.json env block also exposes the key to every Bash tool call and to Claude itself. The existing no-secret-leak hook does not list OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so it would not stop `echo $OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. A tiny wrapper script that reads the key from a 0600 file and execs holstered would keep it out of the session env. The protected-vars list should be updated either way.

Low marginal value for THIS user: ~/.claude/skills holds only 13 skills (dougthepug-design, empat-design, find-skills and 10 gitnexus-*, plus a 'synced' entry), and ~/.agents/skills holds 4. The plugin skills (caveman:*, anthropic-skills:*, etc.) live outside the scanned $HOME roots (roots.rs:14-23). Claude Code already sees these 13 skills in its own listing (skillListingBudgetFraction 0.02), so routing them via a paid, ~1s-per-prompt network call gains little.

Stateless: nothing dedups across turns (no session state in src/). The same SKILL.md body (up to 8,000 bytes) is re-injected on every matching prompt, with a forced 'Follow it for this task' directive that overrides Claude's own judgement about whether to load the skill. Under the 10,000-char per-hook additionalContext cap (Claude Code docs), 8,000 bytes plus headers just fits, but three picks lose most of each body to truncation.

Every prompt's skill-shortlist descriptions (local skill names and descriptions) are sent out as well as the prompt text. The user prompt (which may carry injected instructions from pasted content) is also the Jev state, so a poisoned paste could steer which local skill gets force-injected. The blast radius is limited to installed skills.

polyhook caller detection is env-first (POLYHOOK_CALLER, CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION, ..., GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR) before JSON heuristics. A stray GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR or CURSOR_SESSION_ID in the environment would make it emit the wrong output format for Claude Code, and the failure is silent. The chain is polyhook 0.2.0 -> polyhook-core 0.2.0, a second young single-author dependency that is also a supply-chain hop.

Floating model alias `~typesafe/jev-latest` (not pinned to jev-1.13) means routing behaviour can change silently. The /alpha endpoint has no SLA. Every prompt pays a ~1s median network call, and up to 8s on an outage with no circuit breaker.
Skill discovery does a full WalkDir with follow_links(true), reading every SKILL.md on each prompt. This is cheap with 13 skills, but it is unbounded work with symlinks.
gh-tupe12334-holstered.note: Verified from source: Jev via OpenRouter is native. It POSTs to https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY and model ~typesafe/jev-latest (a real OpenRouter alias). The request is one `choice` question over the BM25 top-20 skills plus `none`, and the answer is read from answers.skill.choice/probabilities. Claude Code correctness is confirmed: polyhook-core emits hookSpecificOutput{hookEventName:"UserPromptSubmit", additionalContext}, and `{}` for approve, which is valid for UserPromptSubmit. All error, timeout and missing-key paths exit 0 with no output (main.rs:33-39), and any other exit code is non-blocking per the Claude Code docs, so it fails open. There is no shell exec, no telemetry, no install scripts and no key in argv, and the npm package has only optionalDependencies; the audit's security claims hold. The audit's substance is largely right, but it has wrong line references throughout, a wrong 'no Node at runtime' claim for the npm route, a stale 60s timeout claim, stale eval numbers, and it missed the PATH and key-exposure problems in this specific environment. The integration model is right (automatic and fail-open), but the value to this user is narrow: only 13 personal skills are scanned, plugin skills are ignored, and Claude already lists them. Each prompt sends its text and skill descriptions to OpenRouter and TypeSafe and adds ~1s. The project is 5 days old with a single maintainer and 4 stars. A hardened setup would use a built-from-source binary, an absolute-path user hook, a key-file wrapper, HOLSTERED_TIMEOUT_MS around 2000, and OPENROUTER_API_KEY added to the secret-leak guard. Even then it stays a skill router, not general Jev decision support. Clone used: <scratch path> (HEAD 5c29a03 = latest v1.4.0). Plugin is a single-author 10-day-old project with rapid churn (README stale vs hooks, runtime rewritten Python->TS at 0.24.0 on 2026-09-26); auto-updating plugin means new third-party code runs in every hook with user privileges.

addedCons: Output has no default size cap (DEFAULT_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES = 0). A successful query on a 6k-file root printed 10k lines; a no-answer query printed 5.4 MB. That would flood or overflow Claude Code's context or its Bash output limit, and issue #40 (spend and output budgets) is still open.

Latency and timeout mismatch with Claude Code: large-root queries take 65-385 s (issues #38, #41), versus a 120 s default Bash timeout. The SKILL.md instructs 'wait on that session/process ID', wording that does not match Claude Code's Bash tool, so long searches risk timeout or partial output.

The tool ignores OPENROUTER_API_KEY, so the user needs a second, unmanaged copy of the key. Piping the key via printf in a Claude-run Bash command would put it in a tool call, so it should be run in the user's own terminal.

Skill's Setup step says to run `npm install --global @dzhng/jevgrep@latest` when jg is missing. The model would run it unprompted, unpinned, under bypassPermissions. jg skill uses `npx --yes skills add` from the repo tip (issue #21 open to pin it).

bypassPermissions plus a tool that uploads repo contents means a prompt-injected repo file could steer the model to run jg on a broad root, or to pass --include-sensitive, --include-dependencies or a parent root. Only the query and files are sent, but the flags are model-controlled.

addedCons: Writes Git objects into every repo's .git store on each prompt and edit (git hash-object -w of the untracked working tree via a scratch index), including untracked non-ignored files. Bare 'jevgate' in the hook command plus the user's overridden PATH: if the binary is not on the hook PATH, four events emit 'could not check' noise and nothing is reviewed. The plugin hooks cannot take an absolute path, so this needs a hand-written hooks block.

OPENROUTER_API_KEY must be in the environment Claude Code launches hooks with (or saved via 'jevgate auth login', which takes precedence). refutedPros: Egress hygiene claim 'per-repo consent (agent cannot grant it)... client repos can simply stay un-consented': overstated. Consent is stored in the repo's own committed .system1/config.yaml, so a cloned or untrusted repo can carry consent=true plus an arbitrary endpoint (load.ts:146,154,319). It is not a user-side gate.

'Zero context tax... Stop hook injects a one-line status per stop': the status is a user-visible systemMessage, not injected context. The context cost is lower than the audit says, but the model is also not informed of 'not checked' outcomes.

'Only candidate I inspected that delivers automatic use without a prompt': comparative claim about other candidates, not verifiable here. Also, the auto part is narrow: the routing hint is a local regex over the user's prompt and never fires on Claude's own mid-task judgement. The one deterministic piece, Stop done-check, needs user-written criteria in TASK.md or .system1/done.md and per-repo enablement.
'scrubber 20+ secret regex': 15 rules.
addedCons: Repo-controlled trust boundary (missed security issue): a committed .system1/config.yaml can set egress.consent.granted=true, enable the done-check guard, and set `endpoint` to any http(s) URL. Every `decide` call then sends the user's OPENROUTER_API_KEY as a Bearer header, plus scrubbed repo content, to that URL. Any cloned third-party or client repo becomes a key-exfiltration and consent-bypass vector. This is worse in defaultMode auto and bypassPermissions sessions, and the Stop hook can trigger it with no agent action. Mitigations for this user: never install the plugin globally without an env-level SYSTEM1_ENDPOINT pin (env beats both files, load.ts:~176), or use a low-limit dedicated OpenRouter key, and review .system1/config.yaml in any freshly cloned repo before starting a session.

OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not in the user's no-secret-leak protected-vars list. The key must reach hook and Bash processes through the settings env or the ~/.config/system1/credentials file. That means an extra secret in the environment of every Claude Bash call, so update the guard first.

Auto-invocation does not cover Claude's autonomous decisions: the UserPromptSubmit hint is a local regex over the user's own prompt. It steers only when the user words a batch or judgement request, and Opus can still ignore it (66% unaided, 91% with the hint on the author's own blind set).

done-check has a low-friction failure mode but real friction in practice: it blocks a stop when Claude stops to ask a question in 9 of 12 measured cases (docs/guard.md). It needs curated criteria files in each repo, and writes .system1/ state (guard/state.json, config, ledger) into the working tree, so client repos need a .gitignore decision.

Data leaves via OpenRouter to TypeSafe (alpha endpoint, no SLA) and the scrubber is 15 regexes with self-described 'safety net, not a guarantee'. Any client contract that forbids third-party code transfer applies once consent is granted.

Very young project: created 2026-09-22, 9 npm versions in 8 days, 0 stars, no GitHub release, a single human author who is the only user. Alpha-endpoint churn or author abandonment is likely to break it, and the plugin pins to the exact npm version 0.5.1.

corrections.claimed: Worst case is about 30 s or more of blocking (10 s per attempt, 2 retries, 500 ms to 5 s backoff).
corrections.actual: Understated. The 30 s figure only holds for timeouts. DEFAULT_RETRY_POLICY has respectRetryAfter true and maxRetryAfterMs 60000, so a 429 or 503 with Retry-After up to 60 s is honored before each retry, giving up to about 2 x 60 s of sleep plus attempts. Timeout is 'per attempt, without a total retry budget' and there is no total-deadline option, so a hook must use an external AbortSignal or a maxRetries:0 policy. The audit's mitigation (timeout 1-2 s, maxRetries 0) is right, but the number is wrong.

Weak as a stability pro.

'OpenRouter works by configuration alone' is overstated: it is documented-compatible and code-plausible but untested, with a 32k-context vs 60k-request-limit mismatch and a maintainer issue (#63) still open to verify it.

'Not in the critical path ... an outage cannot block Claude Code' is true, but the same holds for any manually invoked CLI; it is not a differentiating pro for AUTOMATIC use, and the no-timeout bare fetch means a hung connection can stall a Bash tool call in Claude Code until the tool timeout.
addedCons: Not automatic: model-discretion skill only, plus per-repo file. `perch setup claude-code` writes .claude/skills/perch/SKILL.md into each working tree (dirties client repos unless gitignored) and the author himself concedes description matching is unreliable (setup.js:35-46); Claude Code has no alwaysApply equivalent, so it does not meet the user's 'never have to prompt' requirement without a self-built hook.

The published 0.3.5 has no Cloud mode, no rolling-pool concurrency and no parser-download retries; the audit's described behavior (and 0.4.0's Cloud key-as-token path) will change on the next release (PR #156 open), so the recommended env config may behave differently after an upgrade.

Misconfiguration leaks the OpenRouter key: after 0.4.0, PERCH_API_KEY without PERCH_BASE_URL sends the key to dash.perchscan.com; in 0.3.5 it goes to api.typesafe.ai. PERCH_BASE_URL is required, must be the full URL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone (not the /api base), and OPENROUTER_API_KEY itself is not read (must be re-exported as PERCH_API_KEY, and it is not in the user's secret-guard list).

Prompt-injection/evasion: code under scan is untrusted state fed to Jev, and per the Jev evals injected instructions in state can move answers (e.g., a comment can suppress a finding), so a clean perch scan on hostile or client code is weak evidence; repo-defined rules (perch.yaml, .perch/rules) also shape the questions and any rule text surfaced in output goes back into the agent's context.

Bare fetch with no timeout in direct mode (systemone.js:34, also in 0.3.5), so a stalled connection blocks the tool call; 32-way concurrency at HEAD can also trip OpenRouter/TypeSafe 429s on the alpha endpoint (no SLA), which it handles by retrying 4 times with 2/4/8 s backoff.

Runtime dependency on GitHub releases for tree-sitter parsers (native/wasm code fetched at first use) plus ~4 MB unpacked bundle; scan reads git HEAD not the worktree, so uncommitted edits are only covered by `check`, and known open bug #218 means check findings on uncommitted code cannot be closed/deduped.

refutedPros: Fail-open everywhere. Not true for the deny path: regex hard denies (SECRET_REF plus NET_SEND, e.g. a command mentioning .env, .pem or .claude/settings.json together with git push, gh api, curl or the word socket) and Jev deny (touches_secrets>=0.7 with network>=0.5, or deny>=0.8) are blocks. In bypass mode there is no prompt to override them, so false denies stop work outright. Only Jev outages fail open.

README claims deny honoured in bypassPermissions is a safety net for a bypass user. The author's e2e test used one harmless command in the desktop app and headless claude -p, not a Linux terminal session. It is supported but thinly tested.
Matches the OpenRouter route with only key/model env changes. Unproven: the noul criteria field and the dict state shape are not in OpenRouter's documented schema, so 'no fork needed' is unverified.
Backups plus uninstall script as a pro for this user. install.sh is zsh, macOS-oriented and would rewrite settings.json, and the user should not run it. This is a con for this user, not a pro.
addedCons: Possible OpenRouter schema mismatch (noul criteria field on every noul question and dict-valued state versus the documented string state and criteria-less noul). If rejected, all Jev features silently no-op while the regex layer keeps running, and the user may believe Jev is active.

Regex hard-deny layer is macOS-tuned and prone to false positives with no override in bypass: SECRET_REF matches any mention of .env, .pem, .ssh or .claude/settings.json, and NET_SEND matches git push, gh api, curl or a bare socket. Example: git rm --cached .env && git push is denied outright, and a Jev deny in bypass mode blocks a command the user chose to run without prompts.

Jev is documented as overconfident on unanswerable input and injectable through state. The gate feeds it untrusted script contents (8000 chars) and command text. In auto mode any Jev ask or deny choice under 0.8 becomes a prompt, so miscalibration becomes friction in the user's default mode.

Ask-to-silent-pass in bypass mode means the Jev gray-zone review adds latency (about 1 s per gray command) and egress in bypass sessions but only ever blocks on hard deny, so its benefit there is small relative to cost.

Gray-zone Bash commands and script contents (client code, up to 8000 chars, regex-redacted) go to OpenRouter, and every user prompt of 15+ chars (first 4000 chars) is sent on UserPromptSubmit, for client projects with unverified retention. OpenRouter also sees the roster of installed skill names and descriptions.

Putting it in the settings.json env block also puts it in a file the gate itself treats as secret.

Only the permission gate and prompt router yield automatic value. Skill routing overlaps with Claude Code's own skill matching, though it may help since skillListingBudgetFraction 0.02 truncates the skill list. The rest (jev-* agents pinned to claude-opus-5-5, dispatch router, jevpack, jevqa needing a second repo, sips) is inert or macOS-only for this user.

The skills teach Claude to write onesie pipelines. None route Claude Code's own decisions through Jev, so the automatic-use goal is unmet with no custom hook. The skills add always-on listing cost (about 1.9k chars of descriptions) with little daily benefit, since the user's skillListingBudgetFraction is 0.02. Bodies are 5-16 KB each when triggered.

The skills carry `allowed-tools: Bash(onesie:*)`, which pre-approves any onesie invocation while a skill is active. A model-written `onesie --state-file <path>` could send file contents to OpenRouter without a prompt. The user's no-secret-leak hook still inspects Bash, but OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not in its protected list.

Every Bash command string goes to OpenRouter (32k context, alpha endpoint, no SLA) if used as a PreToolUse gate. Commands with inline tokens or client hostnames would leave the machine. A regex pre-filter is required for client projects.

Jev's known weaknesses apply directly to this gate: injected text inside a command can shift the score (echo 'rm -rf /' style cases), it is overconfident on unanswerable input, and it is sensitive to label swaps. It must not replace deterministic rules.

In Claude Code, a PreToolUse hook exit code other than 0 or 2 is non-blocking (fail-open), and exit 2 blocks. A wrapper script must translate onesie's exits explicitly (1 to deny, 7 to ask, 2/3/4/5 to allow). Do not pass onesie's exit code through unmapped. The default hook timeout is 600s, so the wrapper must set --timeout and --retries or it can stall for about 30s on outages.

gh-dizk-jev-lens.note: Verified: repo facts (1 star, MIT, not archived, 79 commits, created 2026-09-18, last push 2026-09-19); hook events and fields are valid in 2.1.285 (PostToolUse updatedToolOutput, MessageDisplay, UserPromptSubmit) and the Read/Bash shapes match; Claude Code runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts` from a plugin's package-lock.json (binary strings), so the install path holds and no install scripts run. OpenRouter is a config-only switch documented by OpenRouter (TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api, OpenRouter key, default model jev-latest maps to ~typesafe/jev-latest); no live call made (no key, no candidate code executed). Audit errors corrected: recall path traversal is sanitized (safeName), MCP server is not dependency-free, the gitnexus-conflict con is overstated (that hook never writes updatedToolOutput), MessageDisplay spawns per streamed batch, 4xx errors fail open instantly and silently. Score lowered from 7 to 6: it is the only truly automatic, fail-open candidate with small context cost, but it is 12 days old, single-author, unmeasured on Claude Code, lossy for Read-then-Edit on code (only 31 percent savings on code, with author-reported 2.2 percent dropped-identifier harm), ships client code and command output to a third party on every large result with plaintext local retention, and can silently degrade to a mock classifier. Recommendation: trial on personal projects only, with JEV_LENS_MODEL pinned to jev-1.13, key in key.json (not exported env), key path added to the secret guard, and check /jev-lens:stats for mock=false and recall rate before any client work.

permission-gate.summary: Category: hooks that turn Jev's typed probabilities into allow, ask or deny decisions on Claude Code tool calls. Most of the 60 members are young, single-author alpha repos, 0 to 5 stars. Most are hard-wired to api.typesafe.ai. OpenRouter-native ones are toolgate, blastgate, Rahul's jev-auto-mode, jevexec, failproofai and leepokai's jev-guard (HEAD only). Several others switch with a one-line or env change (nafiurrahmanniloy jev-guard, greghavens jev-scope-control, yanmad27 ask-jev, agent-reflex). Evidence is self-reported and small-n. For this user (defaultMode auto, frequent bypassPermissions, Anthropic's classifier already in place) the value is a cheap, low-latency second opinion that can only add prompts or denials. It is not a prompt-remover. The wrong event is the PermissionRequest cookbook and several 'auto-approver' repos, because that event does not fire in the user's normal modes.
permission-gate.mechanism: Deterministic command hooks in settings.json or a plugin, which is exactly the 'never say use jev' wiring. PreToolUse fires before any permission-mode check in every mode, including bypassPermissions. It emits hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision allow, ask or deny, and precedence across hooks is deny > defer > ask > allow. A hook deny is binding even in bypass. A hook ask forces a prompt in auto mode (documented). Whether an ask prompts in bypassPermissions is undocumented and unverified. PermissionRequest fires only when a prompt would actually show (ask rules, hook ask, critical-path rm). It does not fire in auto for classifier-decided actions or in bypass, so the official OpenRouter cookbook hook is mostly inert for this user. Typical hook flow: static regex or fast-path first, then one POST to openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions (model typesafe/jev-1.13) or /api/v1/systemone with Noul, Choice or Score questions over the redacted command plus recent user prompts, then thresholds in code. Any hook timeout or crash is non-blocking, so it fails open to the normal flow.
permission-gate.builtInAlternative: Claude Code already has: allow/ask/deny rules; the auto-mode classifier (Sonnet 5 by default). The classifier sees user messages, tool calls and CLAUDE.md, but never tool results, and blocks exfiltration, remote-code-execution style actions and pushes to untrusted remotes. It also has deterministic PreToolUse command hooks (the user's no-secret-leak.cjs), prompt and agent hooks (an LLM yes/no with no extra infrastructure), PermissionDenied and PermissionRequest events, and critical-path rm protection. Jev is far cheaper and faster (about $0.042 per 1M input tokens, p50 about 200 ms, p95 about 600 ms). Independent evals put it roughly at parity with a frontier LLM on bounded action gates (100/111 vs 102/111, and 55/60 vs Sonnet 5), with clearly worse calibration. It is overconfident on unanswerable inputs, steerable by injected text in state, and on the /alpha endpoint with no SLA. Its edge is being a fast, cheap, typed extra vote on top of the native classifier. It cannot be a better one, and the user's static rules and no-secret-leak hook cover most of the same ground with no egress.
permission-gate.worthItReason: Anthropic's classifier plus the user's deny rules and no-secret-leak hook already gate most risk, and Jev is not a better judge (accuracy a bit below mid-price LLMs; 1.0 probability on 56% of answers, 9 of them wrong). Most 'auto-approver' repos remove prompts, which the user in auto and bypass modes mostly does not have, and PermissionRequest hooks and gates keyed on default/acceptEdits mode do nothing there. What remains is Jev as an add-only layer: deny or ask on things like out-of-scope commits, pushes, deploys or unrequested edits, especially in bypass sessions where a hook deny is the only certain brake. Costs are real. Every judged call adds about 0.3 to 1 s and sends commands, prompts and sometimes code to OpenRouter and TypeSafe, which needs a data-policy check for client projects. Every candidate is days to weeks old, and no study measures the false-approve rate on real Claude Code traffic. Worth a shadow-mode trial on personal projects with a narrow scope. Not a daily must-have, and not something to run on client repos without a data-handling decision.
