final.customGlue: Everything is in <scratch path> (36 files, 356 KB; copy to <repo> first: /tmp is a tmpfs at 99%, 323 MB free). Installed code is 1,283 lines of Node built-ins only (shellclass 451, jevlib 275, brake 116, mcp 98, doctor ~100, webscreen 71, skeleton 68, probe 55, report 41, questions 16); tests: classify 144 + e2e 46 = 190 pass (offline, local mock of the OpenRouter endpoint, temp git repos), shelf gate 28 pass. I started from the max design's tree and applied: (P1) trust boundary: passwd home, argv-only test flag, no env path/binary overrides, taint guard, redirect:'error', 0600+uid checks, ZDR forced, realpath + conservative env/cwd root classes; (P2) key file ~/.config/jev/.env; (P3) /api/v1/systemone + family model pin + expected_model drift => no enforcement; (P4) scrubbed git environment, fsmonitor/hooks off, no index lock; (P5) JEV_ACK removed; (P6) core set + t1_enforce/t2_enforce per rule id + t1_scope subagents; (P7) T1 false-positive fixes found by replay (main :old-branch, /run/user and /dev/shm scratch, tamper-in-code heuristic split out of the core); (P8) unjudgeable rm -rf $VAR never sent; (P9) webscreen: root classes, curl vs gh split, dedupe by tool_use_id, web_trusted_hosts, watchdog; (P10) MCP deferred, no alwaysLoad; (P11) shared questions.cjs, probe.cjs + 24-case probe set; (P12) doctor with behavioural guard check and live diagnosis; (P13) report with agent split, core/shadow/scope_skipped, error rate, last successful call; (P14) install kit: settings-snippet (async web handlers in log phase), merge-settings.sh (idempotent, backup, --web-sync; tested on a copy of your real settings.json: unrelated sections unchanged, second run 'no change needed'), policy.example.json, claude-md-block.txt, mcp-add.txt, guard-patch.diff + guard-test-cases.py (verified on a copy of your guard), INSTALL.txt; (P15) skill rebuilt with the new addendum; (P16) stop-shadow, perm-gate and the pragmatic jev-gate moved to shelf/; (P17) backtest/volume.cjs answers 'what would each choice of personal roots send to Jev' from your own transcripts (counts only). Architects' original trees stay under .../wf2/design-*. NOT verified (no key, no live Claude Code run): authenticated calls to /api/v1/systemone (model id, zdr/data_collection acceptance, rate limits under ~16 parallel agents, real score distributions); that '!' bypasses PreToolUse; that hooks fire in Workflow subagents under bypass (docs say yes); skill activation; T2 precision; injection hit rate; guardrail features on your plan.
final.expectedValue: Honest and small on the Claude Code side, real on the app-building side. (b) skill: value scales with how often you build bounded-decision features (only you know); each gets correct OpenRouter wiring, pinned model, none-option, 2 s timeout, fallback and a client-data check on the first pass; runtime cost of a decision ~$0.00002 at p50 ~0.2 s versus ~1.1-2.0 s for an LLM call (OpenRouter blog, 60 tickets, approximate). (a) brake: T1 core+subagents would have blocked ~7 commands in 21 days (0.33/day) and shadow-logged 14 main-thread ones; that is insurance for a bad day (Sonnet subagents run ~137k Bash calls per 3 weeks), and it is deterministic, not Jev. Jev's own contribution is the T2 gray zone, expected to yield a handful of true vetoes per month at best and possibly none - plan to delete it after 14 days of shadow unless labelled data says otherwise. Tripwire: cheap insurance, probably a few genuine hits per month at most. Triage: unknown adoption. What does NOT change: no component saves subscription quota except a working triage cascade; permission prompts (you have essentially none), model quality (Opus 5.5) and code review are not improved by Jev. What would change my mind: a labelled shadow log with several true T2 vetoes, or a triage trial showing routine use.
risks: Live behaviour unverified: nobody used a key. Unknown until 'doctor --live': acceptance of provider zdr/data_collection on /api/v1/systemone, response model string, rate limits under bursts of ~16 parallel agents (429 => fail-open + breaker), real score distributions. 'probe' and the canaries are the acceptance tests.

T2 precision is a base-rate trap: ~2.9k gray commands per 21 days, a handful of real dangers, an overconfident model (saturates at 1.0 on ~56% of answers, moves under injected text, wrong on unanswerable input) and a text-only view (no idea what a script or $VAR does). It may be net-negative; it is deny-only, shadow-only and deletable.

A deny inside an unattended subagent stops that step and relies on the lead to report it; false positives cost time. There is no agent-typable override by design (the human override is '!'). Whether a subagent, told not to work around a deny, will still find a workaround is untested; the brake is accident prevention, not an adversarial boundary.

Project settings can defeat the hooks: a project's .claude/settings*.json may set disableAllHooks or define its own hooks/env (hooks-guide: it overrides yours). The trust-boundary hardening stops accidental redirection, not a malicious repo you have trusted. Audit client repos for such settings.

The key file is readable by any process that runs as you: an agent with arbitrary code execution could load the lib and print the key. The guard, deny rules and T1 tamper rule raise the bar; the $5 credit limit and ZDR-only routing bound the damage.

Egress and classification errors: commands (personal roots), public page text (personal+unknown roots) and item snippets go to OpenRouter then TypeSafe (hosted, closed source, alpha route family, no SLA). Regex redaction is best effort. 72.5% of your Bash calls are in roots that are 'unknown' until you classify Dev/* and websites/*; a wrongly classified client root would leak commands (default for unlisted = off).

The injection tripwire sees WebFetch summaries, not raw pages, and is beaten by adaptive text; benign 'for AI agents' docs (llms.txt, AGENTS.md) will be flagged and need web_trusted_hosts. gh reads of private repos in personal roots are sent to Jev unless you remove those handlers.

Skill activation is model-discretion and the description is the first thing dropped under the 2% listing budget: the CLAUDE.md pointer and the /doctor check are the mitigation; check on the first few real features. The vendored upstream text tells Claude to read live docs (an injection channel).

Maintenance: ~1.3k lines and regex tables to own (about 15 min per quarter plus re-labelling after any model change), hook semantics can change with Claude Code updates, and a Node upgrade that breaks the ~/.nvm/current symlink makes the hooks exit 127 (a visible non-blocking hook error in interactive sessions, but silent for unattended subagents): run doctor after upgrades.
Fail-open by design means a dead feature looks like a working one: report prints the last successful Jev call and the fail-open reasons; read it weekly for the first month.

The reference tree lives on a tmpfs at 99%: copy it out first. After the guard patch Claude cannot use $OPENROUTER_API_KEY in Bash, and after the deny rules it cannot edit the installed hooks (updates are done by you from the git repo).
final.latencyBudget: Measured on this machine: the brake's T0 path takes p50 16.6 ms / p95 18.5 ms wall (bare `node -e 0` is 10.6 / 12.4 ms), runs in parallel with no-secret-leak and gitnexus (p50 ~18 ms, p95 ~123 ms, up to seconds on cold indexes), so added wall time is ~0-6 ms on 98.1% of Bash calls. A T1 deny costs the same. T2 with a Jev call: ~0.3-0.8 s (Jev p50 ~194 ms / p95 ~633 ms per OpenRouter, plus TLS) on ~20/day under today's personal roots (~96/day if Dev/* and websites/* become personal), deadline 2.5 s, hook timeout 6 s. Web tripwire: 0 added while async in the log phase; in the warn phase +0.35-0.9 s per screened read (~740/day => ~5 min/day aggregated across parallel agents, negligible per agent). Triage: 2-4 s per 400-item call, only when Claude calls it. Skill: none. Outage worst case: 5 failing calls at up to 2.5 s/4 s, then the breaker skips Jev for 5 minutes at 0 ms; watchdogs exit silently at 5.2 s (brake) and 6.5 s (webscreen) before any Claude Code timeout.
final.costEstimate: Jev is $0.042 per 1M input tokens, output free. T2: ~1.1k tokens = $0.00005 per call => ~$0.001/day today (~$0.005/day if Dev/websites are personal). Web tripwire: 0.5-3.4k tokens => avg ~$0.0001 => ~$0.074/day at ~740 screens/day. Triage: ~$0.004 per 400 items. Probe: ~$0.0005 per run. Total about $0.08/day (~$2.4/month) at today's roots; hard caps: $0.50/day in the hooks, $5 credit limit on the OpenRouter key. No Claude subscription quota is spent by any Jev call. Human time: ~90 min to install, ~30 min at day 4, ~30 min at day 14, ~15 min at day 30, ~15 min per quarter.
final.privacy: Leaves the machine only via OpenRouter (provider zdr:true + data_collection:deny forced; the TypeSafe endpoint is on OpenRouter's public ZDR list, checked today; OpenRouter stores prompts only if you opt in) to TypeSafe (hosted, closed source; provider record: no training, no retention; direct ZDR is enterprise-only). What is sent: T2 (personal roots only, judgeable commands only): redacted command <=1.8k chars, <=5 code windows around destructive patterns, agent description <=200 chars, last real user message <=400 chars, git facts, matched rule ids; web tripwire: public page/raw curl text <=12k chars for personal+unknown roots (gh reads: personal only), host only - never URL, query, cwd, prompt or session id; triage: item texts <=700 chars, personal roots only. Never sent: files, transcripts, env, keys, anything from client roots (command, triage, Bash reads and, by default, web text), commands from unknown roots, T1 (local only), secret-shaped strings (redacted). Local: ~/.local/state/jev logs (0600, 30 days) hold redacted commands for personal roots and name-free skeletons elsewhere; the key lives only in ~/.config/jev/.env (0600, guarded). Per-root policy is in your home config, never in a repo; kill switch = touch ~/.config/jev/OFF. Check openrouter.ai/settings/privacy (leave logging off) and get a client-contract answer before enabling anything beyond personal roots.
final.isJevWorthIt: For building with Jev (meaning b): yes - about 120 tokens resident, and the one place where Jev's speed, price and typed output beat what Claude Code already has. For Claude Code's own decisions (meaning a): mostly no - the protection that matters in your bypass sessions is deterministic (the T1 brake, guard hardening) and would exist without Jev; Jev's gray-zone veto and the injection tripwire are cheap shadow experiments with delete rules, and the triage tool is a trial. If you want the minimum: guard patch + deny rules + skill + T1 shadow->enforce (no key needed). Add the key and the Jev stages only if you accept the egress and will spend the 30 minutes of labelling that decides whether they stay.

judge.thoughts:
Candid version.

WHERE JEV REALLY HELPS
1. Inside products you build. A typed, roughly calibrated, 0.2 s, $0.00002 decision beats a fragile 'return JSON' prompt for routing, triage, moderation and gating, and Claude cannot know the API (launched Sept 2026, after its June 2026 cutoff). So the vendored skill is the only part that makes Jev 'automatic' in a way that really matters: it fires when the task is a decision feature, without you saying 'jev'. How much that is worth depends on how often you build such features; only you know.
2. Bulk cascade screening (jev_triage) is the one thing Claude cannot do cheaply by itself, but I would not bet on it: tools that rely on model discretion were called 0 of 150 times unprompted in the only public bench. Also, Workflow scripts are plain JS without HTTP, so a Jev call can only appear in your dominant workflow through an agent calling an MCP tool. Treat it as a 3-week trial.
3. A semantic second look at gray-zone Bash in unattended runs. Be honest about it: almost all of the protection is the deterministic part, which is not Jev. Replayed on your own last 21 days, the default enforcement (core rules, subagents only) would have blocked about 7 commands (3 rm -rf .git, 2 git clean -fdx, 1 wide find -delete, tamper) and shadow-logged 14 main-thread ones (9 force pushes, 3 history rewrites, 3 gh repo admin). That is insurance for a bad day, not a daily win. The Jev part has a base-rate problem: ~2.9k gray commands, a handful of real dangers, a 1% false-deny rate roughly halves precision, and 23% of them (rm -rf $VAR) cannot be judged from text. Expect to delete that stage after two weeks of shadow.
4. The injection tripwire is cheap insurance with a low base rate. WebFetch returns a small model's summary, so the raw channels (curl, gh) matter more; a crafted evidence-like line takes detection from 96.5% to 26.5%, so it catches blunt attacks only.

WHERE IT IS HYPE OR REDUNDANT FOR YOU
Permission auto-approval (22 days of main transcripts: 2,762 bypass, 17 plan, 0 auto/default; the PermissionRequest cookbook hook has nothing to do, and in auto mode a stronger transcript-aware classifier decides first). Model/effort/skill routing (Opus 5.5 can only be downgraded; proxies sit on your OAuth traffic and disable tool search). Context pruning and compaction (lossy, unredacted originals on disk, early-access function hooks). Stop verifiers (the one A/B showed no gain, AUROC 0.50-0.64, every false flag burns an Opus turn). Code review and search (Jev is worse than Opus on code judgment: 71.5% accuracy, ECE 0.19; gitnexus and Grep are better). Memory layers (duplicate CLAUDE.md). Nothing here saves subscription quota except a working triage cascade.

WHAT THE ARCHITECTS GOT WRONG THAT I VERIFIED
'openrouter.key' is not protected by your guard (both max and safety assumed it is; a dotenv-named file is). JEV_ACK was agent-typable and spelled out in the deny message. Config, state and git paths were overridable from the environment. T1 had false positives in your own history (main :old-branch, /run/user scratch dirs, a heredoc heuristic that fires while building the hooks). WebFetch is summarised, so the safety design screened the wrong channel. Enforcing in the main thread would mostly block things you asked for.

THE BIGGER LEVERS ARE NOT JEV
block-rm.sh is unwired (the T1 brake supersedes it). A project can set disableAllHooks. You have hundreds of compactions (867 boundary records in 22 days, 57 main sessions), so a SessionStart(compact) hook that re-injects a small pinned-notes file is likely worth more than anything in the Jev stack. And 5.8k subagent transcripts in 22 days is your real quota cost; that is workflow design, not Jev.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY
No key was used, so authenticated route behaviour, ZDR acceptance, rate limits under parallel agents, real score distributions, '!' bypassing hooks, hooks firing in Workflow subagents under bypass, and skill activation are untested. doctor --live, probe and the canaries are how you find out.
judge.multiMcpAnswer: No. Not several servers, and not one from the ecosystem. Best combination: zero MCP servers on day one; deterministic hooks (jev-brake, jev-webscreen) for everything that must happen without model discretion; the vendored skill + CLAUDE.md for app-building knowledge; and, only as a 3-week trial after the hooks are stable, exactly ONE self-hosted stdio server (node, absolute path, no npx, no env block, the process reads the guarded ~/.config/jev/.env itself) exposing exactly ONE tool (jev_triage), deferred by tool search (do not set alwaysLoad). Reasons, each checked: (1) Discretion: MCP tools are chosen by the model; the only measured adoption was 0 of 150 unprompted calls, so extra servers add confusion, not use. (2) Cost is not the problem - docs: with tool search 'only tool names and server instructions load at session start' - but overlap is: gitnexus (17 tools) and playwright (25) already fill the deferred list and community Jev servers ship 5-12 near-identical verbs (ask, verify, screen, find, pick, rank, classify). (3) Egress: MCP arguments are model-composed diffs/logs/code, invisible to your guard (matcher Bash|Read|Grep|NotebookEdit) and executed silently in bypass; several setup helpers put the key in argv or plaintext ~/.claude.json. (4) Startup: bare npx/node under your PATH override (caveman-shrink already fails with CONNECTION_CLOSED); alwaysLoad would make startup wait up to 5 s and cost ~585 tokens every turn. (5) Hooks cannot lean on MCP: command hooks cannot call MCP tools, mcp_tool hooks are skipped at SessionStart and their output is parsed as stdout, so an MCP cannot express a PreToolUse/PermissionRequest decision. (6) Workflow scripts are plain JS with no Node/HTTP API, so in your dominant workflow a Jev call can only come from an agent calling an MCP tool (workflow agents reach session MCP tools via ToolSearch); that is the only real argument for the single trial tool. If you ever want a second verb, add it to the SAME server and extend the guard to mcp__jev__*; never a second server. Delete the server if fewer than one call per week by day 21.
implementationPlan: STEP 0 (5 min, do this first: the reference tree lives on a tmpfs that is 99% full). Run in YOUR terminal: SRC=<scratch path> ; mkdir -p <repo> && cp -a $SRC/. <repo>/ && cd <repo> && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm 'jev: judged reference build'. The same ordered commands are in install/INSTALL.txt (canonical copy). Every step below is run by you; Claude must not touch ~/.claude, ~/.config/jev or the key (deny rules and the T1 tamper rule enforce that once installed).

STEP 1 (15 min) Read and test before trusting: cd <repo> && wc -l jev/lib/*.cjs jev/hooks/*.cjs jev/mcp/*.cjs (about 1.3k lines; read jevlib.cjs, brake.cjs, webscreen.cjs; shellclass.cjs is the rule table). Run HOME=/nonexistent-home/x node --test test/classify.test.cjs test/e2e.test.cjs -> expect tests 190, pass 190 (HOME must not be under /tmp because the classifier treats /tmp as scratch). Then (cd shelf && HOME=/nonexistent-home/x node --test jev-gate.test.cjs) -> tests 28, pass 28.

STEP 2 (10 min) Secret-leak guard: cd ~/.claude/hooks && cp -p no-secret-leak.cjs no-secret-leak.cjs.bak-jev && cp -p no-secret-leak.test.cjs no-secret-leak.test.cjs.bak-jev && patch no-secret-leak.cjs < <repo>/install/guard-patch.diff && python3 <repo>/install/guard-test-cases.py && node no-secret-leak.test.cjs -> ALL PASS (30 cases). The patch adds 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY' after 'GH_TOKEN' in PROTECTED_VARS; the key file is named .env because the guard protects that name and does NOT protect openrouter.key. Side effect: Claude can no longer use $OPENROUTER_API_KEY in Bash.

STEP 3 (15 min) Install code, folders and policy: rm -rf ~/.claude/hooks/jev && mkdir -p ~/.claude/hooks/jev && cp -a <repo>/jev/. ~/.claude/hooks/jev/ ; mkdir -p ~/.config/jev ~/.local/state/jev && chmod 700 ~/.config/jev ~/.local/state/jev ; cp <repo>/install/policy.example.json ~/.config/jev/policy.json && chmod 600 ~/.config/jev/policy.json. Decide the roots with data: node <repo>/backtest/volume.cjs 21 --personal <personal root>,<personal root 2>,<dev root> (counts only; today 72.5% of your Bash calls are in roots that stay 'unknown' until classified; classifying Dev/* and websites/* as personal raises the judgeable T2 volume from ~20/day to ~96/day). Then edit ~/.config/jev/policy.json roots. Run node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/doctor.cjs: FAILs for key, hooks and deny rules are expected now.

STEP 4 (5 min) Register hooks and deny rules (idempotent, writes a backup, leaves everything else untouched; tested on a copy of your real settings.json): bash <repo>/install/merge-settings.sh (dry run, read the diff) then bash <repo>/install/merge-settings.sh --apply. Rollback: cp -p ~/.claude/settings.json.bak-jev-<timestamp> ~/.claude/settings.json. In Claude Code run /hooks: expect PreToolUse Bash +1, PostToolUse WebFetch|WebSearch +1 and Bash +7 (the file watcher normally picks up edits; restart the session if not). All hook commands are exec form with ~/.nvm/current/bin/node, so the PATH override in settings env is irrelevant.

STEP 5 (10 min) Skill and pointer: mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/typesafe-ai && cp <repo>/skill/typesafe-ai/SKILL.md <repo>/skill/typesafe-ai/LICENSE ~/.claude/skills/typesafe-ai/ ; sha256sum ~/.claude/skills/typesafe-ai/SKILL.md -> b5779472954c6992ded0dcf131125db2f20d21fabeb1521d603040e4b00776c0. Append the first two bullets of install/claude-md-block.txt to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md by hand. In Claude Code run /doctor (or /context): the typesafe-ai row must show its description, not only the name; if it is dropped, set the four least-used gitnexus skills to name-only via skillOverrides in settings.json.

STEP 6 (day 0-3, no key needed) Shadow the deterministic brake and collect data. Canary (harmless, local bare remote): mkdir -p <personal root>/jev-canary && cd <personal root>/jev-canary && git init -q -b main work && git init -q --bare remote.git && cd work && git commit -q --allow-empty -m init && git remote add origin ../remote.git && git push -q origin HEAD:main. In Claude Code, in that work dir, ask: 'run git push --force origin HEAD:main'. It runs (shadow) and node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/report.cjs 1 --would shows a T1 would_deny row with agent=main. Let normal work continue for at least 3 days including one heavy day (days above 10k Bash calls happened 4 times in the last 3 weeks).

STEP 7 (day 1, 30 min) OpenRouter side, then the key (your terminal only). In the OpenRouter dashboard: create key 'claude-code-jev' with a $5 credit limit; openrouter.ai/settings/privacy: keep prompt/response logging OFF; optional guardrail on that key (model allowlist typesafe/jev-1.13, ZDR, budget $0.25/day; docs: openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/guardrails; whether your plan has guardrails is unverified). Then: read -rsp 'OpenRouter key: ' K; echo; ( umask 077; printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=%s\n' "$K" > ~/.config/jev/.env ); unset K; chmod 600 ~/.config/jev/.env. Then node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/doctor.cjs --live: everything ok; copy 'response model=...' into policy.json as "expected_model". If the live call FAILs, doctor prints the diagnosis (works without zdr/data_collection => route not no-retention: stop and decide; works only on /api/alpha/decisions => set "endpoint" to the alpha URL). Then node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/probe.cjs, judge the 24-row table by eye, then node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/probe.cjs --save-baseline. Finally node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/doctor.cjs --seal and commit the repo.

STEP 8 (day 3-4, 30 min) T1 review, then enforce the core rules for subagents: node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/report.cjs 4 --would ; label every T1 row right/wrong. Gate: no would_deny on a core rule id that was legitimate work (expect ~1 core hit per day, ~0.3/day in subagents). For each false positive fix jev/lib/shellclass.cjs in the repo, add a case to test/classify.test.cjs, re-run tests, re-copy to ~/.claude/hooks/jev and re-seal; restart the clock for that id only. Then set "mode": {"brake_t1": "enforce"} in ~/.config/jev/policy.json (t1_enforce stays 'core', t1_scope stays 'subagents') and add the brake bullet from claude-md-block.txt to CLAUDE.md. Canary from a SUBAGENT (ask Claude to spawn one that runs the force push): the deny text must appear; a '! git push --force origin HEAD:main' typed by you must still work. Main-thread rows stay shadow; if at day 14 none of them was unwanted, leave them that way, otherwise set t1_scope to 'all'.

STEP 9 (day 4-7) Web tripwire: the web hooks are async and policy webscreen is 'log' (zero latency). After 3-4 days: node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/report.cjs 4 --would ; read the first ~20 flagged rows (host + scores); put benign hosts that address agents on purpose (llms.txt/AGENTS.md style docs) into web_trusted_hosts. If the flagged share is <=1% of screened calls and the rest are genuine agent-directed text: set "webscreen": "warn" and run bash <repo>/install/merge-settings.sh --web-sync --apply (synchronous handlers are required to add context). Otherwise leave it in log, or delete the PostToolUse entries.

STEP 10 (day 14, 30 min) T2 verdict: node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/report.cjs 14 --would ; label at most ~60 rows. Per rule id set t2_enforce only with >=20 labelled would_deny over >=14 days, precision >=90% (at most 2 false in 20), zero cases you had asked for, and at least one true catch that T1 did not already cover; then "brake_t2": "enforce" with "t2_enforce": ["<id>"]. Otherwise set "brake_t2": "off" and delete the Jev stage; nothing else depends on it. Also check report for drift rows and the Jev error rate (gate: under 5% of Jev calls, p95 under 1.5 s, one constant response model).

STEP 11 (day 14-35, optional) jev_triage trial: run the claude mcp add-json command in install/mcp-add.txt (user scope, no env block), add the last bullet of claude-md-block.txt. Day 21: count calls with grep -rho 'mcp__jev__jev_triage' ~/.claude/projects --include=*.jsonl -c over the last 21 days (files modified in that window) and read ~/.local/state/jev logs (c=triage). Fewer than one call per week, or spot-checks that keep showing wrong drops => claude mcp remove jev --scope user.

STEP 12 (day 30, 15 min) Keep/kill review: keep a component only if it produced a confirmed catch or measurable savings, or is free insurance without friction (skill, T1 core, guard patch). Delete T2, the tripwire or the MCP tool when the numbers do not support them. Record the decision in the repo.

STEP 13 (ongoing) Maintenance: after every Node upgrade run node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/doctor.cjs (the ~/.nvm/current symlink is what the hooks use); monthly and whenever the response model changes run probe.cjs, compare with the baseline, and keep T2 in shadow until re-labelled; quarterly re-run backtest/volume.cjs and the tests, and check the upstream skill with gh api 'repos/typesafe-ai/skills/commits?path=skills/typesafe-ai/SKILL.md' (re-vendor only by reading the new file and re-running skill/build-skill.py, which refuses on an unreviewed hash). Edits to hooks are made in the git repo and re-installed by you; the installed dir is protected from Claude on purpose.

ROLLBACK (any time): touch ~/.config/jev/OFF (instant, every hook and the MCP tool go silent) | restore settings.json from ~/.claude/settings.json.bak-jev-<timestamp> | rm -rf ~/.claude/hooks/jev ~/.config/jev ~/.claude/skills/typesafe-ai | claude mcp remove jev --scope user | remove the Jev bullets from ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md | restore no-secret-leak.cjs from its .bak-jev (keeping the OPENROUTER_API_KEY line is harmless) | revoke the OpenRouter key.
testPlan: OFFLINE SUITES: cd <repo> && HOME=/nonexistent-home/x node --test test/classify.test.cjs test/e2e.test.cjs -> 190 pass (144 rule-table cases incl. the real-corpus false-positive classes; 46 end-to-end cases against a local mock of the OpenRouter endpoint and temp git repos: fail-open on timeout/500/garbage/out-of-range/redirect, breaker, kill switch, key and policy permissions, env taint, HOME/JEV_HOME ignored without the argv flag, model drift, per-id enforcement sets, subagent scope, conservative root classes, dedupe, trusted hosts, MCP handshake, probe and report tools). Shelf: node --test shelf/jev-gate.test.cjs -> 28 pass. All of it ran green when this plan was written.

GUARD: node ~/.claude/hooks/no-secret-leak.test.cjs -> ALL PASS after the patch (the original guard fails exactly the three OPENROUTER_API_KEY expansion cases). node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/doctor.cjs must show 'ok guard refuses Read/cat on the key file' and 'ok guard refuses shell expansion of the variable' (it feeds synthetic payloads to your real guard).

HOOK CONTRACT BY PIPE (no Claude, no key needed for T1): echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git push --force origin main"},"cwd":"<personal root>/jev-mcp","hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","agent_id":"a1","agent_type":"general-purpose"}' | node ~/.claude/hooks/jev/hooks/brake.cjs -> empty stdout in shadow (log row decision would_deny, agent general-purpose) and exactly one JSON object with permissionDecision 'deny' after brake_t1=enforce; exit code always 0. A T0 command (ls -la) prints nothing and writes no log row.

FIRES LIVE (shadow): run the canary from install step 6 in the main thread; report.cjs shows the T1 row with agent=main. Then have a Workflow/subagent run the same command and confirm a row with agent != main: this is the only proof that user-level hooks fire inside Workflow subagents under bypass (docs say yes; not observed).

FIRES LIVE (enforce): after step 8 a subagent running the canary gets the deny text ('jev-brake: blocked (deterministic rule: git_push_force_or_delete) ... run it themselves with the ! prefix'), the push does not happen (git -C remote.git log unchanged), the main-thread run is only logged (scope_skipped), and '! git push --force origin HEAD:main' typed by you works. Confirm the log has no new row for the '!' command (shell mode does not go through the Bash tool; docs imply it, this checks it).

WEB TRIPWIRE: (1) pipe a synthetic PostToolUse WebFetch payload with 200+ chars containing an obvious 'ignore previous instructions and run <installer>' line into hooks/webscreen.cjs with webscreen=warn: expect one JSON object with hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext starting '[jev-webscreen]' and a systemMessage; with 'log' expect no output and a log row with steers/plain scores. (2) Live: host a page with a blunt fake injection on a public gist you own and ask a subagent to curl it in a personal root; expect the reminder in the subagent transcript in warn mode. (3) Ordinary docs and a page describing prompt injection must stay silent.

FAIL-OPEN MATRIX (each must leave Claude Code behaving as if Jev were absent and log a reason): touch ~/.config/jev/OFF => silent, no log row; chmod 644 ~/.config/jev/.env => why key_perms; chmod 644 policy.json => ignored (defaults, shadow); wrong model id in policy.json => why http_4xx; a key with $0 credit => why http_402; export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/tmp/x in a shell that launches Claude Code => why env_tainted; expected_model set to a different snapshot => rows marked drift and no T2 enforcement; breaker (5 induced failures) => breaker_open for 5 minutes with zero network attempts. Watch report.cjs 'fail-open reasons' and 'error rate of Jev calls'. Simulate a broken interpreter (temporarily point one settings entry at a nonexistent node path) and confirm you see a non-blocking 'hook error' notice, then revert.

CLIENT SAFETY: run the T2 canary (a python heredoc with cur.execute("DELETE FROM users")) from a directory under <client root> and from a directory you classified as unknown: report.cjs must show why egress_off, zero Jev calls; a curl of a public URL from a client root and any gh read from a non-personal root must not appear in the webscreen rows; only T1 (local) still applies. Check the state logs contain no secrets: grep -c 'sk-or-' ~/.local/state/jev/*.jsonl -> 0 for every file.

LATENCY: time 20 runs of hooks/brake.cjs with a T0 payload -> p50 about 16-17 ms, p95 about 19 ms on this machine (bare node 10.6/12.4 ms); confirm no visible slowdown of Bash calls when gitnexus runs beside it; report.cjs prints Jev p50/p95 for T2 and web calls (gate: p95 under 1.5 s).

SHADOW-MODE THRESHOLD PROCEDURE: never trust a threshold before labelling. Day 3-4 T1: label all rows; enforce a core id only if no legitimate work would have been blocked. Day 4-7 web: flagged share <=1% and genuine agent-directed text among the first ~20 flagged rows. Day 14 T2: label up to 60 would_deny rows split main/subagent; precision = true_vetoes / (true_vetoes + false_vetoes); per rule id require >=20 labelled rows, precision >=90%, zero rows for actions you had requested, >=1 veto T1 missed; base-rate check: with ~430 judgeable gray commands per 21 days (2,022 if Dev/websites are personal) and a handful of real dangers, a false-deny rate above ~1% makes precision worse than 50%, so a first-look 'no true positives' means delete the stage. Re-label a fresh sample after any model change or when probe.cjs reports changed verdicts. Global gates before any enforcement: Jev error rate <5%, p95 <1.5 s, one constant response model, zero drift rows.

PROBE / DRIFT: probe.cjs after doctor --live, then monthly and on any response-model change; --save-baseline only after you have judged the table. The first table is also the only calibration check on real Jev outputs for the questions the hooks ask; if injected texts are not flagged (fewer than 5 of 6) or benign commands are flagged, lower expectations or delete that stage.

SKILL ACTIVATION: in a scratch repo start a fresh session and ask five differently worded feature requests that need a bounded decision WITHOUT mentioning Jev (e.g. 'add a router that sorts incoming support emails into 5 teams', 'add a moderation step for user comments'). Pass = the Skill tool loads typesafe-ai and Claude states a fit check in at least 3 of 5; if not, tighten the CLAUDE.md bullet, then the skill description, then free listing budget with skillOverrides. Also verify Claude refuses to put the key in a Bash command and asks before adding a Jev call to a client repo.
TRIAGE TRIAL: from a personal repo ask for a screen of ~50 items against one criterion and confirm buckets, spot-check and cost trailer; from a client root confirm 'refused'; count calls at day 21.

REGRESSION: after every Claude Code update (now 2.1.285) and Node upgrade re-run doctor, the pipe tests and the canaries; audit client repos for hook-disabling settings: find <disk> <disk> -maxdepth 5 -path '*/.claude/settings*.json' 2>/dev/null | xargs -r grep -l -e disableAllHooks -e '"hooks"' .
openQuestionsForUser: Which of <dev root>/* and <websites root>/* are personal and which are client work? Today only <personal root> and <personal root 2> are proposed as personal (13% of Bash calls); 72.5% of your activity is in roots that stay 'unknown' (no command egress, no shadow data) until you decide. Classifying Dev/* and websites/* as personal raises the judgeable T2 volume from ~20/day to ~96/day.

Client contracts: may command text from personal roots, public web-page text (screened for personal AND unknown roots by default) and item snippets go to OpenRouter then TypeSafe, even with zdr:true + data_collection:deny and logging off? Should client roots ever get the name-free 'skeleton' mode later, or stay fully off?

Do you actually use auto or default mode anywhere? Settings say defaultMode auto, but 22 days of transcripts show 2,762 bypassPermissions, 17 plan and 0 auto/default records. If you plan auto/default or unattended `claude -p` jobs without bypass, the shelved PermissionRequest gate becomes relevant.

How often do you build features with bounded decisions (classification, routing, moderation, gating, scoring) for yourself or clients? If rarely, the skill + T1 brake is the whole value and everything Jev-side beyond it is optional.

Is a hard deny with no agent override acceptable for unattended subagents (force pushes, history rewrites, rm -rf .git, git clean -x, gh repo admin, config tampering), with '!' as your override? Are any of those routine for you (e.g. force-pushing your own feature branches or re-initialising scratch repos with rm -rf .git)? Should the main thread stay shadow (default) or be enforced too?

Do you want Edit/Write on ~/.claude/settings.json denied as well (it is the root of trust for every hook including no-secret-leak, but it would block the update-config skill and any 'edit my settings' request until you lift the rule)?
Should gh reads of private repos in personal roots be screened (their text is sent to Jev)? If not, drop the gh `if` handlers from install/settings-snippet.json.

OpenRouter account: are you fine with a dedicated key limited to $5, do you have guardrails/workspaces on your plan, and is prompt/response logging off in openrouter.ai/settings/privacy? Do you use the same account for apps you build (then use a separate capped key per app)?

Is NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or a proxy set globally in the shell that starts Claude Code? The taint guard would silence every Jev call; doctor shows it, and policy.env_allow can whitelist a name you have inspected.
Do any client repos carry project-level .claude/settings*.json with hooks, env blocks or disableAllHooks? They can override or bypass user-level hooks; the audit command is in the test plan.

Who maintains this after week 4? Budget is ~15 minutes per quarter plus re-labelling after a model change; if that is too much, keep only the guard patch, deny rules, skill and the T1 brake (no key, no egress) and delete the rest.

issues.issue: False premise behind the brake. jev-brake's role says it is 'the only mechanism that binds in your bypassPermissions sessions' (the max-design score repeats it). Claude Code 2.1.285 docs say otherwise: permissions.deny rules 'block in every mode, including bypassPermissions' (permission-modes.md L30; L416: deny rules block push commands as written in every mode), and a native rm/rmdir critical-path check still fires in bypass since v2.1.281 (root, top-level dirs, home, cwd and parents, "$DIR"/*, "$1"/*, $(pwd), var+/mnt): prompt with a 2-minute countdown, then deny, immediate deny after 3 unanswered (L649-735). The plan never compares its ~40-rule lexer with permissions.deny for its top patterns, never subtracts native catches from the replay (rm_root_or_home overlaps; part of the 23% rm_unresolved_target T2 class is natively flagged), and does not note that an unattended subagent stalls 2 minutes on the native prompt before being denied.
issues.fix: Correct the claim. Make tier 1 about 10 permissions.deny patterns (git push --force/-f, gh repo delete/archive/transfer, git clean -fdx, git filter-branch, git reflog expire, terraform destroy, crontab -r, dd of=/dev/*, mkfs*): zero code, zero spawn, main thread and subagents. Keep the lexer only for what deny rules cannot express (git -C, bash -c, agent_id scoping, owned-repo exemptions) and re-run the replay net of native catches.

issues.issue: T1 'core' set has reproducible false positives and negatives, and on your own 21-day replay most subagent core hits look like harmless scratch work, so the plan's own graduation gate ('no would_deny on a core id that was legitimate work') would fail. Probing the shipped classify()/brake: FPs denied in subagents = kill -1 <pid> (SIGHUP; end-to-end deny confirmed), pkill -1 nginx, fdisk -l, parted -l, zfs list, zpool status, gh repo edit --description/--enable-issues/--add-topic, kubectl delete pod web-node-1 (word-boundary match on node/cluster/ns/pv), cp ~/.claude/settings.json /tmp/x (read-only copy flagged as tamper), rm -rf node_modules/.git; unconditional git clean -fdx / rm -rf .git ignore the created/owned-repo check that only conditional rules get. FNs (not enforced): mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdb1 is T0 (only bare 'mkfs' matches); rm -rf /*, rm -rf ~/*, rm -rf $HOME/*, chmod -R 777 / are T1 but outside T1_CORE (shadow); find $HOME -type f -delete is only T2 because any filter flag counts as 'filtered'. Replay of the same 21 days: 9 unconditional core hits in subagent transcripts = 2x cp from ~/.claude into a temp dir, 1x force-push to a scratch bare repo, 2x git clean -fdxq after checkout --detach/reset --hard in a harness worktree, 3x the same rm -rf ... .git in a tmp path, 1x find -exec rm -rf under home; main thread 14 = 8 force pushes, 3 history rewrites, 3 'gh repo admin' of which at least two are benign gh repo edit metadata changes. No per-root or per-rule exemption exists except the human '!' (no human in unattended runs) or disabling the rule id globally, so enforcement would hard-fail Workflow runs.
issues.fix: Fix the rules (tamper = writes only; gh repo delete/archive/transfer only; exact kubectl resource kinds; kill only 'kill -9 -1'-style; skip listing flags for fdisk/parted/zfs; mkfs.*; glob forms of rm into core; find unfiltered = no name/type/time predicate at all). Apply the owned/created/scratchpad exemption to unconditional rules and add a policy t1_exempt_roots. Add tests from these cases, re-run the replay and enforce only ids with zero false hits.

issues.issue: Web tripwire contradicts the 'unknown = no egress, client data never sent' narrative. web_root_classes defaults to ['personal','unknown'], so from day 1 (the async log phase already sends) up to 12k chars of every WebFetch/WebSearch/curl/wget result from unclassified roots leave for OpenRouter then TypeSafe; 72.5% of your activity is unclassified (websites/*, Dev/*). Replay with the shipped regexes: 3,887 https curl/wget commands in 21 days (personal 659, client 569, unknown 2,659); 2,376 outputs would be sent (unknown 1,782, about 85/day). AUTHED (webscreen.cjs L24) misses header/cookie/netrc auth (literal X-Api-Key header, -b cookiejar, --netrc, --oauth2-bearer; 13 cases in the window), PRIVATE_HOST (L20) lacks dotless intranet names (tools-reference.md L547 says bare intranet names are reached with curl), 169.254/16, 100.64/10 (Tailscale), *.localhost, *.home.arpa. There is no local pre-filter, and about two thirds of screens are WebFetch/WebSearch, the channel the plan itself says returns only a small model's summary, while raw channels stay unscreened (Playwright MCP snapshot/evaluate/console output, about 1.4k calls in 22 days).
issues.fix: Default web_root_classes to ['personal'] until roots are classified; widen AUTHED/PRIVATE_HOST; add a local deterministic pre-filter (text addressed to AI agents, hidden or zero-width text, HTML comments) and send only hits plus a small random sample; drop or sample WebFetch/WebSearch; add mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot|evaluate|console_messages if raw pages matter.

issues.issue: 'Key file named .env, which I verified your guard really protects' is true only for commands that spell .env. Feeding the user's real guard (original and patched) synthetic payloads, all ALLOWED: grep -rn sk-or ~/.config/jev/ ; cd ~/.config/jev && grep -r . . ; cat ~/.config/jev/.[a-z]* ; head -c 300 ~/.config/jev/.e* ; find ~/.config/jev -type f -exec cat {} + ; tar cf - ~/.config/jev | base64 ; python3 -c open('.../.en'+'v') ; and the Grep tool with path=~/.config/jev (with or without glob). permissions.md L334: Read/Edit deny rules do not cover a command that reads files without naming them (grep -r . run inside the directory) or arbitrary subprocesses, and Grep/Glob coverage is best-effort. Debugging 'why is Jev failing' makes such accidental commands plausible; the key would then reach the transcript and API (bounded by the $5 cap and revocable, but it contradicts the stated protection).
issues.fix: Extend guard-patch.diff: add a directory pattern for .config/jev (any command or Grep/Read path naming the dir together with a reader => deny) to SECRET_FILE_ALT and checkPath, plus a test per form above. Consider sandbox.filesystem.denyRead for ~/.config/jev (sandboxing.md L207-213; sandbox is currently disabled in settings.json) or a keyring/helper-based key.

issues.issue: Trust boundary is asymmetric. Deny rules protect only ~/.claude/hooks/jev/** and ~/.config/jev/**, but the guard (~/.claude/hooks/no-secret-leak.cjs) and ~/.claude/settings.json (which registers guard, gitnexus, brake and tripwire and can set disableAllHooks) stay writable by the Edit/Write tools; the guard matcher and the T1 tamper rule (Bash only, subagents only) never see those tools, and bypass allows writes to the protected .claude directory (permission-modes.md L603-630). The kill switch ~/.config/jev/OFF can be created with touch (not in the tamper verb list) and ~/.local/state/jev (breaker.json, spend-*.json, created/<session>.json which grants rm exemptions) is unprotected. One Edit call by a confused or injected subagent disables the stack, so 'raises the bar' is overstated. Open question 6 leaves this to the user, but the default should be safe.
issues.fix: Add Edit(~/.claude/settings.json), Edit(~/.claude/settings.local.json), Edit(~/.claude/hooks/**) and Edit(~/.local/state/jev/**) to permissions.deny (user edits outside Claude or lifts temporarily); add touch/mkdir to tamper verbs; otherwise state plainly that these controls are advisory against an agent.

issues.issue: Coverage gap: the Monitor tool runs shell commands under Bash permission rules (tools-reference.md L39, L341) but hook matchers are tool-name based, so matcher 'Bash' (brake, curl/wget tripwire) and the user's guard matcher 'Bash|Read|Grep|NotebookEdit' never see Monitor commands. Replay: about 300 Monitor commands in 21 days (agents are steered to Monitor for waits); 9 of them contain rm/find -delete/git reset --hard patterns. Destructive commands and .env reads can bypass every hook by switching tool.
issues.fix: Use matcher 'Bash|Monitor' for the brake (tool_input.command is the same field) and add Monitor to the guard matcher; an 'if' rule matches one tool only (hooks-guide.md L123), so add Monitor-specific handlers where 'if' is used.

issues.issue: Wrong hook fact: webscreen must switch to synchronous in 'warn' because 'only a synchronous hook can add context'. hooks.md L3697-3703: async command hooks deliver additionalContext and systemMessage to Claude on the next conversation turn; asyncRewake also wakes Claude on exit 2 and does enforce timeout. The sync choice adds 0.35-0.9 s (up to the 8 s hook timeout) to every screened read of every parallel subagent and requires a settings-mutating --web-sync switch.
issues.fix: Keep the handlers async (or asyncRewake) and measure delivery timing in a canary; justify sync only by 'warning arrives with the tool result instead of one turn later', not by capability.

issues.issue: Faulty reasoning in multiMcpAnswer point 5: 'mcp_tool hooks ... output is parsed as stdout, so an MCP cannot express a PreToolUse/PermissionRequest decision'. hooks.md L572-574: the tool's text is read like command-hook stdout with the exit-0 parsing rule, so a tool that returns hookSpecificOutput JSON does express a decision; on PreToolUse Claude Code also waits for a connecting server within the hook timeout (L576-578). A warm MCP process could keep a TLS connection and shared breaker/budget state, avoiding a node cold start and TLS handshake per hook call.
issues.fix: Drop the claim and evaluate one server serving both jev_triage and mcp_tool hooks (SessionStart-at-launch mcp_tool hooks are skipped, keep command hooks there).

issues.issue: Deny-rule details are wrong. (a) Write(~/.config/jev/**) and Write(~/.claude/hooks/jev/**) in settings-snippet.json are accepted but never consulted and warn at every startup (permissions.md L331); Edit and Read denies already cover the Write tool; doctor.cjs even warns when they are missing. (b) 'your existing Read(**/.env) deny rules' do not cover ~/.config/jev/.env: Read(**/.env) matches only .env 'at or under the current directory' (permissions.md L379); protection comes solely from the added Read(~/.config/jev/**) and the guard.
issues.fix: Remove the Write() lines and the doctor check; correct whyThis to say the added Read(~/.config/jev/**) rule plus the guard are the protection.

issues.issue: Privacy invariant 'nothing from client roots' is not enforced for commands that merely mention client paths, and redaction has gaps. The T2 root class comes from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and hook cwd only, so in a personal-root session 'cd <client root>/<client>/... && psql -c DELETE ...' is sent verbatim in full mode (tested with jevlib redact+abbreviate). Redaction lets through mysql -pSecret, curl -u user:pass, X-Api-Key headers with <40 chars, JSON "password": "..."; the same redact() feeds web text, triage items and local logs. <personal root> is classed personal wholesale although it contains devprotocol, stripe, www and similar; open question 1 only asks about Dev/* and websites/*.
issues.fix: Before choosing the egress mode, scan the command for absolute paths under roots.client (and unknown) and downgrade to skeleton/off; extend RED (-p<pw>, -u user:pass, X-*-Key/Token headers, JSON secret fields, short hex keys); list client sub-paths of <personal root> under roots.client (client wins).

issues.issue: Ownership-tracking bug and labelling aids. extractCreated() mis-parses git clone with option values: 'git clone --depth 1 URL dst' and 'git clone -b br URL dst' record <cwd>/https:/... instead of dst (only --depth=1 works), so agent-created clones are not exempt (the depth-N clone is the most common form). Conditional T1 rules resolve git facts from the hook cwd, not the directory after 'cd x && git reset --hard'. Skeletons print branch names like feature/x as <in-project>, so 'label every T1 row' cannot tell main from a feature branch.
issues.fix: Parse clone options that take values (--depth, -b/--branch, --origin, -c, --reference), use ctx.vcwd for gitFacts, keep the branch token class in the skeleton; add tests.

issues.issue: Unstated assumptions behind t1_scope='subagents' and 'hooks fire'. It keys on agent_id (documented for subagents, hooks.md L745), but settings.json sets CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 and teammates in separate processes or --agent sessions carry no agent_id, so they count as main thread (shadow only). In interactive sessions hooks from every settings file, including ~/.claude/settings.json, are held back until the folder's trust dialog is accepted (hooks.md L3773-3778), so a fresh client checkout has neither guard nor brake until then.
issues.fix: Add canaries for a teammate and a claude --agent session, log agent_type as well, and add the trust-dialog caveat to the install notes.

issues.issue: API mismatches in the skill addendum. SystemOneRequest in @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0 exposes only state, questions and model, so the 'preferred' SDK route cannot set the provider preferences (zdr, data_collection) that the hooks force (extras are spread into the body at runtime but not typed); generated apps are ZDR only if the OpenRouter account enforces it. Model ids are inconsistent (SDK example jev-1.13, raw HTTP typesafe/jev-1.13; both accepted per OpenRouter docs). The vendored upstream body still says 'Read the live docs as part of the task' while the addendum says fetch only when writing Jev code, and in warn mode the tripwire will flag docs.typesafe.ai (its coding-agents page addresses agents) every time the skill sends Claude there.
issues.fix: Tell the addendum to pass provider via a typed cast or use raw fetch when ZDR matters (or enforce ZDR on the account); use one model-id form; pre-seed web_trusted_hosts with docs.typesafe.ai and openrouter.ai.

issues.issue: Wrongly front-loaded components. The install ships the parts the plan itself expects to delete (T2 adjudication, probe set, budget/breaker/drift machinery, MCP triage, web tripwire) although T2 has about 429 judgeable commands per 21 days against a handful of real dangers, triage has 0/150 unprompted-adoption evidence, and 24 probe cases are far below the 300 labelled cases the skill itself demands. About 1.3k lines of regex security code, 13 steps and roughly 90 minutes for a value the plan calls 'small'.
issues.fix: Stage it: A now = guard patch with directory pattern, fixed deny rules (incl. native deny patterns), skill and pointer; B = T1 in shadow with the fixes above (no key); C = personal-only tripwire with pre-filter; T2 and triage only if B/C logs show unmet need.

issues.issue: Silent-death risk. Everything fails open and the only mitigation is 'read report.cjs weekly', so a revoked or exhausted key (http_401/402), a retired model id or ZDR-list change (404), a stuck breaker or a NODE_OPTIONS taint leaves a dead stack that looks healthy; nothing alerts.
issues.fix: Add a SessionStart command hook that prints one line when there was no successful Jev call for N days, the breaker is open or the fail-open rate is high; make doctor check the ZDR listing for the pinned model.

issues.issue: Incorrect rejection rationale: 'bare npx/node under your PATH override' and 'absolute paths needed'. settings.json env PATH is ~/.nvm/current/bin:~/miniconda3/bin:~/miniconda3/condabin:~/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, so node, npx and python3 resolve (the existing gitnexus PostToolUse hook already uses bare node); real gaps are ~/.cargo/bin, ~/.bun/bin, ~/go/bin, ~/.deno/bin.
issues.fix: Keep absolute paths as hygiene but remove PATH from the rejection reasons; supply chain, egress and key handling remain valid.

issues.issue: Small factual slips. '14 main-thread (9 force pushes, 3 history rewrites, 3 gh repo admin)' sums to 15 (replay: 8+3+3 in main; the 9th force push is a subagent scratch repo) and two of the three 'gh repo admin' are benign gh repo edit calls; '~7 commands = insurance' hides that most are scratch operations; tool-call risk 55/60 was 'same as Sonnet 5', not Opus; the 8.0 self-score is unverifiable without a live run; the 46 e2e tests and the MCP handshake against the real Claude Code client were not re-run here (classify 144/144 pass).
issues.fix: Correct numbers and wording, present 8.0 as opinion, add a real-client MCP handshake canary.

issues.issue: Volumes are means over a bursty window. Two days (09-29, 09-30) hold 30% of Bash calls (50,360 of 167,470), 49% of T2 hits (1,424 of 2,882) and 87 of 133 unconditional T1 hits; T2/day median 65, p90 472, max 952, mean 144. 09-29 comes from other heavy multi-agent projects, 09-30 partly from this research run (6.6k of 16.7k Bash calls; ~91 tamper_code hits come from agents editing hooks). '~1 core hit/day', '~20 T2/day personal', '$0.08/day' and the 'three days incl. a heavy day' gate are therefore unstable.
issues.fix: Plan budgets, timeouts and gates on p90/max days and exclude research-run days from base rates.

issues.issue: Operational and latency notes. /tmp tmpfs is now 100% full (301 MB free; 25 GB under <scratch dir>, 8.8 GB in this session's scratchpad); Claude Code's per-command output files and the e2e temp repos live there, and the plan says copy but not clean. Measured on this machine: brake T0 p50 24.5 ms vs 18.5 ms for bare node (+6 ms; guard 21.7) and classify() < 20 ms on all 167k commands, so ordering with gitnexus/guard is fine and the quoted 16.6 ms is a faster moment; but referenced-script reads hit cold disk (1.6 s max seen) and spawnSync git calls (1.2-1.5 s each, about 6.6 s worst case) block the event loop, so the 5.2 s watchdog cannot fire before the 6 s hook timeout.
issues.fix: Clean <scratch dir> scratchpads (or set TMPDIR elsewhere) before install and tests; put one shared deadline over all git calls and readSmall and skip conditional resolution when exceeded.

issues.issue: Client-data analysis stops at 'ask the client'. Commands, page text and prompts sent to OpenRouter and TypeSafe are transfers of potentially personal data to US subprocessors, relevant for EU client work (DPA/subprocessor disclosure); OpenRouter still records request metadata; ZDR status is per endpoint snapshot, so a new dated snapshot without ZDR would 404 under zdr:true and fail open silently.
issues.fix: Add a short compliance note, keep client roots at egress off, and have doctor verify ZDR status of the pinned model.

critique.overall: Directionally sound and honest about limits: everything fails open, T1 needs no key or egress, rollout is shadow-first, the key stays out of env/argv, and the OpenRouter route matches the OpenAPI.
